## Out of scope
- The LAN executor, workers, the authenticated LAN listener and machine tokens: the next slice.
- The GitHub Actions executor (#310).
- Agent stages.

findings.title: Redacting the whole run state on every save changes what a resumed run executes and compares
findings.detail: `save()` now persists `redactGateData(this.state)` while the live state stays as it was, so a resumed run reads altered inputs. `gatesConfig`, `baselineScripts`, spec, holdout, feedback and answers all go through credential replacement and VT-control stripping. Reproduced with a temporary engine test: a gate command containing a registered synthetic credential, and separately one containing a literal ESC[31m, each went from "uninterrupted: succeeded" to "restarted: needs_human", with a blocking `regressed` gate and altered-command output. An unchanged script became a blocking `gate-script-changed` finding, and sanitized holdout steps changed a gate substitution from `blocked` to `met`. The persisted baseline cache entry also stops satisfying `cacheableBaseline`'s exact-command comparison. That is the earlier "redacted data is executed" finding in a new place, since the handle now correctly carries only an identity. None of the seven fixes needed it, and it adds an extra stringify and parse to every save: a 12.7 MB synthetic state went from 8.86 ms to 17.78 ms per save. Fix: revert the whole-state redaction. Redact gate results and output where they are stored or shown (artifacts, events, `lastGates`, the baseline artifact), as main already does, and leave the configuration the engine executes or compares literally untouched. Test: the credential and escape-character commands give the same verdict uninterrupted and after a restart at `gate-started`.

findings.title: Local gate work can keep running after its execution is forgotten
findings.detail: Two paths drop an execution without stopping it. (1) `executeGate` awaits `Promise.all([execution.result, events])`. If a hook called while forwarding events throws (a land-log write, say), the promise rejects, the `finally` neither cancels nor awaits the execution, and `runGateExecution` (gate-execution.ts:62) then clears the handle. Reproduced: a hook threw `log write failed` after the first check, a replacement execution completed, and the original check (`sleep 900`) kept running. (2) gate-execution.ts:29 discards a stored handle for another purpose or SHA with only a save. When that execution is still live in this process, it keeps running too. Normal shutdown cancellation does work, but discarding isn't cancelling. Fix: before forgetting an execution, whether by error, discard or settle, cancel it and await its end. Make a hook failure cancel the execution and surface as the stage's error, so it can't leave a result behind. Test: a throwing hook, and a discarded live handle, each leave no running child (check by the pid the test started) and no occupied gate slot.

findings.title: Keep the change near its budget
findings.detail: The PR is now 449 changed source lines (+311 net) against an issue budget of about 200 for a behaviour-preserving seam. Reverting the whole-state redaction should bring it down. Avoid further reshaping beyond these two fixes.

## Tests (no network, fake gh)
- The change view returns files, a capped diff and the head SHA.

findings.title: When the catalogue key can't be computed, the final freshness check is skipped and newly private text can be returned
findings.detail: On a key failure `key` is null. The catalogue is rebuilt, but the end-of-assembly check that compares the catalogue with current inputs is skipped. Reproduced with a temporary MCP test: the key computation was forced to fail, a verifier diagnostic containing a new private literal (`fallbackRaceSecret`) was appended while Git inspection was in progress, and the response came back `available: true` with that literal unchanged in the report. Fix: when freshness can't be established after the awaits, either rebuild the catalogue and reapply redaction to everything assembled, or refuse with `available: false` ("privacy inputs changed; restart"). Never return content checked against a catalogue that may be stale. Test: the sequence above withholds the literal or refuses.

findings.title: A whitespace pattern built from holdout text scans quadratically
findings.detail: A multiline detail containing a quoted tab followed by a character (for example `"\tZ"`) yields a pattern with `\s+Z`. Against a long whitespace run ending in a different character, the scan is quadratic: 32K, 64K and 128K characters took 497, 1,670 and 6,293 ms, with 469, 1,633 and 6,251 ms of CPU. That runs before paging, so the page bound doesn't limit it, and both the diff and the holdout text come from untrusted sources. Escaping of metacharacters is fine; this is quadratic scanning, not exponential backtracking. Fix: canonicalize whitespace once (collapse runs to a single space in a normalized copy with a line map) and match details literally against that copy, instead of putting `\s+` in patterns. Test: a 128K whitespace line against such a detail completes in a few milliseconds and the detail is still withheld where it actually occurs.

findings.title: Generic tokens from multiline details still withhold unrelated lines
findings.detail: The prefix-stripped matching works: unrelated `}` and `return true;` lines stay readable, and interleaved `-`, `+` and context lines map correctly. Altered lines fell from 30.7% to 3.7% of the earlier replayed diff (22 of 589), and this round's own diff is 4.7% (26 of 558). But tokens such as `1` and `toBe` are still extracted from a multiline assertion detail, so unrelated `const counter = 1;` and `expect(counter).toBe(2);` are withheld. Fix: apply the same distinctiveness rule to tokens taken from multiline details as to single-line details, and don't extract bare numbers or common identifiers as standalone patterns. The whole phrase, matched across lines, still protects the detail. Test: those two lines stay readable while the multiline holdout phrase is withheld.

findings.title: The catalogue cache has no size bound
findings.detail: The cache helps: with the same fixture (5,000 diagnostics, 10.37 MB), warm reads went from 1,185–1,207 ms to 780–784 ms, and synchronous work before the first await from 378–388 ms to 1 ms. Diagnostic, round, state and privacy-input changes invalidate it correctly. But retention is one catalogue per Store with no cap on bytes or pattern count. Bound it (for example skip caching above a size or pattern limit, and rebuild instead), so one very large run can't pin a large catalogue in the daemon.

head: 069d40c1a77ea4c1353933223f3123d4fc5f1ced
prompt:
Fixes #484.

## What's wrong
The daemon's HTTP API treats loopback as the owner. Review verdicts, land requests, run creation and cancellation, `/mcp` and `/api/admin/*` need no credential beyond coming from `127.0.0.1`.

The agent sandboxes that edit code allow loopback network. Measured 2026-10-10 on unconfined macOS with main's profiles, as a single read-only `GET /api/health`:

| Sandbox | `curl http://127.0.0.1:<daemon port>/api/health` |
|---|---|
| Codex editor profile (`codex sandbox` + `editorProfile`) | 200 |
| Outer Seatbelt profile for Claude editors (`seatbeltBackend.wrap`) | 200 |
| Claude reader sandbox | loopback denied (per #483's probe) |

So an implementer, which runs model-written commands, can reach the control plane. It could:
- `POST /api/runs/<own run>/review` with `approve` at its PR head;
- then `POST /api/land`;
- or create, cancel or answer runs, or call `/mcp` tools.

That bypasses the orchestrator's review entirely. Land checks and CI still run, but review is the gate this factory relies on. AGENTS.md's trust boundaries assume model-controlled processes can't steer the factory. That assumption doesn't hold today.

## Change
1. **Authenticate the local API.**
   - The daemon creates a random API token at startup, mode 0600, in a path every agent sandbox read-denies. That means the Seatbelt `denyRead`, Codex filesystem `none` and the Claude reader `denyRead`, the same way `privateReadPaths` already protects the database.
   - Every mutating route, every `/api/admin/*` route and `/mcp` require it as a bearer header. That includes review, land, runs, answers, cancel, feed ack, the gate-slot lease and providers or routing changes.
   - The CLI, the MCP stdio proxy, the gate-slot client and `scripts/land-pr.sh` read the token and send it.
   - Read-only `GET /api/health` may stay open.
   - The UI's existing sign-in (passkey or password session) also counts on loopback.
2. **Agent-side wrappers use their own narrow capability.** #483's per-invocation capability is enough for the gate-slot lease endpoint. It never grants any other route.
3. **Defence in depth.** In the Seatbelt editor profile, deny outbound connections to the daemon's own port, and the Codex profile's equivalent if it can express one. Agents' tests can still bind and reach other loopback ports.
4. **Rollout without breaking the running release.**
   - Step 1 ships clients that send the token when the file exists, with the daemon accepting either form.
   - Step 2 enforces, behind a config key that defaults on after a release.
   - Document this next to the key.

## Tests
- **Real probes**, in tests marked `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`, from the Codex editor profile and the outer Seatbelt profile:
  - `POST /api/runs/<id>/review` without the token gets 401;
  - reading the token file is denied;
  - the agent's own lease capability still works for the gate-slot endpoint only.
- **Unit tests:** every mutating or admin route refuses a request without the token. The CLI and MCP proxy succeed with it. An older client gets a clear error after enforcement.

## Priority
This is a trust-boundary bypass on main, found while reviewing #483 (which doesn't cause it). It needs fixing before the M6 work pilot, and before more agent-facing surface is added.


Scope for this run: steps 1 to 4 if they fit in about 400 changed source lines. Otherwise deliver steps 1, 2 and 4 (token, capability-only lease, rollout) first and leave step 3 for a follow-up.

findings.title: A failed startup leaves started work running and drops the token's protection too early
findings.detail: Two cleanup gaps in `startDaemon`. (1) If `mount(factory)` rejects after it has already started the land queue, `integrations` was never assigned, so its `stop()` can't be called. A temporary test injected a failure into real integration mounting after land startup: land started 1, land stopped 0, one notifier timer still live, token protected false. (2) On a real bind failure, `startHttp` (src/server/http.ts:722) releases the token's read protection before `startDaemon` tears down the integrations, so a confined profile built during teardown (a land check still finishing, say) lacks the denial. Fix: make mounting exception-safe, so a partial mount stops what it started (have `mount` clean up after itself on failure, or return its stop handle before the step that can fail). Release the token protection only after every started component has stopped. Test: both injected failures leave no running land queue or timers, and every profile built until teardown completes denies the token path.

findings.title: With enforcement on, a proxy-authenticated setup over plain HTTP can never authenticate
findings.detail: With enforcement on, proxied requests now need a token or session too (intended: tests and GUIDE say "all routes"). But the HTTPS check on `public_origins` still exempts `auth = "proxy"`, and the session cookie is Secure. head: 4898db92b7f1ae6814b957e5f19da8cb221c4f99
prompt:
Fixes #487.

## What's wrong
Edit-mode agents and gate commands can read the owner's credentials. The outer Seatbelt profile (`src/harness/sandbox.ts`) confines writes and signals, but its only read rule is `denyRead`, and `writeRoots` fills that with `privateReadPaths()`: the SQLite database and its sidecars. The Codex editor profile denies the same paths. Confined readers already deny home directories (`privateReadRoots`), but editors and gates don't.

`agentEnv()` strips factory secrets from the environment and drops `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, and gates set `HOME` to scratch. Both help with environment variables, but not with files read by absolute path, and `ssh` finds keys through the password database, not `$HOME`.

Measured on 2026-10-10 on unconfined macOS, with main's profiles, `agentEnv()` plus `HOME=<scratch>`, and a one-byte read (`head -c 1`, nothing printed):

| Probe | Codex editor profile | Outer Seatbelt profile (Claude editors, every gate command) |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.ssh/<private key>` (default key, work key) | readable | readable |
| `~/.config/limitless/secrets.env` | readable | readable |
| `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` (GitHub token) | readable | readable |
| `~/.codex/auth.json` | readable | readable |
| `curl https://example.com` | 200 | 200 |
| `ssh -o BatchMode=yes <LAN host> true` | denied (publickey) | **exit 0** |

Gate commands run the candidate's code: its tests and scripts, and for Dependabot PRs, the updated dependency's install scripts and code. So anything that gets code into a run can read every credential above, send it out over HTTPS, or open a shell on another machine the owner's key reaches. That includes a prompt-injected implementer, a malicious package version or a crafted PR. AGENTS.md's trust boundaries treat that code as untrusted, but the profiles don't enforce it for reads.

Related, and narrower: #335 covers one backend token file, and #484 the loopback API. This issue covers the home directory.

## Change
1. **Gate commands: deny reads under the home directory, with a small allowlist.**
   - In the outer Seatbelt profile, add `deny file-read*` on the home directory, followed by allows for:
     - the run's checkout and scratch;
     - the git paths the checkout needs (its common directory and the bare repository cache);
     - the toolchains gates use: the bun, cargo and rustup homes, and any other toolchain path the factory's own config names.

     Keep the allowlist in one place and short.
   - Other runs' checkouts, the factory's data directory (except what this run needs) and every credential store fall outside it.
   - System paths stay readable.
2. **Editors: deny the credential stores.** The Claude editor's whole CLI runs inside the outer profile and needs its own login, so a home-wide deny isn't possible there yet (#369). For both editor profiles (outer Seatbelt for Claude, Codex's filesystem profile), deny reads of:
   - `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/limitless`, `~/.config/gh`, `~/.codex` (Codex's CLI reads it outside the tool sandbox), `~/.aws`, `~/.netrc`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.docker`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.kube`, plus a configurable `[sandbox] deny_read = [...]` for anything else an installation keeps (optional, default empty).
   - Name what stays readable to Claude editors (their own CLI login) as a known gap under #369.
3. **One implementation.** The list and the home-wide rule come from one module, used by `writeRoots` (gates and Claude editors) and the Codex editor profile. Reuse the existing `denyRead` plumbing, and add nothing in parallel to it.
4. **Fail closed, precisely.** If the home directory can't be resolved, or an allowlisted path overlaps a denied credential path, refuse to start the gate or the editor with a clear reason. Don't fall back to the current profile.

## Tests
- **Real probes**, in tests titled with `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`. Use temporary stand-in files created under a temporary home, or measure the real paths with existence checks only, and never print a real file's content:
  - From the outer profile as a gate runs it, reading a file under `~/.ssh` and `~/.config/limitless` is denied, and so are another run's checkout and a file directly under the home directory. Reading the checkout, scratch, the git common directory and `bun --version` from the bun home all work.
  - From the Codex editor profile and the outer profile as a Claude editor runs it, each listed credential store is denied, and the checkout and scratch stay readable.
  - `ssh -o BatchMode=yes` to an unreachable address fails because the key can't be read, not because of the network. Assert on the read denial, not on a host.
- **Unit tests:** the profile text contains the home deny and allowlist for gates and the credential denies for editors. The overlap check refuses.
- The existing gate, sandbox, codex and claude tests pass, including the real-Seatbelt ones run unconfined.

## Budget and scope
About 150 changed source lines plus tests. Out of scope:
- network egress restrictions;
- macOS Keychain access through `security`, which is a separate gap (name it in the report);
- confining Claude editors' own login (#369);
- the loopback API (#484).

## Priority
This is a trust-boundary bypass on main, found while checking whether an SSH-based worker transport would be safe (#165). It comes before any worker work, and before the M6 work pilot.

findings.title: Under the new gate profile, this repository's own test suite fails, so every gate would fail after deploy
findings.detail: The factory's gates for this PR passed only because gates run the daemon's (main's) profile, not the PR's. Measured on 2026-10-11 by running this PR's `runGates` (the new gate profile) on a recorded worktree of this PR, with the repository cache and checkout under the real home directory as factory checkouts are (`~/.limitless/runs/...`). Setup, lint and typecheck passed, but the test check failed with 6 or more failures. (1) Four UI tests ("original prompt renders plain multiline text...", "Providers keeps controls...", "direct navigation to every UI route...", "guarded UI/assets, API, SSE...") fail with `EPERM: operation not permitted, stat '<home>/package.json'`: Bun's resolver and bundler walk up parent directories looking for package.json (and similarly bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json, node_modules), and with the home-wide read deny the walk gets EPERM instead of ENOENT and aborts. The ancestor `file-read-metadata` grants cover the ancestor directories themselves, not files inside them. (2) Four failure-injection tests ("unconfirmed holdout shutdown preserves its snapshot...", and "an unavailable pinned implementer stops with its chain and reason: disabled|quota|rejected") fail deterministically inside the gate profile (Expected "needs_human", Received "failed", 4 of 4 when run alone under the profile) and pass unconfined in the same checkout. Reproduce with this PR's code: `recordWorktree(wt)`, then `runGates(wt, { setup: [], checks: [{ name: "t", run: "bun test test/failure-injection.test.ts -t 'unavailable pinned implementer'" }] }, signal)`, with `wt` under the home directory. Fix: make what toolchains legitimately probe in ancestor directories resolve as absent or readable (for example allow read of the specific manifest names, package.json, bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json and jsconfig.json, plus metadata for `node_modules` in each ancestor of the allowed roots, never credential paths), find what the failure-injection runs hit under the profile, and add a test that runs a real `bun test` of a small fixture project under the gate profile from a checkout located under a temporary home. Then run the full suite under the new gate profile, from a checkout under the home directory, and report the result in the PR.

findings.title: The gate allowance for the Cargo home exposes Cargo's registry credentials
findings.detail: Gates are allowed to read the whole `CARGO_HOME` (default `~/.cargo`), and the credential list (line 89) doesn't include `credentials.toml` or `credentials`, which hold private registry tokens (see Cargo's documented home layout). A temporary probe confirmed that a synthetic `~/.cargo/credentials.toml` falls inside the allowance and has no specific denial. Adding it to `[sandbox] deny_read` instead makes the overlap check (line 122) refuse to launch any gate. Fix: allow only what builds need from the Cargo home (`bin`, `registry`, `git`, `config.toml` and `config`, which `runConfined` already copies into scratch), and deny `credentials.toml` and `credentials` as specific denies that win over the allowance. Do the same review for the bun and rustup homes. Test: a profile and an unconfined real-Seatbelt probe show `credentials.toml` denied while `cargo --version` and a cached registry read work.

findings.title: Editors can still read credential stores at relocated paths
findings.detail: The credential list uses default paths under the home directory only. `agentEnv()` (src/util/proc.ts:699) passes `CODEX_HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` through, and Codex and gh honour them (gh documents `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). A temporary probe set synthetic custom Codex and gh homes: `agentEnv()` kept them, and the editor deny list covered neither the custom `auth.json` nor `hosts.yml`. Fix: compute the effective location of each store from the daemon's own environment (`CODEX_HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gh`, `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR`, `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, `GNUPGHOME`, `KUBECONFIG`, `NETRC`, `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, `CARGO_HOME/credentials*`), and deny those as well as the defaults, in both spellings. Test: with those variables pointing at temporary stand-ins, the editor and gate profiles deny each one.

findings.title: Loading another config replaces the running factory's read policy
findings.detail: `configureReadPolicy` overwrites a module-global `configured` every time `loadConfig` runs, and `homeReadPolicy` (line 84) reads that global, not the `Config` of the factory that launched the work. Production callers don't set `readPolicyScope`. A temporary probe loaded config A with a custom `deny_read` entry, then config B with no `[sandbox]` table: the next policy dropped both A's entry and A's config-directory denial. Any code path that loads a config in the daemon process (eval settings, `limitless` commands run in-process, tests) can widen a running factory's sandbox. Fix: make the policy part of `Config` (an immutable value built in `loadConfig`), and pass it where profiles are built (through `EngineDeps` or the confinement scope that `executeRun`, the land queue and evals already set), rather than a module global. Test: loading a second config doesn't change the policy that the first factory's gates and editors get.

findings.title: The final re-deny of private paths inside an allowance has no effective test
findings.detail: The last rule re-denies registered private paths (the database) that sit inside an allowed path such as the checkout. Removing it left every non-skipped test passing. The real database test (test/sandbox.test.ts:217) puts the database outside the allowance, so it never exercises the overlap. Add a fixture with the registered database inside the checkout: a profile assertion that fails without the rule, plus an unconfined real-Seatbelt read probe. Note in the PR that the filesystem-denial, listing and SSH probes skip in confined gates and in Linux CI, so they are checked only unconfined.

findings.title: Two tests fail when run unconfined on macOS
findings.detail: Both fail on a developer machine, in hand landings and in reviews, though not in the factory's gates or CI. (1) test/gates.test.ts "waiting behind a lease does not spend the internal gate's execution timeout" runs a gate in the caller's checkout. In a linked worktree without a `.git-paths` sidecar, the new policy correctly throws "Missing or invalid trusted Git paths". Give the test its own fixture repository with a recorded worktree (`recordWorktree`) instead of the caller's checkout, and keep the fail-closed behaviour. (2) test/scratch.test.ts:1622 "Codex editor denies credential reads" passes a `CODEX_HOME` that doesn't exist, so codex exits before probing ("CODEX_HOME points to ... but that path does not exist"). Create the directory first. With that one change the test passes, 37 assertions, so the Codex profile itself works.

head: aac48884f5f00a69720eefd44fd5a8d4e9a92301
prompt:
Fixes #484.

## What's wrong
The daemon's HTTP API treats loopback as the owner. Review verdicts, land requests, run creation and cancellation, `/mcp` and `/api/admin/*` need no credential beyond coming from `127.0.0.1`.

The agent sandboxes that edit code allow loopback network. Measured 2026-10-10 on unconfined macOS with main's profiles, as a single read-only `GET /api/health`:

| Sandbox | `curl http://127.0.0.1:<daemon port>/api/health` |
|---|---|
| Codex editor profile (`codex sandbox` + `editorProfile`) | 200 |
| Outer Seatbelt profile for Claude editors (`seatbeltBackend.wrap`) | 200 |
| Claude reader sandbox | loopback denied (per #483's probe) |

So an implementer, which runs model-written commands, can reach the control plane. It could:
- `POST /api/runs/<own run>/review` with `approve` at its PR head;
- then `POST /api/land`;
- or create, cancel or answer runs, or call `/mcp` tools.

That bypasses the orchestrator's review entirely. Land checks and CI still run, but review is the gate this factory relies on. AGENTS.md's trust boundaries assume model-controlled processes can't steer the factory. That assumption doesn't hold today.

## Change
1. **Authenticate the local API.**
   - The daemon creates a random API token at startup, mode 0600, in a path every agent sandbox read-denies. That means the Seatbelt `denyRead`, Codex filesystem `none` and the Claude reader `denyRead`, the same way `privateReadPaths` already protects the database.
   - Every mutating route, every `/api/admin/*` route and `/mcp` require it as a bearer header. That includes review, land, runs, answers, cancel, feed ack, the gate-slot lease and providers or routing changes.
   - The CLI, the MCP stdio proxy, the gate-slot client and `scripts/land-pr.sh` read the token and send it.
   - Read-only `GET /api/health` may stay open.
   - The UI's existing sign-in (passkey or password session) also counts on loopback.
2. **Agent-side wrappers use their own narrow capability.** #483's per-invocation capability is enough for the gate-slot lease endpoint. It never grants any other route.
3. **Defence in depth.** In the Seatbelt editor profile, deny outbound connections to the daemon's own port, and the Codex profile's equivalent if it can express one. Agents' tests can still bind and reach other loopback ports.
4. **Rollout without breaking the running release.**
   - Step 1 ships clients that send the token when the file exists, with the daemon accepting either form.
   - Step 2 enforces, behind a config key that defaults on after a release.
   - Document this next to the key.

## Tests
- **Real probes**, in tests marked `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`, from the Codex editor profile and the outer Seatbelt profile:
  - `POST /api/runs/<id>/review` without the token gets 401;
  - reading the token file is denied;
  - the agent's own lease capability still works for the gate-slot endpoint only.
- **Unit tests:** every mutating or admin route refuses a request without the token. The CLI and MCP proxy succeed with it. An older client gets a clear error after enforcement.

## Priority
This is a trust-boundary bypass on main, found while reviewing #483 (which doesn't cause it). It needs fixing before the M6 work pilot, and before more agent-facing surface is added.


Scope for this run: steps 1 to 4 if they fit in about 400 changed source lines. Otherwise deliver steps 1, 2 and 4 (token, capability-only lease, rollout) first and leave step 3 for a follow-up.

findings.title: A failed second bind releases token protection before the first listener has stopped
findings.detail: Mount failures and a failed first bind now clean up correctly. Re-measured: six injected mount-step failures, profiles built during delayed teardown still deny the token path, repeated `stop()` is harmless, and real CLI SIGINT and SIGTERM shutdown passes. One path remains. When the LAN listener (the second bind) fails, the catch block calls `local.stop(true)` without awaiting it, and `startDaemon` never gets that listener's stop handle. With an injected asynchronous shutdown around a real Bun listener, startup had already returned, token protection was gone, and `/api/health` on the first listener still returned 200. Fix: await both listeners' stop calls in that catch block before releasing (or let the error carry them to `startDaemon`'s `stop`), so protection is released only after every listener has closed. Test: the injected slow-stop case, asserting the listener is closed and the token path still denied until the release.

head: 13a7b2e1742d8f0ac1d6cab08146deae65a032f9
prompt:
Fixes #482.

Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput). Matt chose this on 2026-10-10: the second machine starts by running gate suites, the largest measured share of test CPU, behind one executor interface that the GitHub Actions executor (#310) will share. This first slice is the seam alone, with behaviour unchanged. The LAN gate executor follows in its own issue.

Design reference: `docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md` §6.2, the executor interface.

## Change
1. **An `Executor` interface in `src/gates/`**, as in research §6.2:
   - `start(req, signal)` returns an `ExecutionHandle` (`kind`, `id`, `startedAt`, optional `url`). The caller persists the handle before it awaits anything.
   - `attach(handle, signal)` re-attaches to work already started, after a daemon restart as well, without starting it again. It returns an `Execution` with `events`, `result` and an idempotent `cancel()`.
   - Gate work uses `Req = { repo, baseSha, headSha, gates, checks }` and `Res = GateRun`. `gates` is the `GateConfig` read from the base commit, as today. `compareGates`, the regression retries and the baseline cache don't change.
2. **The local executor.** Today's `runGates` becomes the `local` executor with identical behaviour: the gate slot, confinement, scratch and process scope, timeouts and events. For `local`, `attach` after a restart re-runs the check, exactly as a resumed gate stage does today.
3. **One path for every gate run in the daemon.** Route these through the executor, reusing one implementation for each:
   - the prepare baseline;
   - the gates stage;
   - post-change and baseline retries;
   - the landing queue's checks.

   `limitless deploy`'s gate and `scripts/land-pr.sh` stay as they are (out of scope).
4. **Selection.** An optional config key, `[gates] executor = "local"` by default. Only `local` exists for now; another value fails config validation with a clear message.
5. **Durability.** Store the handle in the stage's run state, so the resume path knows which executor and execution it belongs to. Runs that predate the change, with no handle stored, resume on `local` as today.

## Tests (no network)
- The existing gate, baseline-cache, land-queue and pipeline gate tests pass unchanged, which shows behaviour is preserved.
- A fake executor injected into the engine:
  - its `GateRun` result decides the stage;
  - the handle is persisted before the result is awaited;
  - a restart between start and result calls `attach` and not `start`;
  - cancelling the run calls `cancel()` once.
- A run with no stored handle resumes on `local`.

## Budget
About 200 changed source lines plus tests. It is a refactor: no new behaviour beyond the seam.

## Out of scope
- The LAN executor, workers, the authenticated LAN listener and machine tokens: the next slice.
- The GitHub Actions executor (#310).
- Agent stages.

findings.title: Restore main's load-time redaction of run state that this round removed
findings.detail: Removing the whole-state redaction from `save()` was right. But this round also deleted the line main already has in the `RunContext` constructor, `this.state = redactGateData(this.state);` (origin/main src/pipeline/context.ts:307, from 004983b "redact credentials in gate output before it is stored or sent"). That line protects older stored run state, which may contain credentials in gate output or feedback, when a run is loaded. Reproduced with a temporary test: resuming legacy state that contained a registered synthetic credential, and letting the run exhaust its implementation rounds, persisted the credential in `runs.error` and in the error event (through src/pipeline/engine.ts:861, :285 and :346). The same probe passes on main. The issue asks for behaviour unchanged, so restore that constructor line exactly as on main. Don't redesign load-side redaction in this PR. Add a test that resumes state containing a registered synthetic credential and asserts it doesn't reach `runs.error` or events. Keep everything else in this round as it is: the forgotten-execution fix and the removal of save-side redaction are verified.

findings.title: Inside a gate, a missing optional toolchain path makes the read policy refuse, so this repository's own suite fails under the new profile
findings.detail:
Five of the six earlier findings are fixed: narrow Cargo, rustup and bun allowances with credentials denied, relocated stores denied, a per-config policy, the specific re-deny test, and the two fixtures. The gate-profile blocker is still open. The orchestrator ran this PR's `runGates` on a recorded worktree under the real home, inside `readPolicyScope.run(loadConfig().readPolicy, ...)`. Setup, lint and typecheck passed, and the test check failed after 1,079 s. Every visible failure carried `Cannot resolve read policy path <home>/.rustup/toolchains`:
- "an unavailable pinned implementer stops with its chain and reason: quota|rejected";
- "pinned verifier exhaustion redacts private holdout details: unavailable|rejected";
- "audit allowances > engine audit honors persisted allowances: no opt-in|inline mention";
- "audit allowances > private-string audit events and retry feedback redact filenames and values";
- "a changes verdict runs one round that pushes onto the PR branch with the findings quoted".

This PR's own real-Seatbelt regression, test/sandbox.test.ts:818 "failure-injection outcomes survive a gate checkout under home", also fails unconfined with the same error. Cause: inside a gate, the home directory is read-denied, so the strict component resolver gets EPERM from `realpathSync` (and `lstatSync`) on an absent optional path such as `~/.rustup/toolchains`, instead of ENOENT, and refuses. Tests that build factories and gates run nested inside the gate, so after a deploy every gate of this repository would fail.

Fix:
- Separate required roots (checkout, scratch, Git paths) from optional toolchain candidates (bun, cargo and rustup subpaths, `toolchain_paths`).
- In the component resolver, call `lstatSync(next, { throwIfNoEntry: false })` before `realpathSync(next)`, and don't realpath a component proven absent.
- Treat an optional candidate as absent, and omit it from the allowances, when it doesn't exist, or when its existence can't be inspected because a denied ancestor blocks it (EPERM or EACCES from lstat on a path under the denied home). An optional allowance for a path that can't be seen grants nothing anyway.
- Keep refusing for required roots that can't be resolved, for an existing entry (including a dangling symlink) that can't resolve, and for any overlap with a credential path, even for absent descendants.
- Don't use `existsSync()` or catch-all exception handling to classify absence.

Tests, since real Seatbelt doesn't run in factory gates or CI: make the resolver's `lstatSync` and `realpathSync` injectable, and add non-skipped tests.
- With lstat and realpath throwing EPERM for every path under a temporary home (as inside a confined gate) and no `.rustup`, `.cargo` or `.bun` present, the gate policy computes without throwing and omits those allowances.
- A required root under the same conditions still refuses.
- An existing dangling symlink candidate still refuses.

head: 43f588fc20464c2c7c805a4446017f64a2287f99
prompt:
CLI: send the API token only to the daemon that issued it

## What's wrong
`apiTokenHeaders()` (`src/cli/api-token.ts`) reads `~/.limitless/api-token` (or `$LIMITLESS_HOME/api-token`) and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer …` on every CLI request, to whatever daemon `LIMITLESS_URL` names. The token belongs to one daemon, the one that published it at startup (#489), but nothing checks that the URL points at that daemon.

Found on 2026-10-11, when the first deploy after #489 failed. Tests spawn the CLI with `LIMITLESS_URL` set to their own in-process daemon. They sent it the live daemon's token, the test daemon rejected the bearer it didn't issue, and 46 tests failed with 401. #495 isolates the suite, but the CLI behaviour remains:
- `LIMITLESS_URL=https://<remote origin>` (the proxied UI, a second machine, a typo, a hostile value in an inherited environment) receives the loopback token over the network.
- Any process that can set `LIMITLESS_URL` for a CLI invocation, such as a wrapper script or a CI step, can collect the token.

With `[server] require_api_token = true`, that token is the credential that authorizes loopback API calls such as approve, land and gate slots.

## Change
- Send the token only to the daemon that wrote it. For example, the daemon also records its own loopback origin (scheme, host, port) next to the token, with the same file protections. The CLI attaches the token only when the request's origin matches exactly, after the same URL normalization the daemon applies. Otherwise it sends no token, and the request fails with 401 as it would for any unauthenticated client, or uses a session if one exists.
- Keep older daemons working: if the origin record is missing, attach the token only to the default loopback origins for the configured port.

## Tests
- With a token and a recorded origin, a request to a different port, host or scheme carries no `authorization` header. A request to the recorded origin carries it.
- A missing origin record falls back to the configured loopback port only.
- The token never appears in an error message or log from these paths (`redactCredentials`).

## Budget
About 40 changed source lines plus tests.

Closes #496

findings.title: Missing-record fallback ignores the configured daemon port
findings.detail: Without an `api-token.origin` record (an older daemon), `apiTokenHeaders` authorizes only `http://127.0.0.1:${LIMITLESS_PORT ?? 7400}`. With `[server] port = 7412` in config.toml and no `LIMITLESS_PORT`, setup targets 7412 correctly but sends no authorization header, so authenticated calls to an older daemon fail. The helper would also send the token to port 7400 when that isn't the daemon's port. Measured with a temporary home and a synthetic token. Fix: resolve the effective daemon port the same way the CLI and setup do (the configured `[server] port`, overridden by `LIMITLESS_PORT`). Use one implementation, have every caller pass it, and use it for the fallback origin. Test: no record, configured port 7412, no env → the 7412 origin gets the header, 7400 doesn't.

findings.title: After a rollback, newer clients lose access until the stale origin record is removed
findings.detail: An older daemon started after a rollback rotates `api-token` but leaves the newer release's `api-token.origin` untouched. On the same listener origin with enforcement enabled, the previous release's CLI got HTTP 200 and this PR's CLI got 401, because the record's `tokenHash` no longer matches. AGENTS.md requires the previous release to keep working across a rollback, and a newer CLI talking to an older daemon is part of that. Fix: treat a record whose hash doesn't match the current token as absent, and fall back to the configured loopback origin (the previous finding). That is exactly the trust an older daemon without a record gets: the record can only narrow the recipient, never widen it. Keep rejecting a record whose origin isn't a plain http(s) origin. Test: a record with a mismatched hash and a token on the configured loopback port → the header goes to that port only.

findings.title: A malformed or unreadable config.toml now aborts every CLI and MCP request

findings.title: The client port resolver disagrees with the daemon, so the token fallback can authorize another listener
findings.detail: The daemon resolves its port with `num(Number(process.env.LIMITLESS_PORT) || server.port, 7400)` (src/config.ts:287), so `LIMITLESS_PORT=+49751`, `7413.0`, `1e3` or a hex form all select that number. `resolveClientPort` accepts only `/^\d+$/` and otherwise falls back to `[server] port`. Measured with temporary homes and a synthetic token: with `LIMITLESS_PORT=+49751` and configured port 49752, the daemon used 49751 while the CLI, the lease client and `httpBackend` all chose 49752. With a missing or stale origin record they sent the bearer token to the unrelated listener on 49752, and made zero requests to 49751. Configured port 0 also differs: the daemon binds an ephemeral port, while clients pick 7400. Fix: move the daemon's exact port rule into one small exported function that both `loadConfig` and the client resolver call. It takes the env value and the raw `[server]` table and never throws, so malformed config stays non-fatal. In `apiTokenHeaders`' fallback, send no token unless the resolved port is a definite integer 1–65535 from that same rule; for example port 0, a non-integer, or an unreadable or invalid config with no env override should withhold the token. Keep routing unchanged otherwise. Tests: `LIMITLESS_PORT=+49751` with configured 49752 → client and daemon agree on 49751, and 49752 gets no token; configured port 0 → no token fallback.

head: 768978b213da63b807ef54f6cfe440f40f762217
prompt:
Agent-test wrapper: a truncated lease reply body exits at once instead of waiting

## What's wrong
The agent-test wrapper (#483) waits out its budget and exits 75 when the gate-slot service is slow, resets the connection, or sends truncated headers. A truncated response **body** is handled differently: the command exits 1 within a few milliseconds.

`localLeaseClient` (`src/cli/gate-slot.ts`, around lines 64–65) wraps `response.json()` in a blanket `.catch()` that throws `LeaseRejected`. Bun reports a body cut off mid-read as a `TypeError` with `code: "ECONNRESET"`, so a transport failure while reading becomes a rejection, and rejections end the command at once.

Measured on 2026-10-10 against a real local server that sends valid headers and then closes mid-body, with a 5 s budget: the wrapper exited 1 after 3–4 ms, for normal acquisition and for parent reuse. The binary never started, so this fails closed, but the agent sees an error instead of a wait. Found while reviewing #483 round 3. The behaviour predates that round.

## Change
- In `localLeaseClient`, distinguish a body that failed to arrive (a read error with a transport code such as `ECONNRESET`) from a complete body that isn't valid JSON or fails the reply schema.
- For the agent-test path, the first is a transport failure. The wrapper keeps waiting within its budget, then exits 75 with the last failure named, the same as a reset during headers.
- The second stays `LeaseRejected`.
- The non-agent `limitless gate-slot` CLI and the deploy gate keep their current behaviour.

## Tests
With real local servers, as in #483's probes:
- a truncated body makes the wrapper exit 75 at its budget without starting the binary;
- malformed but complete JSON still exits at once as rejected;
- the `limitless gate-slot` CLI is unchanged in both cases.

## Budget
About 20 changed source lines plus tests.

Closes #491

findings.title: The truncated-body test asserts macOS error wording and fails on Linux CI
findings.detail: CI (ubuntu-latest) fails "local lease service truncated body waits (Unix=%s, parent=%s)": `Expected to contain: "ECONNRESET"`, received `agent-test: bun test waited 501.59ms for the gate lane; try a targeted run: bun test <file>; last failure: Error: HTTP: TypeError: Unable to connect…`. Linux reports the cut body as a connection or timeout error rather than ECONNRESET; the behaviour under test is identical. AGENTS.md: a test must pass on Linux CI as well as macOS. #483 hit the same wording difference, and its fix (6066ce8) asserts the shape of the message instead of the platform's error name. Fix: assert the behaviour, for example exit 75, the full budget waited (`waited [\d.]+ms for the gate lane`), the test binary never started, and a `last failure:` present, and drop the ECONNRESET substring. If you need to show the body-read path specifically, use an injected client that throws a body error, so the assertion doesn't depend on the OS. Keep the test failing without the source change.

head: bd6282b65bbeed36fa0647315ce7653c6df5c7c5
prompt:
Previews: run candidate build, seed and serve commands confined

## Why
The confinement from #233 / #323 covers edit-mode agents, gate commands and implement-eval hidden commands. The preview flow still runs candidate code unconfined: `src/pipeline/preview.ts` around lines 184 and 199 runs the repository's `[preview] build` and `serve` commands, and the seed command, with the user's full write access.

A candidate's preview command can therefore rewrite the run's private git admin dir, the factory's recorded `.git-paths`, the repo cache or `$HOME`. That is the same class of escape #323 closed for agents and gates. The trusted git operations now refuse a tampered admin dir, which narrows the damage, but the other targets stay writable.

## Fix
Run the preview's `build`, `seed` and `serve` through the same confinement backend as gates (`runConfined`). The writable roots are the checkout, the preview scratch and the preview's own `LIMITLESS_HOME` / `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR` scratch dirs. It fails closed like the gates.

The served process needs to bind its port, and confinement covers writes, not network, so that should be unaffected. Check that.

## Acceptance
- With the fake backend, a preview build that tries to write the admin dir, the repo cache or `$HOME` is denied, and a write inside the checkout succeeds.
- The real-Seatbelt preview test is skipped off darwin and under `LIMITLESS_CONFINED`.
- An existing UI preview of this repository still builds and serves.

Found in the #323 review; it predates #323. Related: #233, #335.

Closes #340

findings.title: Unterminated serve output can exhaust daemon memory
findings.detail: The new persistent line callbacks route serve output through runProcess's lineSplitter, whose pending buffer grows until a newline (src/util/proc.ts:324). Neither tailLimit: 4000 nor collect's slice bounds that buffer. After readiness, emitting 32 MiB without newlines increased retained daemon heap by 32,380,489 bytes; newline-terminated output plateaued. A candidate can keep emitting and exhaust the shared daemon. Bound line framing, including startup-marker parsing, and add an unterminated-output regression test. Reproduce with real Seatbelt unconfined, as the factory's verifier can't.

findings.title: Case-sensitive denial matcher fails on Bun's expected EPERM
findings.detail: The real Seatbelt test receives 'EPERM: operation not permitted' when writing cache.git/worktrees/preview/index. Its case-sensitive /Operation not permitted|Permission denied/ matcher rejects that expected denial and rethrows it, causing 'Preview build failed' before the remaining targets or loopback checks run. The fake emits the capitalized spelling and masks the defect. Check EPERM/EACCES error codes; the temporary errno-based probe passed every protected target.

With the flag, lines that differ only in case are treated as duplicates; the first occurrence is kept with its original casing and order. Without the flag, behavior stays exactly as now (case-sensitive). The flag must be parsed as an option and not included in the text being deduplicated. head: ceb2e9fc37f24c09eace037fa721abe0eb4585a8
prompt:
# MCP change view: show the implementer's diff; withhold only holdout material

## What happened
Found in the new-agent test re-run (#473, v2, 2026-10-13). The agent called `limitless_get_change` before every approval, 8 calls in total, as #477 intended. But almost nothing it received was code:
- Every file diff of sandbox #12, #13 and #14's final head came back as `"text":"[withheld: holdout text]"`.
- The run reports for #13 and #14 were withheld the same way.
- #14's first head showed its README with `[16 private details withheld]`.

So the agent approved #12 and #13 on the factory's own gates and review alone, and it said so in its report. That is the v1 finding #477 set out to fix.

## Why
`src/integrations/mcp-change.ts` (around lines 330–370) withholds a value whole when any holdout detail appears in it, however short, after normalization. For a small feature, the holdout tests share words with the code by design (`uppercase`, `truncate`, `dedupe`), so every diff matches.

## What the redaction protects
The holdout is hidden from implementers, so they can't fit the hidden tests. That includes a review round's implementer, who reads the findings an MCP reviewer writes. Two things fall on different sides of that line:
- **The PR's diff of files the implementer wrote is the implementer's own text.** Showing it to the owner's reviewer reveals nothing the implementer doesn't already have.
- **Holdout-only material must stay withheld.** That covers hidden test text, holdout results, and report prose quoting them.

## Change
Return the delivered head's diff for files that are in the PR's tree, without holdout withholding. Keep withholding holdout-only material: hidden tests not in the PR, holdout sections of reports, and verifier prose. Keep the existing private-string and credential redaction on everything.

Report sections and file diffs that are still withheld should say why, for example `withheld: holdout result`, and how much was withheld. Say the same in the tool description, so a reviewer knows what it can and can't see.

## Acceptance
On a run whose holdout tests share words with the feature, `limitless_get_change` returns the implementer's diff text, with private strings and credentials redacted.

The holdout test text, and any report line that quotes it, stays withheld.

Tests must cover both, and show the first one failing on today's code.

Privacy-sensitive: land only when every review finding is fixed.

Budget: about 120 changed source lines, plus tests. Out of scope: the feed, review rounds and other MCP tools.

Closes #509

findings.title: A holdout quotation wrapped across report lines stays visible
findings.detail: Report withholding checks each line on its own (lines 347-355). Cross-line matching covers only catalogue details that already contain a line break (line 326). So private single-line holdout prose that a report quotes wrapped across lines stays visible. Reproduced: a non-public criterion H-1 with evidence `the amber lantern glows`, and a persisted report.md containing `Quoted result: the amber lantern\nglows\nPublic checks passed.`. The report page returned by `limitless_get_change` still shows both `amber lantern` and `glows`. Main's source shows them too, but #509 requires that any report line quoting holdout material stays withheld, and this PR rewrites exactly this filter. Fix: before splitting a report into lines, match each holdout prose detail with whitespace normalized, treating line breaks and their escaped forms as spaces, and withhold every line the match spans. Apply it to verifier prose in the same way. Add a test that fails on today's code: the wrapped quotation is withheld, and the following public line (`Public checks passed.`) stays visible.

findings.title: Short or malformed criterion IDs and generic evidence become global private patterns
findings.detail: This PR adds every non-public criterion ID to the catalogue (line 258). It also adds whole private-row prose (lines 243-244). Both apply to every report line. A verifier ID such as `a` or `1`, or generic evidence such as `Passed`, therefore withholds ordinary lines. Reproduced: a non-public criterion with id `a` hides the report lines `All gates passed` and `2 files changed`. Main's source keeps them visible, so this PR introduced it. Fix: add a criterion ID only when it canonically matches one of the run's holdout scenario IDs. Add whole prose only when it is distinctive: more than one word and at least the existing DISTINCTIVE_LENGTH, so that short generic phrases stay public. Real holdout quotations must still be withheld. Add a test that shows ordinary lines visible alongside a malformed id and generic evidence, and that fails on this PR's current code.

head: c4202d52af600e0340c30b5314190469fea339ac
prompt:
# Agent surface accuracy: merge fields, MCP approver names, specific change-view and 401 errors

Small accuracy issues from the new-agent test re-run (#473, v2, 2026-10-13). None blocked the agent, but each gave it wrong or unhelpful information.

1. **Merge fields still disagree.** For the same PR, the land queue's merge left the parent run's `run.merged` with `mergedBy: null` and `mergedAt: null`: feed 1388 for sandbox #12, and 1411 for #14. The round run's event for #14 (1415) says "merged by MattFlower". #476 aimed for consistent merge fields, so fill them from the merge the queue recorded.
2. **MCP approvals are recorded as `reviewer: "human"`.** See `review.approved` 1385, 1392 and 1409. Record the MCP consumer instead (`mcp:<consumer>`, as #479 did for `requestedBy`), so the feed shows who approved.
3. **The change-view error says nothing specific.** `limitless_get_change` with `{"run": …, "file": 1}`, called just after a conflict round moved the head, returned `Change view request failed; check arguments and local availability.` Name the failing part: an unknown file index, a head that changed (give the new head), or a commit not available locally.
4. **The CLI's 401 blames the CLI version.** After #499, a CLI whose `LIMITLESS_URL` names a different origin for the same daemon (`http://localhost:7400` against a token issued for `http://127.0.0.1:7400`) gets `401: API token required …; update the limitless CLI`. The CLI is current: it withheld the token because the origin differs. Say that, and name the origin the token is bound to.

## Acceptance
Each item has a test that fails on today's code. Behaviour is otherwise unchanged.

Budget: about 100 changed source lines, plus tests. Out of scope: the feed filter and review rounds (#510), change-view redaction (#515, #516).

Closes #512

findings.title: The post-merge metadata read opens a window where a cancel is overwritten
findings.detail: After `mergePullRequest` succeeds, `merge()` now awaits `(this.deps.client ?? getGitHubPr)(entry.prUrl, signal)` before calling `landed()`. Before this PR, `landed()` ran right after the merge, with nothing awaited in between. A cancel during the new read aborts the signal and records the entry as `cancelled`. The read's `.catch(() => null)` then swallows the abort, and `landed()` → `finish(entry.id, "landed", …)` overwrites the cancel. Late writes must never overwrite a cancel (AGENTS.md, #388). Fix: record the landing exactly as before, immediately after the merge. Then fill `mergedBy` and `mergedAt` as a best-effort, conditional update of the run fields only: it never changes the land entry's state, and it writes only fields that are still null. Add a test that cancels during that read and fails on this PR's current code, and keep the read bounded.

findings.title: Marking the owner merged can resolve the landed round as superseded
findings.detail: `landed()` now calls `updateRun(id, { merged: true, … })` for both the entry's run and the owner run. `updateRun` calls `supersedeByIssue()` whenever `merged` is set (src/db/store.ts, around line 1780), and that resolves every `needs_human` run in the repository that closes one of the same issues, except the run being updated. The land entry's run is often the review round (for example #514's land entry is its round run), and a round's prompt keeps the original request with its `Closes #N`. So when the round is `needs_human`, the owner update resolves the round that just landed as `superseded`, not merged. Later reconciliation preserves that resolution. Before this PR only the entry's run was updated. Fix: record the merge for each run being landed through the merge resolver (`resolveMergedRun`, which handles needs_human and resolved transitions), before any supersession. Supersession must exclude the runs being landed. Add a test that fails today: a needs_human round and a succeeded owner, both closing #N; after landing, the round is resolved as merged and not superseded.

findings.title: MCP approvals without a consumer are still recorded as human
findings.detail: #512 asked that MCP approvals stop being recorded as `human`. With this PR an MCP `limitless_review` call that omits the optional `consumer` still records `human`, and the new test asserts that (test/mcp-proxy.test.ts around lines 81 and 93). Fix: at the MCP boundary, record a review without a consumer as `mcp`, and with one as `mcp:<consumer>`. Keep the HTTP and CLI `reviewer` behaviour unchanged. Nothing branches on the reviewer value, so this affects attribution only. Update the test so it fails on today's code.

findings.title: Landing publishes before its outer transaction commits, and never drains the feed

Subscribers can therefore see merge and resolution messages that a later failure in the same transaction rolls back. Then `publishFeed()` returns early because `db.inTransaction` is true (around line 686), and nothing drains the feed after the outer commit. Publish the buffered messages and drain the feed only after the outermost commit. findings.title: A cancelled entry drops an already confirmed merge
findings.detail: When the entry is no longer active, `landed()` returns before recording anything. That skips the entry transition, as intended, but it also skips every run merge record. A late observation can confirm the merge after a cancel: `awaitCi()` returns a `MERGED` observation (around line 458) and `landed()` discards it. Cancelled entries are not processed again on restart (around line 145), so the runs stay unmerged until the notifier happens to observe the merge with a valid `mergedAt`. Fix: keep the entry `cancelled`, but always record a merge GitHub confirmed for the PR's runs, through the same resolver path. Add a test: cancel the entry, then let the observation report MERGED. The entry stays cancelled and the runs are resolved as merged, with no second merge command.

findings.title: Landing through the owner run still supersedes the PR's own rounds
findings.detail: The round-1 fix covers an entry that names a round run: `ids` then holds the round and its owner. When the entry names the owner run, which test/land-queue.test.ts around line 1629 supports, `ids` is just the owner. Marking it merged then resolves a same-issue `needs_human` round of the same PR as `superseded`, not merged (src/db/store.ts `supersedeByIssue`, around 1785 and 1889). Reconciliation passes no exclusions either (src/integrations/github-notifier.ts around 204), so restart recovery can do the same. Main already does this, but the round-1 finding asked that the runs being landed be excluded from supersession, and a PR's rounds are among them. Fix: resolve every run that shares the landed PR (the owner and all its rounds) as merged, and exclude them from supersession, whichever run the entry names. Use one helper in both `landed()` and `reconcileMergedRuns`. Add a test that lands through the owner while a same-issue `needs_human` round exists, and that fails today.

# Change view: a multiline registered credential survives patch redaction

## What happens
Found while reviewing #514. It predates that PR: main's `src/integrations/mcp-change.ts` behaves the same way.

A credential registered with a line break, for example a multi-line key `alpha-secret-…\nbeta-secret-…` (`registerCredential`, src/util/proc.ts around 671–677), appears in a unified diff as `+alpha-secret-…` and `+beta-secret-…` on separate lines.

Literal matching (src/gates/private.ts around 64–70) then fails:
- the per-line check sees only one half of the value, so it doesn't match;
- the whole-patch check doesn't match either, because the `+` prefix breaks up the literal.

So `limitless_get_change` returns both halves.

Reproduced with a throwaway test: register that two-line credential, commit a file containing both lines in the PR head, and both lines come back in `diff.text`.

## Change
Before paging, check the reconstructed new-side and old-side file text (patch lines without their `+`, `-` or ` ` prefix) against registered credentials and private strings. Map any match back to the patch lines it spans, and withhold those lines. Other places that render credentials inside a line-prefixed format (quoted output, diffs in reports) should get the same treatment, or be listed here as follow-ups.

## Acceptance
A test with a multiline registered credential in an added file fails on today's code. With the fix, neither line of the credential appears in any page of the patch, and the rest of the file stays visible.

Privacy: land only when every review finding is fixed.

Budget: About 80 changed source lines, plus tests. Out of scope: report holdout filtering (#516) and other outputs unless they render diffs. Privacy: every review finding must be fixed before landing.

Closes #515

findings.title: Replace the hunk span heuristic with whole-file withholding for multiline private values
findings.detail: The run ended after 5 rounds, and its last in-run finding is still open. A credential's last line leaks when a hunk is clipped inside the credential at end of file with no trailing newline. `privatePatchLines` (about 90 lines) reconstructs sides per hunk and matches spans, clipped prefixes and suffixes, and adjacent pairs, and each round has found another hunk-boundary case. Patches are the wrong place to look for a multiline value, because a hunk can show any slice of it. Replace the heuristic with a whole-file check. For the selected file, read its full content at the pinned base and the pinned head with the hardened git wrapper (`git show <sha>:<path>`, with the same literal-path handling already used for the diff). If either side contains any multiline registered credential or multiline private string, return no patch text for that file: `[withheld: private text; 1 file]`. Compare after the same normalization the per-line filter uses (NFKC, lowercase, and CRLF/CR as LF). Otherwise use the existing per-line `privacy()` filter unchanged. Hunk headers, function annotations, clipped hunks and missing trailing newlines then need no special handling, because the file is withheld as a whole. Remove `privatePatchLines`. Keep tests that cover: an added file with a two-line credential; a modified file whose hunk is clipped inside the credential at end of file with no trailing newline (the current failing case); a deleted file containing one; a CRLF variant; and a file with no multiline value whose diff stays fully visible. Each must fail on today's main. Budget: about 40 source lines.

prompt:
# Review eval: dependencies in review trials, and a probe-first prompt (eval only)

## Why
The M5.2 gold defects come from the orchestrator's reviews, which reproduce each finding before it counts. Production's reviewer may already run read-only commands and targeted tests, with temporary files under TMPDIR (the review prompt in `src/pipeline/prompts.ts`). It reviews after the gates, so the run's checkout has its dependencies installed.

Eval review trials differ in two ways:
- **No dependencies.** `createEvalWorktree` checks the case out without running the repository's gate setup. A probe that imports a dependency fails. One E3 trial (#531) reported "Full Factory execution was blocked by the installed Zod incompatibility". So today's review eval measures a reviewer that probes less than production's can.
- **Probes are optional.** Nothing asks the reviewer to reproduce a blocker before reporting it.

PLAN's last planned variant is reviewers that run probes instead of only reading the diff, after effort (#508), a different vendor (#522) and an adversarial prompt (#525).

## Change (eval only)
- **Dependencies, opt-in.** An eval systems file may set `setup: true` on a system. Its review trials run the case repository's gate `setup` commands in the trial's own worktree before the reviewer starts. Read the commands from the case's base commit (`gatesAt`, as the implement eval does), never from its head. Run them confined the way gate setup is, and time them as preparation, not as the trial. A failed setup fails that trial's preparation, not the eval run. Reuse the implement eval's setup path instead of adding a second one.
- **A `probe` finder prompt** for single mode, next to `adversarial` and `careful` (#525): for each blocker or major, run a probe (a throwaway test or command under TMPDIR, only the affected test files), and put the command and its observed result in the finding's `detail`. A blocker or major whose probe ran and didn't show the defect is reported as minor or not at all. A probe that can't run because of the sandbox or the environment (nested Seatbelt, loopback servers, a Linux-only path) keeps the finding's severity, and `detail` names the attempted command and the error. Never run the full suite.
- **No edit mode.** Trials stay `readonly`, as production review is.
- **Grading unchanged.** The trial grades what production would block (`blockingReviewFindings` / `reviewVerdict`), and the report records time per trial and preparation time separately.
- **Separate cache identity.** `setup` and the prompt join the trial's cache key, so these trials never reuse today's, and the reverse.
- **Production unchanged.** Production review-system validation still refuses a non-standard single prompt and `setup`.
- **Docs.** One or two lines in docs/EVALS.md under review systems.

## Acceptance
- On the fake harness, a `setup: true` system's trial runs the base commit's setup commands in its own worktree before invoking the reviewer. A head that changes the setup commands doesn't change what runs (a test shows this).
- A failed setup fails only that trial's preparation.
- Trials with `setup` or the `probe` prompt don't reuse cached trials without them.
- A production config with `probe` or `setup` is still refused.
- The schema tests fail on today's code.

Budget: about 60 source lines, plus tests. Out of scope: probes or setup in production review, the verifier, edit-mode reviewers, and the eval run itself. The run is pre-registered in its own issue once this lands, on the same 35 dev cases as #508. Its baseline is the standard prompt with `setup: true` (production's reviewer with its dependencies installed). No stored trial measures that, so it is a new paid arm, not a re-run of a stored baseline. The pre-registration names it.


Closes #530

findings.title: Setup edits to tracked files reach the reviewer
findings.detail: After `prepareEvalGates(..., true)` the trial goes straight to the review without restoring tracked files, so the reviewer reads whatever setup wrote instead of the labelled commit. Reproduced with a fixture whose base setup is `printf setup-overwrite > CURRENT.txt`: the readonly reviewer read `setup-overwrite`. Production removes gate-generated edits before review (src/pipeline/engine.ts, the checkout after gates). After setup, restore tracked content to the case head and keep ignored and untracked payloads such as node_modules, then add a test where setup modifies a tracked file and the reviewer still sees the committed content.

findings.title: A setup arm counts as production routing evidence and makes policy selection order-dependent
findings.detail: Routing evidence counts every single-mode `standard` system with the matching implementer-report mode, and its comment relies on 'at most one such system per target'. `setup: true` makes a second, distinct configuration for the same target, so an eval with a control arm and a setup arm feeds both into policy and the summary picked depends on trial order. Reproduced: control passed, setup arm failed; the selected candidate's pass rate was 1 in one trial order and 0 when the trials were reversed, with zero paired cases in both. Production review doesn't run eval setup, so exclude `setup` systems from routing evidence (the same way non-standard prompts are), with a test that a control plus setup eval routes on the control only.

findings.title: Finder replay ignores setup, so a setup system can reuse findings made without dependencies
findings.detail: `validateReplay` compares mode, finder count, prompts, lenses and targets, never `setup`. Reproduced: a panel source without setup replayed into the same panel with `setup: true`; validation passed and the trial completed with no reviewer call, so its finder results came from a checkout without dependencies. Require the source and target systems to have the same `setup` value, with a test that the mismatch is refused.

prompt:
# Catalog: a redundant runtime claude/haiku-5.5 row breaks startup after providers export, and can't be removed

Found while adjudicating M5.2 clean case review-096 (#415 at 2e75ecc). Both points are still on main (5a172e5).

## What happens
#415 made `claude/haiku-5.5` a built-in model. An installation that had added it at runtime keeps a `runtime_models` row with that id. Startup skips the row when the existing model is a code model (`src/app.ts`, around line 104), and warns on every start.

1. **`limitless providers export --write` makes the next start fail.** Export writes every effective model into config. On the next start, `claude/haiku-5.5` is a config model (`source: "config"`), the exception only covers `source: "code"`, and startup throws `catalog collision: claude/haiku-5.5`. The daemon's own startup warnings recommend that command ("deprecated implicit provider; migrate with limitless providers export --write").
2. **The row can't be removed.** `RuntimeCatalog.remove` calls `editable(id)` (`src/router/runtime-catalog.ts`), which finds the built-in and throws "code and config models are read-only". So the warning never goes away.

Reproduced at 2e75ecc with an isolated `LIMITLESS_HOME` and config directory, and no network:
1. Persist a runtime `claude/haiku-5.5` with the built-in's metadata.
2. Construct `Factory`: it starts, with the warning.
3. Run `providersExport(true, true)`.
4. Reload config and construct `Factory` again: it throws `catalog collision: claude/haiku-5.5`.

This installation has such a row.

## Change
- Startup treats a runtime row that duplicates a built-in or exported model id as redundant whatever the existing model's source: a code model, or a config model exported from it. Only a genuine conflict, a runtime model whose id belongs to an unrelated config model, stays fatal.
- Removing a redundant runtime row works. Either `limitless catalog remove <id>` deletes a runtime row that a built-in or config model shadows, or startup deletes the redundant row once and records that it did.
- No change to how other collisions are reported.

## Acceptance
- A test fails on today's code: a runtime `claude/haiku-5.5` row, then `providersExport(true, true)`, then a restart, starts without throwing.
- The row can be removed (or is removed once), and the warning stops.
- A runtime model colliding with an unrelated config model still fails startup with `catalog collision`.

Budget: about 20 source lines, plus tests.


Closes #534

findings.title: A config model that redefines a built-in id now hides a colliding runtime row
findings.detail: The guard skips a runtime row whenever its id is any built-in id (`MODELS.some((m) => m.id === model.id)`), whatever the effective model is. The issue keeps a runtime row that collides with an unrelated config model fatal, and treats only a code built-in, or a config model exported from it, as redundant. Reproduced with a throwaway test: config defines `claude/haiku-5.5` with backend `org/unrelated-model`, and a runtime `claude/haiku-5.5` row exists. The PR head starts with the unrelated backend and warns 'redundant runtime entry; using built-in definition', which is false. The merge base throws `catalog collision: claude/haiku-5.5`. Skip only when the existing model is the code built-in, or a config model whose definition equals that built-in's (what `providers export` writes); keep every other collision fatal, and make the warning name the definition actually used. Add a test with a built-in id redefined in config.

prompt:
# Factory git status runs filters configured inside nested repositories in agent checkouts

## What happens
`git status` checks each populated submodule by running git inside it, with that submodule's own git directory and configuration. The factory's `worktreeGit` empties only the hook and filter keys it finds in the checkout's own repository configuration (`src/git/command.ts`), and the land script's `safe_git` does the same (`scripts/land-pr.sh`). A filter configured in a nested repository's git directory is never found, so it runs.

A nested repository is something an agent or a gate command can create inside its checkout. `commitAll` (`src/git/repos.ts`) stages it as a gitlink with `git add -A` and then runs `git status --porcelain`. `discardChanges` runs the same status. Both run in the daemon, outside the agent's sandbox.

Reproduced on main (5a172e5) with git 2.54, using a throwaway test in a temporary repository:
1. Inside the checkout, create a nested repository with one committed file.
2. In the nested repository's `.git/config`, configure `filter.<name>.clean` to create a marker file. Assign that filter to `*` in its `.git/info/attributes`. Then change the file's mtime.
3. `commitAll(work, …)` creates the marker. So does a later `discardChanges(work)`.

The land script has the same gap in its post-check dirty check (`scripts/land-pr.sh`, the isolated `status --porcelain`). There a submodule whose `.git` file points back at the land clone's admin directory also applies a filter from the clone's own configuration, which #405 meant to rule out. It needs a gitlink in the landed commit.

## Change
- Status calls on checkouts the factory doesn't own stop inspecting submodule work trees. Pass `--ignore-submodules=dirty` on the command line: it outranks `.gitmodules` and repository configuration. In the probe it runs no filter and still reports an added gitlink (`A nested`) or a changed gitlink commit (`M nested`), so `commitAll` still commits it and the audit still blocks it. A committed `.gitmodules` with `ignore = none` doesn't re-enable the inspection.
- One guard for every path: `worktreeGit`'s base flags (or each status/porcelain diff it runs on a work tree), and `safe_git` in `scripts/land-pr.sh`. Range diffs that pass `--ignore-submodules=none` (`diffSince`, the audit) compare commits, never work trees. They keep it, so committed `.gitmodules` settings still can't hide gitlinks.
- Check every other work-tree git call in `src/git`, `src/land` and `src/pipeline` for the same recursion: diffs against the work tree, resets and checkout steps.

## Acceptance
- A test fails on today's code: `commitAll` and `discardChanges` on a checkout with a nested repository whose own config defines a clean filter don't run the filter, and the nested repository is still committed as a gitlink (the existing gitlink audit tests still pass).
- A land-script test (the `test/land-pr.test.ts` harness) covers the post-check status with a populated submodule whose `.git` points at the clone's admin directory and a filter in the clone's config.
- A committed `.gitmodules` with `ignore = none` for that submodule doesn't make the filter run.
- Committed `.gitmodules` `ignore = all` still can't hide gitlinks from the audit (existing test).

Privacy and security: land only when every review finding is fixed. Budget: about 20 source lines, plus tests.


## Constraint from the first attempt (2026-10-14)
The first run's test enabled `submodule.recurse` on a fixture whose nested repository's git directory pointed back at its parent. The run then left hundreds of live processes, and the machine's load went above 300. In these tests:
- don't set `submodule.recurse`, and don't run recursive submodule commands;
- give each nested-repository fixture its own git directory, unless the test is about a `.git` file that points at the parent's admin directory, and then run only the factory's status or diff calls on it;
- run only the affected test files, one at a time, never the full suite.

Closes #533

findings.title: git add -A in commitAll still runs a nested repository's filter
findings.detail: The new flag covers only commands named status or diff. `git add -A` runs its own status inside a populated nested repository (GIT_TRACE shows `cd nested; GIT_DIR=.git git status --porcelain=2 -uno`). Reproduced with real git 2.54 at this head: a committed gitlink plus a committed `.gitmodules` entry with `ignore = none`, then a clean filter configured in the nested repository's own .git/config, `* filter=...` in its info/attributes, its file's mtime changed and an ordinary parent file edited. `commitAll()` ran the filter (marker created) and returned a commit. The new test misses this because its second call advances the nested HEAD. Make every staging call on an agent-writable checkout (commitAll, merge completion, the eval runners' add calls) skip nested work-tree inspection even when committed `.gitmodules` asks for it, while added and changed gitlink commits are still staged and audited. Add a regression test with an unchanged existing gitlink and `ignore = none`.

findings.title: prepareMerge's internal stash still runs a nested repository's filter
findings.detail: `git merge --no-ff --no-commit` runs `git stash create`, which inspects populated nested repositories with their own configuration (trace: `git stash create`, then `cd nested; GIT_DIR=.git git status --porcelain=2`). `submodule.recurse=false` does not stop it. Reproduced at this head with the same fixture as the add finding, for an otherwise clean merge: `prepareMerge()` ran the nested filter. Cover merge's and any other command's internal dirty checks the same way, and test `prepareMerge` with a committed `.gitmodules` `ignore = none`.
