The factory's `worktreeGit` empties only the hook and filter keys it finds in the checkout's own repository configuration (`src/git/command.ts`), and the land script's `safe_git` does the same (`scripts/land-pr.sh`). A filter configured in a nested repository's git directory is never found, so it runs.

A nested repository is something an agent or a gate command can create inside its checkout. `commitAll` (`src/git/repos.ts`) stages it as a gitlink with `git add -A` and then runs `git status --porcelain`. `discardChanges` runs the same status. Both run in the daemon, outside the agent's sandbox.

Reproduced on main (5a172e5) with git 2.54, using a throwaway test in a temporary repository:
1. Inside the checkout, create a nested repository with one committed file.
2. In the nested repository's `.git/config`, configure `filter.<name>.clean` to create a marker file. Assign that filter to `*` in its `.git/info/attributes`. Then change the file's mtime.
3. `commitAll(work, …)` creates the marker. So does a later `discardChanges(work)`.

The land script has the same gap in its post-check dirty check (`scripts/land-pr.sh`, the isolated `status --porcelain`). There a submodule whose `.git` file points back at the land clone's admin directory also applies a filter from the clone's own configuration, which #405 meant to rule out. It needs a gitlink in the landed commit.

## Change
- Status calls on checkouts the factory doesn't own stop inspecting submodule work trees. Pass `--ignore-submodules=dirty` on the command line: it outranks `.gitmodules` and repository configuration. In the probe it runs no filter and still reports an added gitlink (`A nested`) or a changed gitlink commit (`M nested`), so `commitAll` still commits it and the audit still blocks it. A committed `.gitmodules` with `ignore = none` doesn't re-enable the inspection.
- One guard for every path: `worktreeGit`'s base flags (or each status/porcelain diff it runs on a work tree), and `safe_git` in `scripts/land-pr.sh`. Range diffs that pass `--ignore-submodules=none` (`diffSince`, the audit) compare commits, never work trees. They keep it, so committed `.gitmodules` settings still can't hide gitlinks.
- Check every other work-tree git call in `src/git`, `src/land` and `src/pipeline` for the same recursion: diffs against the work tree, resets and checkout steps.

## Acceptance
- A test fails on today's code: `commitAll` and `discardChanges` on a checkout with a nested repository whose own config defines a clean filter don't run the filter, and the nested repository is still committed as a gitlink (the existing gitlink audit tests still pass).
- A land-script test (the `test/land-pr.test.ts` harness) covers the post-check status with a populated submodule whose `.git` points at the clone's admin directory and a filter in the clone's config.
- A committed `.gitmodules` with `ignore = none` for that submodule doesn't make the filter run.
- Committed `.gitmodules` `ignore = all` still can't hide gitlinks from the audit (existing test).

Privacy and security: land only when every review finding is fixed. Budget: about 20 source lines, plus tests.


## Constraint from the first attempt (2026-10-14)
The first run's test enabled `submodule.recurse` on a fixture whose nested repository's git directory pointed back at its parent. The run then left hundreds of live processes, and the machine's load went above 300. In these tests:
- don't set `submodule.recurse`, and don't run recursive submodule commands;
- give each nested-repository fixture its own git directory, unless the test is about a `.git` file that points at the parent's admin directory, and then run only the factory's status or diff calls on it;
- run only the affected test files, one at a time, never the full suite.

Closes #533

findings.title: Merge still runs a nested repository's filter when .gitmodules no longer maps the gitlink
findings.detail: `submoduleFlags` overrides `submodule.<name>.ignore` only for names in the current `.gitmodules` (worktree file, else index or HEAD). A gitlink without a current mapping keeps the committed configuration for git's internal dirty checks. Reproduced at this head with real git 2.54: a tracked populated gitlink, a committed `.gitmodules` with `ignore = none`, a clean filter in the nested repository's own config, then only the worktree `.gitmodules` emptied. `prepareMerge` ran the filter (trace: `git stash create`, then `cd nested; GIT_DIR=.git git status --porcelain=2 -uno`). Codex also reproduced it with an include-only file and a changed path mapping, and adding the HEAD name's override by hand still failed. Name-specific overrides can't cover this. Make the protection independent of `.gitmodules`: the factory never populates submodules itself, so either refuse with a clear reason before any merge, rebase or other command with an internal dirty check runs in a checkout that contains a populated nested repository (a gitlink path or untracked directory holding `.git`), or prove another mechanism with tests. Cover an emptied, include-only and remapped `.gitmodules`.

findings.title: stageAll fails on file and directory replacements that add -A handles
findings.detail: Passing every cached and untracked path to `update-index --add --remove --replace` fails when a path changes kind. Reproduced by Codex against `add -A` in identical repositories: tracked `keep` replaced by directory `keep/inside` fails with `keep: is a directory - add individual files instead`, and tracked `folder/inside` replaced by symlink `folder` fails with `'folder/inside' is beyond a symbolic link`. `add -A` stages both. This breaks commitAll, merge completion and eval grading for ordinary changes. Remove index entries whose paths are gone or replaced before adding the new ones, and add tests for both replacements.

findings.title: A conflicted .gitmodules makes rebase cleanup throw before it can abort
findings.detail: `submoduleFlags` throws `Cannot inspect submodule configuration` when it can't parse `.gitmodules`. After a rebase that leaves conflict markers in `.gitmodules`, the wrapper throws before `rebaseOnto`'s `rebase --abort` runs, so the rebase directory stays active (reproduced by Codex with conflicting section-name edits; plain `git rebase --abort` then succeeded). Abort and cleanup commands must always run; don't let configuration parsing block them, and keep failing closed only for commands that would otherwise run a dirty check. Add a test with a conflicted `.gitmodules`.

# Workers: pull-based gate workers (pairing, heartbeats, leased gate jobs)

Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput), the slice after the executor seam (#482). Matt decided on 2026-10-10 that other machines join as **discovered, as-available workers**, not as a fixed list. This slice builds the worker protocol and a `lan` gate executor on top of the seam. Discovery over Bonjour and availability rules follow in the next slice; here a worker is given the coordinator's URL.

Design reference: docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md §6.2 (executor interface), §3.5 (infrastructure failures).

## Shape
**Workers connect out to the coordinator, the way CI runners do.**
- A worker runs `limitless worker --coordinator https://<host>:<port>`.
- The coordinator never holds a list of machines. It knows only the workers that are paired and sending heartbeats right now.

## Change
1. **A worker listener on the coordinator, off by default.**
   - Configured with `[workers] listen = "<address>:<port>"`.
   - It serves only `/worker/*` routes, separate from the owner API and its port.
   - TLS uses a self-signed certificate generated at first start. Its key is stored as a private file: mode 0600 and read-denied in every agent sandbox, the same way as the API token (#484) and the credential stores (#487).
2. **Pairing.**
   - `limitless worker pair --coordinator <url>` sends the worker's name and its certificate fingerprint.
   - The coordinator records a pending request and shows a short code. The worker prints the same code.
   - The owner approves with `limitless workers approve <code>` (an authenticated owner route), or in the UI.
   - The coordinator then issues a per-worker token and stores only its hash. The worker stores the token and the coordinator's fingerprint, pinned.
   - `limitless workers revoke <name>` ends a worker's access at once.
   - The pairing route only ever creates a pending request. It's rate-limited and grants nothing until approved.
3. **Heartbeats, every 10 s, with the worker's token.** Each carries:
   - the release SHA, bun version, OS and version, CPU count and RAM;
   - free gate slots, whether the machine is on AC power, and idle seconds;
   - the jobs the worker holds.

   The coordinator keeps a `workers` table (additive migration) with each worker's last heartbeat and capabilities. A worker counts as available only while its heartbeats are fresh (30 s).
4. **Version lockstep.** A worker gets jobs only when its release SHA and bun version equal the coordinator's. Otherwise it shows as "needs update" and receives nothing.
5. **Gate jobs** (a `gate_jobs` table: request, state, worker, lease expiry, result).
   - The `lan` executor's `start` enqueues a job and returns `{ kind: "lan", id }`. `attach` waits for the job's result from the store, so a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.
   - Workers long-poll `POST /worker/lease` (up to 30 s). A job goes only to a matching, available worker that is asking for work at that moment.
   - Leases expire after 60 s unless renewed by heartbeats.
6. **The worker runs the job.**
   - It fetches `GET /worker/jobs/:id/bundle`, a git bundle of the head (and base) from the coordinator's repository cache, so the worker needs no GitHub credentials. It imports the bundle into its own repository cache through the hardened git wrapper.
   - It checks out exactly the requested head and records `git rev-parse HEAD`.
   - It runs the request's gate config through `runLocalGates`, with its own Seatbelt confinement, scratch and gate slots.
   - It posts check events as they finish, then the `GateRun` and the checked SHA.
   - The worker redacts output with its own registered credentials before sending. Its token and the coordinator's fingerprint are read-denied to its gates.
7. **The coordinator checks the result.**
   - The result is untrusted data. It's validated against the `GateRun` schema, its SHA must equal the requested head, and its checks must be the requested ones.
   - It's redacted again with the coordinator's credentials and private strings before anything stores or shows it.
   - A result that fails any check is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
8. **Infrastructure failures**:
   - no worker took the job within 60 s;
   - the lease expired;
   - the worker disconnected;
   - the result was invalid.

   These retry once on another available worker, then fall back to the local executor. They are logged as gate events, never sent to the implementer as feedback, and never turn a failing check into a pass. Cancelling the run cancels the job, and the worker stops it on its next heartbeat or lease reply.
9. **Selection.**
   - `[gates] executor = "lan"`, with `[workers] repos = ["owner/name"]` as a per-repository opt-in. Code goes to other machines only for listed repositories.
   - The prepare baseline and the run's gates use the same executor kind. The executor kind joins the baseline cache's environment hash.

## Tests (loopback only, temporary homes, no external network)
Run an in-process coordinator listener and a worker loop over loopback TLS, with certificates generated in temporary directories:
- **Pairing:**
  - an unapproved worker gets no token and no jobs;
  - approval issues a token;
  - revoking a worker refuses its next heartbeat.
- **A job end to end:** the worker leases it, runs real gate commands from a bundle and posts the result. The `GateRun` matches what the local executor gives for the same commit.
- **Restart:** a coordinator restart between `start` and the result re-attaches and doesn't enqueue again.
- **Infrastructure failures:**
  - a worker that stops heartbeating mid-job loses the lease;
  - the job retries once, then runs locally;
  - no implementer feedback is recorded.
- **Bad results:**
  - one whose SHA differs from the request is refused and treated as an infrastructure failure;
  - an extra check, or a check missing from the request, is refused the same way.
- **Version mismatch:** a mismatched worker gets no jobs.
- **Privacy:**
  - the worker's token and the coordinator's TLS key are unreadable from the gate sandbox (real-Seatbelt probes, `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`);
  - a credential printed by a gate reaches the coordinator redacted.

## Budget
About 450 source lines plus tests. If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop.

## Out of scope
- Bonjour discovery, availability rules (AC power, idle) and a Workers page in the UI: the next slice.
- Whole-run workers, workers that update themselves, and waking sleeping machines.
- Linux workers (they need their own confinement).
- Model logins on workers.


Closes #513

findings.title: About 2.8 times the source budget: split as #513 says
findings.detail: #513's budget is about 450 source lines plus tests, and it says: 'If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the lan executor and the worker loop.' This PR adds about 1260 source lines. Keep the first slice here: listener and TLS (src/workers/tls.ts), pairing and heartbeats (src/server/workers.ts, src/workers/protocol.ts, src/workers/validation.ts, src/db/workers.ts and its migration), config, the CLI commands and the GUIDE section. Remove the second slice: src/gates/lan.ts; the src/gates/executor.ts, src/gates/cache.ts, src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts and src/pipeline/engine.ts changes; src/workers/client.ts's job loop; and their tests. It moves to #547, which points at this head for the existing code. With the second slice gone, no gate job can be leased: say so in the GUIDE, and keep the first slice's acceptance tests (pairing, heartbeats, revocation, TLS pinning) passing.

prompt:
# M5.1: confirm a failing test check by re-running only its failing files first

## Why (measured 2026-10-10, this repository, with 1 gate slot since 2026-10-09 20:13)
When a test check fails after the change, the gate re-runs the whole check once inside a slot to tell a regression from a flake (`src/gates/run.ts`, the post-change retry). In this window:
- There were 6 such retries. From the failure to the retry's result took 4.3 hours of run wall time in total, with a median of 52 minutes each, mostly waiting for the single slot behind other suites.
- 4 of the 6 failed again: real regressions the implementer then fixed. 2 passed and were classified flaky.

Example: #476's run spent about 2 of its 2 h 25 m in gates, around a 39-second fix.

## Change
1. **Targeted retry first.** For a check whose test runner can list its failures in a parsed, structured way, retry only the failing test files.
   - Configure it per repository in the base commit's `.limitless.toml`, for example `[gates] retry_files = "bun test {files}"`.
   - For this repository, get the failing files from bun's structured reporter (`--reporter=junit` or equivalent). Don't scrape the human-readable output.
   - If the files can't be determined, fall back to today's full retry.
2. **Honest classification.**
   - A targeted retry that fails again confirms a regression, as today.
   - A targeted retry that passes is not yet a flake: a test can pass alone and fail beside others. Run the full check once more, as today, before classifying the failure flaky.
   - A flake keeps its `flaky` classification and its original failure (AGENTS.md "Retries and fallbacks are bounded and honest"). A security check's failure never becomes a pass.
3. **The slot.** A targeted retry of a few files may run without waiting for the gate slot. Make that conditional on a size bound, the number of files and the earlier duration.
4. Baseline retries use the same rule.

## Tests (no network, fake runner)
- A failure whose files are known gets a targeted retry. If it fails again, it's a regression, with no full rerun.
- If it passes, the full check runs once more and decides between flaky and regression.
- Unknown files fall back to a full retry.
- Configuration comes from the base commit only.
- A security check still never passes on a retry.

## Out of scope
Timeouts, which #347 covers. The gate-slot limit.


Closes #480

findings.title: Targeted retry arguments are Bun path filters, so the retry can run files that never failed
findings.detail: Only names starting with '-' get a './' prefix. Bun treats any other relative argument as a substring filter over test paths. Reproduction (Bun 1.4.2): files a.test.ts, data.test.ts and test/a.test.ts; `bun test 'a.test.ts'` ran all 3 files, `bun test './a.test.ts'` ran 1. Codex reproduced the same with test/a.test.ts and other/test/a.test.ts: the bare form also ran the unrelated failing file and exited 1. So a targeted retry can confirm a failure in a file that passed in the original run, and the five-file bound for skipping the gate slot does not bound what actually runs. Fix: prefix every validated relative name with './' (keep the quoting), and add a test where a failing file name is a substring of another file's path.

findings.title: The targeted retry runs files without the per-file isolation the full check has
findings.detail: The full check runs `bun test --parallel=...`, and `bun test --help` says --parallel implies --isolate (a fresh global object per file). The retry template `bun test {files}` runs every file in one shared global. Reproduction: two files that each read and then set globalThis.owner, expecting it unset first. `bun test --parallel=1 ./a.test.ts ./b.test.ts` passes both; `bun test ./a.test.ts ./b.test.ts` fails b (it sees a's value). A targeted retry of two or more files can therefore fail when the full check would pass. After the change that becomes a false regression with no full rerun. On the baseline it is worse: the base check stays failing, and a check that fails on base never blocks, so a real regression in that check is not blocking for the whole run. Codex reproduced that end to end: retryBaselineFailures kept the baseline failing, and compareGates then returned still_failing with blocking=false for a candidate failure. Fix: `retry_files = "bun test --isolate {files}"`, with a test that two files leaking a global pass in a targeted retry.

findings.title: The baseline cache stores the new failure-file fields before redaction
findings.detail: `store.putBaselineCache(key, fresh, ...)` writes the baseline before `ctx.state.baseline = redactGateData(...)` runs at line 589. Before this PR the cached result's outputs were already redacted at capture (runOne passes redactOutput: true). The new fields are not: firstAttempt.failedFiles, the failedFileTimes keys and targetedRetry.command (which contains the file names) come from the report unredacted. Reproduction (Codex, temporary factory test): register a synthetic credential, use it in a failing test file name, script baseline failure, then targeted pass, then full pass. The run succeeds and the run state and events are redacted, but `SELECT gate_run FROM passing_baselines` contains the literal credential in all three fields. AGENTS.md requires redaction wherever secret-bearing text is stored. Fix: redact the baseline before caching it (one redaction for both the cache and the run state), plus a test that reads the cache row.

findings.title: A targeted retry that skips the gate slot keeps the check's full timeout
findings.detail: The bypass checks the earlier JUnit duration (at most 60 s over at most 5 files), but the retry inherits the check's timeoutSec (1800 s here). A file that hangs on retry (an intermittent deadlock is a common flake) then runs outside the gate slot for up to 30 minutes, holding one of the two agentTestSlots that implementers' test runs share. The duration also comes from a report written by the run under test, so it is a hint, not a limit. Reproduction (Codex): parse a report with `<testsuite file="test/a.test.ts" failures="1" time="0"/>`, then call retryRegressions; the runner receives targeted=true, skipGateSlot=true and the unchanged 1800 s timeout. Fix: when a retry skips the slot, cap its timeout at a small multiple of the bound (for example 2 x UNSLOTTED_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS). A targeted timeout already falls through to the slotted full retry, so the cap enforces the bound without losing the check. Apply it once, in retryFailures, so the baseline and regression paths share it. Add a test that the unslotted request carries the capped timeout and that a timeout leads to the full retry.

findings.title: A confirmed targeted failure replaces the full check's output, so the implementer can miss failures the report doesn't list
findings.detail: When the targeted retry fails, the result becomes `{ ...attempt, firstAttempt, targetedRetry }`, and formatGateFeedback shows only that attempt's command and output. Bun's JUnit report leaves out a test file that throws while loading. Reproduction (Bun 1.4.2): c.test.ts throws at top level and d.test.ts has a failing test; the command exits 1, but the report lists only d.test.ts and parseJUnit returns failedFiles ["d.test.ts"]. The targeted retry of d fails again, the regression is confirmed (correctly), but the feedback no longer shows c.test.ts's load error, which costs the implementer an extra round. Classification is unaffected, because a targeted pass always goes on to the full retry. Fix: when a targeted retry confirms the failure, keep the original full run as the visible result (command and output) and attach the targeted attempt as targetedRetry; or include the first attempt's output in the feedback. Add a test that the feedback for a confirmed targeted failure still contains the original output.

4. **Version lockstep.** A worker gets jobs only when its release SHA and bun version equal the coordinator's. Otherwise it shows as "needs update" and receives nothing.
5. **Gate jobs** (a `gate_jobs` table: request, state, worker, lease expiry, result).
   - The `lan` executor's `start` enqueues a job and returns `{ kind: "lan", id }`. `attach` waits for the job's result from the store, so a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.
   - Workers long-poll `POST /worker/lease` (up to 30 s). A job goes only to a matching, available worker that is asking for work at that moment.
   - Leases expire after 60 s unless renewed by heartbeats.
6. **The worker runs the job.**
   - It fetches `GET /worker/jobs/:id/bundle`, a git bundle of the head (and base) from the coordinator's repository cache, so the worker needs no GitHub credentials. It imports the bundle into its own repository cache through the hardened git wrapper.
   - It checks out exactly the requested head and records `git rev-parse HEAD`.
   - It runs the request's gate config through `runLocalGates`, with its own Seatbelt confinement, scratch and gate slots.
   - It posts check events as they finish, then the `GateRun` and the checked SHA.
   - The worker redacts output with its own registered credentials before sending. Its token and the coordinator's fingerprint are read-denied to its gates.
7. **The coordinator checks the result.**
   - The result is untrusted data. It's validated against the `GateRun` schema, its SHA must equal the requested head, and its checks must be the requested ones.
   - It's redacted again with the coordinator's credentials and private strings before anything stores or shows it.
   - A result that fails any check is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
8. **Infrastructure failures**:
   - no worker took the job within 60 s;
   - the lease expired;
   - the worker disconnected;
   - the result was invalid.

   These retry once on another available worker, then fall back to the local executor. They are logged as gate events, never sent to the implementer as feedback, and never turn a failing check into a pass. Cancelling the run cancels the job, and the worker stops it on its next heartbeat or lease reply.
9. **Selection.**
   - `[gates] executor = "lan"`, with `[workers] repos = ["owner/name"]` as a per-repository opt-in. Code goes to other machines only for listed repositories.
   - The prepare baseline and the run's gates use the same executor kind. The executor kind joins the baseline cache's environment hash.

## Tests (loopback only, temporary homes, no external network)
Run an in-process coordinator listener and a worker loop over loopback TLS, with certificates generated in temporary directories:
- **Pairing:**
  - an unapproved worker gets no token and no jobs;
  - approval issues a token;
  - revoking a worker refuses its next heartbeat.
- **A job end to end:** the worker leases it, runs real gate commands from a bundle and posts the result. The `GateRun` matches what the local executor gives for the same commit.
- **Restart:** a coordinator restart between `start` and the result re-attaches and doesn't enqueue again.
- **Infrastructure failures:**
  - a worker that stops heartbeating mid-job loses the lease;
  - the job retries once, then runs locally;
  - no implementer feedback is recorded.
- **Bad results:**
  - one whose SHA differs from the request is refused and treated as an infrastructure failure;
  - an extra check, or a check missing from the request, is refused the same way.
- **Version mismatch:** a mismatched worker gets no jobs.
- **Privacy:**
  - the worker's token and the coordinator's TLS key are unreadable from the gate sandbox (real-Seatbelt probes, `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`);
  - a credential printed by a gate reaches the coordinator redacted.

## Budget
About 450 source lines plus tests. If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop.

## Out of scope
- Bonjour discovery, availability rules (AC power, idle) and a Workers page in the UI: the next slice.
- Whole-run workers, workers that update themselves, and waking sleeping machines.
- Linux workers (they need their own confinement).
- Model logins on workers.


Closes #513

findings.title: Pairing can't detect a relay between worker and coordinator
findings.detail: The worker accepts any certificate on its first request, prints the code the server returned, and pins whatever fingerprint it observed. The displayed code is chosen by the server and is not bound to either TLS endpoint, so comparing the two codes cannot show that the worker reached a different machine. Reproduction (Codex): two loopback TLS listeners, one relaying /worker/pair and /worker/pair/claim to the coordinator. Both displayed codes matched, pairWorker saved the relay's fingerprint instead of the coordinator's, and the token the relay received then authenticated to the coordinator. Fix: derive the displayed code independently on each side from values each side observed: the coordinator from its own certificate fingerprint, the worker fingerprint in the request and a server nonce; the worker from the coordinator fingerprint it observed on the TLS socket, its own fingerprint and the nonce from the reply. The worker must print its locally derived code, never a code from the response. In the same probe, independently derived codes differed through the relay. Add a test with an in-process relay showing the codes differ, and one showing they match on a direct connection.

findings.title: The coordinator key and worker credentials are read-denied only while a listener or worker process holds them
findings.detail: protectPrivateFile runs inside certificate() and privateFile(), so a path is protected only while that call's holder is alive. startWorkerListener returns before certificate() when [workers] listen is unset, and the worker files are protected only inside the `limitless worker` process. Its registrations don't reach agents launched by a daemon on the same machine, and runWorker never protects worker/key.pem. The API token (src/server/api-token.ts) and the database (src/db/store.ts) are protected for the daemon's whole lifetime. Reproduction (Codex, real Seatbelt): start and stop the listener, then start with listen unset; an editor profile built through homeReadPolicy could read the retained worker-tls/key.pem, while the active listener's profile denied it. With a worker running against the same data home, sandboxed reads of worker/token, worker/key.pem and worker/coordinator-fingerprint succeeded. Fix: at daemon start, before integrations or runs start and whether or not a listener is configured, protect worker-tls/key.pem, worker/token, worker/key.pem and worker/coordinator-fingerprint, and keep them protected until shutdown. Also protect worker/key.pem in runWorker. Extend the real-Seatbelt test to start the daemon's protection with listen unset and probe all four paths.

findings.title: The pairing claim secret is not registered for redaction
findings.detail: The 64-hex claim secret lets its holder collect the worker's token once the pairing is approved, but neither side registers it, so redactCredentials leaves it unchanged in logs, errors and events. Reproduction (Codex): complete a pairing, then pass its secret through redactCredentials; it comes back unchanged, while the issued token is redacted. Fix: registerCredential for the secret on the coordinator when it is issued and on the worker when it is received. The short pairing code is meant to be displayed and can stay in its two intended displays.

findings.title: Expired pairing requests accumulate past the pending cap and still list as pending
findings.detail: The 100-request cap counts only unexpired rows, and nothing removes expired ones. Reproduction (Codex, injected clock): create 100 requests, advance 600001 ms, and repeat three times. The table holds 300 pending rows and list() shows all 300 as pending. The unauthenticated pairing route can therefore grow the table and the owner's `workers ls` without bound. Fix: delete expired pending rows when a pairing is created (the same transaction as the count), and show only unexpired requests as pending. Add a test with the injected clock.

findings.title: No test shows that a wrong claim secret gets no token
findings.detail: Mutation (Codex): change claim() so an unmatched secret falls back to the first approved worker. A 64-character zero secret then returns that worker's token, yet all 51 tests in test/workers.test.ts and test/config-routing.test.ts still pass. Add negative claim tests: a correctly shaped wrong secret, another pairing's secret (returns only that pairing's own state, never the first worker's token), and the secret of a revoked pairing. Each must fail under that mutation.

prompt:
# Resuming a run sanitizes state it later executes or compares

## What's wrong
When the daemon reopens a run, the `RunContext` constructor sanitizes every string in the stored run state (`this.state = redactGateData(this.state)`, `src/pipeline/context.ts`). That is right for diagnostics: legacy gate output, feedback and errors may hold registered credentials or terminal escapes from before #393. But it also rewrites state that the run later executes or compares exactly. So a resumed run can behave differently from an uninterrupted one whenever a stored value contains a registered credential or a terminal escape.

Found while reviewing #486, on 2026-10-11, with temporary tests:
- On `origin/main`, a gate command containing a registered synthetic credential, killed at `gate-started` and resumed, runs `[redacted]` instead of the command, and the run ends needs_human.
- A partial fix shows the coupling. #486's round 3 kept `gatesConfig` literal but left the stored baseline sanitized, and a gate whose name contains `ESC[31m` then stopped matching its baseline in `compareGates` (`src/gates/run.ts`): it was a blocking `new_failure` instead of `still_failing`. Main sanitizes both sides, so it matches today. Any fix must keep the two consistent.

Fields the constructor sanitizes that are later executed, used as git refs or paths, or compared exactly:
- **Commands and configuration:** `gatesConfig`, `baselineScripts`, `previewConfig` (build, seed and serve commands, environment values, readiness paths).
- **Paths and refs:** `worktreePath`, `conflictFiles`, `reviewBaseSha`, `pendingRebaseSha`, `preRebaseHead`, `lastVerifiedSha`, `reviewedSha`, `verification`.
- **Identities and IDs:** gate names inside `baseline`, `preRebaseGates`, `lastGates`, `gateEvidence` and `completedChecks`; criterion and scenario IDs in `spec` and `holdout`; finding IDs in `lastAudit` and `lastReview`; routing identities (`implementer`, `triedImplementers`, `specAuthorVendor`, `holdoutModelId`); review lens names; and control strings such as `phase` and `flow`.

Numbers and booleans are unaffected. It is rare in practice, because a value has to contain a registered credential or a terminal escape, but when it happens the run's outcome changes silently.

## Change
- Load stored state literally. Sanitize the outward copies instead, at the points where state leaves the process or reaches a model: events, run errors, feedback and prompts, PR comments, MCP and HTTP output (HTTP and SSE reads already go through `redactGateData`).
- Keep sanitizing legacy diagnostic fields on load (`feedback`, `terminalReason`, `needsHumanReason`, `implementerReport`, `implementerIssue`, `rebaseNote`, and gate `output`/`failures`). Those are only ever shown, never executed or compared.
- Gate audit findings that quote package scripts (`gate-script-changed`, `src/gates/audit.ts`) must be redacted before they are stored as events, feedback or errors. The quoted script comes from the base commit's checkout, which the agent can already read, so this is defence in depth rather than a new exposure.

## Tests
- A run whose stored gate command contains a registered synthetic credential, killed at `gate-started` and resumed, runs the literal command and gets the uninterrupted verdict.
- A gate named with a literal `ESC[31m`, failing on both baseline and candidate, stays `still_failing` after a resume.
- After a resume, legacy feedback containing the credential still reaches the run error and events only as `[redacted]`, as `test/pipeline-review.test.ts` checks today.

## Out of scope
The executor seam (#486) keeps main's load-time behaviour exactly; this issue changes it.

## Budget
About 60 changed source lines plus tests.


Closes #494

findings.title: Verification artifacts now store gate evidence without credential or escape redaction
findings.detail: preDeliveryVerifyArtifact only applies redactHoldoutText. Before this PR, the gate names and commands it copies into evidence and gateEvidence had already been sanitized on load. Now they stay literal, and delivery republishes the raw verifyResults. Reproduction (Codex): register a synthetic credential S, name a passing gate ESC[31mS, and have a fake verifier report a covered criterion as sandbox-blocked. Interrupt at stage:verify:after and resume. The run succeeds, but verify-0.json contains literal S and the ESC byte in both evidence and gateEvidence.check. On main the same artifact holds [redacted]. Fix: redact every run artifact at one boundary, for example a ctx.artifact helper that applies redactGateData the way ctx.event does, and route all putArtifact calls in src/pipeline through it (AGENTS.md "One guard, every path"). Add a test that reads verify-0.json after the resume.

findings.title: redactGateDiagnostics treats any object with ok and output keys as a gate result, including package script maps
findings.detail: The walker rewrites every object that has an `ok` key and a string `output`. baselineScripts maps package.json script names to commands, so a repository with scripts named ok and output matches. Its `output` command is then redacted on load, and confinementError is inserted as if it were a script. Reproduction (Codex): scripts {ok: 'true', output: 'true # S'} with S a registered credential, and gates that invoke both scripts. Kill at gate-started and resume: the audit reports a changed `output` script and a removed `confinementError` script, and the run ends needs_human. On main the same run resumes and succeeds. This is the class of bug #494 fixes: resuming changes an executed value. Fix: redact diagnostics only at the known GateResult locations (baseline.setup/checks, preRebaseGates, lastGates[].result and firstAttempt, completedChecks values that are GateResults), not by key shape anywhere in the state. Add the scripts case as a test.

findings.title: A restored shadow review error is written to its artifact unredacted
findings.detail: shadowLenses.error is a diagnostic (an error message), but it isn't in the legacy field list that's redacted on load, and review-shadow.ts stores it with a raw putArtifact. Reproduction (Codex): register a synthetic credential S, use it as a gate name, seed a legacy shadowLenses.error containing S, reload the RunContext, and call shadowReview with no model invocation. review-0.shadow.json.reason contains literal S, while the log event for the same error is redacted. On main the restored error is redacted. Fix: add shadowLenses.error to the diagnostics redacted on load, and cover this artifact with the single artifact boundary from the first finding.

findings.title: Owner diagnostics print restored terminal escapes to the terminal
findings.detail: recordOwnerDiagnostic redacts credentials but leaves terminal controls, and printOwnerDiagnostics writes the text to the owner's terminal unchanged (`limitless show` and `limitless logs`). Before this PR, restored state had escapes stripped on load, so the text built from it was clean. Reproduction (Codex): an ESC-bearing gate name, environment-blocked verification evidence quoting that name plus private holdout prose; interrupt after verification, mark the saved attempt as the completed retry, and resume. The new run-error owner diagnostic keeps the literal ESC[31m, and printOwnerDiagnostics prints it raw. Fix: apply redactGateOutput (credentials and terminal controls) when the diagnostic is recorded, and strip controls again when printing. Add a test with an ESC-bearing name that checks the printed text.

findings.title: Verifier citations are checked against the literal spec, not the sanitized text the verifier saw
findings.detail: Prompts are now redacted when sent, but citation validation still compares against the literal stored spec. Reproduction (Codex): register a synthetic credential S as a gate name, with the stored requirement 'Run S before delivery'. The resumed prompt shows 'Run [redacted] before delivery'. A verifier that cites exactly that sentence, also quoted in its evidence, gets 'citation is not a stated public requirement' and feedback claiming the citation was absent. On main the citation is accepted. Fix: validate textual citations against the same redacted view the verifier received (apply redactGateOutput to the source before citationInSource), while the stored state stays literal.

# Workers: pull-based gate workers (pairing, heartbeats, leased gate jobs)

Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput), the slice after the executor seam (#482). Matt decided on 2026-10-10 that other machines join as **discovered, as-available workers**, not as a fixed list. This slice builds the worker protocol and a `lan` gate executor on top of the seam. Discovery over Bonjour and availability rules follow in the next slice; here a worker is given the coordinator's URL.

Design reference: docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md §6.2 (executor interface), §3.5 (infrastructure failures).

## Shape
**Workers connect out to the coordinator, the way CI runners do.**
- A worker runs `limitless worker --coordinator https://<host>:<port>`.
- The coordinator never holds a list of machines. It knows only the workers that are paired and sending heartbeats right now.

## Change
1. **A worker listener on the coordinator, off by default.**
   - Configured with `[workers] listen = "<address>:<port>"`.
   - It serves only `/worker/*` routes, separate from the owner API and its port.
   - TLS uses a self-signed certificate generated at first start. Its key is stored as a private file: mode 0600 and read-denied in every agent sandbox, the same way as the API token (#484) and the credential stores (#487).
2. **Pairing.**
   - `limitless worker pair --coordinator <url>` sends the worker's name and its certificate fingerprint.
   - The coordinator records a pending request and shows a short code. The worker prints the same code.
   - The owner approves with `limitless workers approve <code>` (an authenticated owner route), or in the UI.
   - The coordinator then issues a per-worker token and stores only its hash. The worker stores the token and the coordinator's fingerprint, pinned.
   - `limitless workers revoke <name>` ends a worker's access at once.
   - The pairing route only ever creates a pending request. It's rate-limited and grants nothing until approved.
3. **Heartbeats, every 10 s, with the worker's token.** Each carries:
   - the release SHA, bun version, OS and version, CPU count and RAM;
   - free gate slots, whether the machine is on AC power, and idle seconds;
   - the jobs the worker holds.

   The coordinator keeps a `workers` table (additive migration) with each worker's last heartbeat and capabilities. A worker counts as available only while its heartbeats are fresh (30 s).
4. **Version lockstep.** A worker gets jobs only when its release SHA and bun version equal the coordinator's. Otherwise it shows as "needs update" and receives nothing.
5. **Gate jobs** (a `gate_jobs` table: request, state, worker, lease expiry, result).
   - The `lan` executor's `start` enqueues a job and returns `{ kind: "lan", id }`. `attach` waits for the job's result from the store, so a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.
   - Workers long-poll `POST /worker/lease` (up to 30 s). A job goes only to a matching, available worker that is asking for work at that moment.
   - Leases expire after 60 s unless renewed by heartbeats.
6. **The worker runs the job.**
   - It fetches `GET /worker/jobs/:id/bundle`, a git bundle of the head (and base) from the coordinator's repository cache, so the worker needs no GitHub credentials. It imports the bundle into its own repository cache through the hardened git wrapper.
   - It checks out exactly the requested head and records `git rev-parse HEAD`.
   - It runs the request's gate config through `runLocalGates`, with its own Seatbelt confinement, scratch and gate slots.
   - It posts check events as they finish, then the `GateRun` and the checked SHA.
   - The worker redacts output with its own registered credentials before sending. Its token and the coordinator's fingerprint are read-denied to its gates.
7. **The coordinator checks the result.**
   - The result is untrusted data. It's validated against the `GateRun` schema, its SHA must equal the requested head, and its checks must be the requested ones.
   - It's redacted again with the coordinator's credentials and private strings before anything stores or shows it.
   - A result that fails any check is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
8. **Infrastructure failures**:
   - no worker took the job within 60 s;
   - the lease expired;
   - the worker disconnected;
   - the result was invalid.

   These retry once on another available worker, then fall back to the local executor. They are logged as gate events, never sent to the implementer as feedback, and never turn a failing check into a pass. Cancelling the run cancels the job, and the worker stops it on its next heartbeat or lease reply.
9. **Selection.**
   - `[gates] executor = "lan"`, with `[workers] repos = ["owner/name"]` as a per-repository opt-in. Code goes to other machines only for listed repositories.
   - The prepare baseline and the run's gates use the same executor kind. The executor kind joins the baseline cache's environment hash.

## Tests (loopback only, temporary homes, no external network)
Run an in-process coordinator listener and a worker loop over loopback TLS, with certificates generated in temporary directories:
- **Pairing:**
  - an unapproved worker gets no token and no jobs;
  - approval issues a token;
  - revoking a worker refuses its next heartbeat.
- **A job end to end:** the worker leases it, runs real gate commands from a bundle and posts the result. The `GateRun` matches what the local executor gives for the same commit.
- **Restart:** a coordinator restart between `start` and the result re-attaches and doesn't enqueue again.
- **Infrastructure failures:**
  - a worker that stops heartbeating mid-job loses the lease;
  - the job retries once, then runs locally;
  - no implementer feedback is recorded.
- **Bad results:**
  - one whose SHA differs from the request is refused and treated as an infrastructure failure;
  - an extra check, or a check missing from the request, is refused the same way.
- **Version mismatch:** a mismatched worker gets no jobs.
- **Privacy:**
  - the worker's token and the coordinator's TLS key are unreadable from the gate sandbox (real-Seatbelt probes, `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`);
  - a credential printed by a gate reaches the coordinator redacted.

## Budget
About 450 source lines plus tests. If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop.

## Out of scope
- Bonjour discovery, availability rules (AC power, idle) and a Workers page in the UI: the next slice.
- Whole-run workers, workers that update themselves, and waking sleeping machines.
- Linux workers (they need their own confinement).
- Model logins on workers.


Closes #513

findings.title: A 40-bit pairing code built from a relay-chosen nonce can be matched offline
findings.detail: pairWorker derives its code from the nonce in the first reply, which a relay controls, and the code keeps only 40 bits (8 base32 characters). A relay learns the coordinator's code for its relayed request: it's in the reply, and it can also be computed from the public coordinator fingerprint, the forwarded worker fingerprint and the server nonce. The relay can then search substitute nonces offline until the worker's locally derived code matches, without any more coordinator requests. Reproduction (Codex): pairingCode runs at 1.73 million calls/s on one core in JS. With coordinator 'a'x64, relay 'b'x64, worker 'c'x64 and server nonce 'd'x64, the coordinator code was 6Z3ZW638. A search over substitute nonces found one giving 6Z3ZL7RH (first four characters equal) after 905,736 tries in 0.56 s. A full match is about 2^40 work: 7 days in JS on one core, about 18 minutes at 1e9 hashes/s, and less on a current GPU. That is within reach of the pairing window. Fix: compare a value of at least 80 bits. For example, derive 16 base32 characters with the same inputs, show them on both sides in groups of four, and accept the full value in `limitless workers approve`. Alternatively, use a commit/reveal exchange so neither side's contribution can be chosen after seeing the other's. Note that a public worker nonce alone doesn't prevent the adaptive choice. Add a test that the comparison value carries at least 80 bits, and keep the relay tests.

findings.title: A claim after a coordinator restart doesn't re-register the claim secret for redaction
findings.detail: The secret is registered only when pair() generates it, so a claim served by a restarted coordinator (a fresh process with the same database) leaves the incoming secret unregistered. Reproduction (Codex): create and approve a pairing in a file-backed database, start a fresh Bun process, reopen it and call claim(secret). The claim succeeds, but redactCredentials(secret) still returns the plaintext. The existing restart test recreates WorkerStore inside one process, so the global registry from the first process masks the gap. Fix: register a well-formed incoming claim secret in claim() before using it, and test it in a fresh process (or with the credential registry reset).

prompt:
# Change view reports: withhold private verifier evidence by structure, not phrase matching

## What's left after #514
`limitless_get_change` withholds holdout material from report pages by matching catalogue phrases line by line (`src/integrations/mcp-change.ts`). #514's review reproduced four gaps, each with a throwaway test, against both #514 (5222fde) and main (c949a34):

1. **Short private verifier prose that has no harvested literal stays visible when a report quotes it.** Example: evidence `red owl` on H-1, and a report line `Quoted: red owl`. Exposed on main and on #514.
2. **Overlapping quotations.** `matchAll` finds non-overlapping matches, so with private evidence `amber lantern` and `lantern glows ultraviolet`, the report `amber\nlantern\nglows ultraviolet` keeps `glows ultraviolet` visible. Exposed on main and on #514.
3. **A quotation wrapped mid-word,** for example `the amber lan\ntern glows`, still matches nothing. This predates #514.
4. **The opposite failure:** generic multi-word private-row evidence, such as `All checks passed.`, hides every ordinary report line that contains it. This errs on the safe side.

Phrase matching can't tell a quotation of private evidence from an ordinary line with the same words, so tuning thresholds trades 1 against 4.

## Change
Withhold by structure. The report is built by the factory (`src/pipeline/report.ts`) from run state, so render private verifier rows (non-public criteria: evidence, summaries and citations) into marked spans or sections. The change view then drops those spans whole, as it already drops `## Holdout scenarios`.

Keep phrase matching only as a backstop for free text the factory didn't render: verifier notes and model-written prose. Make the backstop's matcher cover overlapping and wrapped matches, including mid-word wraps.

## Acceptance
- Gaps 1–3 are withheld, and lines with gap 4's wording that aren't private-row renderings stay visible.
- Each of these has a test that fails on today's code.
- The existing #514 tests still pass.

Privacy: land only when every review finding is fixed.

Closes #516

findings.title: Replace the quotation-context gate with a per-author provenance rule; add no new patterns
findings.detail: Round 1 ran five fix-and-review loops. Each one tuned a quotation-context gate for short private matches ('Quoted: …'), and each review found a wrapper that defeats it: a bare link `[red owl](u)`, then an image `![red owl](u)`. Nothing was pushed, so the PR is still at 58efddc. Build round 2 from 58efddc. #516 is amended (see the issue's 2026-10-16 section). Keep the structural part: private verifier rows rendered as marked spans and dropped whole. Remove the quotation-context requirement entirely, and decide the prose backstop by who wrote the line. Text the verifier wrote (notes, and evidence on public criteria) is matched against every private verifier string and holdout scenario text. The implementer's report is matched against the private-row summaries the implementer actually received in verify feedback (`formatVerifyFeedback` gives it `publicSummary` after `redactHoldoutText`), and never against private-row evidence or citations it didn't see. Other prose gets harvested literals only. Before matching, normalize: decode HTML entities; unescape Markdown escapes; strip link and image syntax, emphasis, inline code, blockquote markers and table pipes while keeping label text; collapse whitespace across line breaks and join mid-word wraps; then scan every offset so overlapping matches are found. Match before any clipping, or clip only at line or span boundaries. Tests, each of which must fail at 58efddc: (a) the verifier's notes and its public-criterion evidence quote a private phrase plain, as a link, as an image, emphasised, as inline code, in a blockquote, in a table cell, entity-encoded, wrapped across lines, and wrapped mid-word, and every form is withheld; (b) the same forms in the implementer's report, for a private-row summary it received, are withheld; (c) two overlapping private phrases are both withheld; (d) gap 4's generic wording ('All checks passed.' as private-row evidence the implementer never received) stays visible in the implementer's report; (e) the same wording is withheld in the verifier's notes. Keep the existing #514 tests passing.

findings.title: Short private evidence quoted in a public row stays visible
findings.detail: Still open at 58efddc (round 1 pushed nothing). `factoryDetails` (used for factory-rendered text outside private spans) omits `shortProseDetails`. An unknown-row verifier evidence `red owl` quoted as AC-1 evidence `Quoted: red owl` stays visible in the rendered public acceptance row, on both backends. Public rows hold model-written evidence, so they need the short-quotation backstop too (issue gap 1). Public-row evidence is written by the verifier, so the provenance rule matches it against all private strings, with no quotation context.

findings.title: Report clipping cuts quotations so the backstop no longer matches
findings.detail: Still open at 58efddc (round 1 pushed nothing). The implementer summary is cut at 5000 characters and table cells at 300 (`escapeCell`) before the change view matches. With private evidence `the amber lantern glows ultraviolet`, a summary of 4979 filler characters, a newline and the evidence shows `the amber lantern gl`; longer private prose copied into public acceptance evidence shows its first 300 characters. Match clipped tails the way `privateMatches(..., truncated)` does, or withhold a clipped field that may end inside private text.

findings.title: Markdown escaping in rendered cells defeats matching
findings.detail: Still open at 58efddc (round 1 pushed nothing). `escapeCell` escapes `|`, while the change view's matcher works on the escaped text. # Invocation cleanup: freeze marked processes before killing them, and don't start an agent test after its invocation ends

## What happened (2026-10-14)
Two runs ended needs_human with `Invocation termination could not be confirmed: Marked processes still alive: …` (`src/util/proc.ts`, `stopMarkedProcesses`):
- **mv8hblqn0vwehk50p13jah (#533), 15:40.** The Codex implementer's own test built a nested-repository fixture with `submodule.recurse` and a git directory pointing back at the parent. Hundreds of processes were alive when the invocation ended. Load reached 311.
- **mv8gny3y0rh69tr00ql8za (#528's review round), 15:52.** The Claude implementer ran the full suite. It waited 808 s for the gate lane, so Claude's Bash tool moved the command to the background at its 600 s limit. The turn then ended with the suite still running, and about 40 marked processes outlived the cleanup.

`stopMarkedProcesses` signals each marked PID, SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after the grace period, and gives up after the grace period plus 10 s. A tree that keeps forking replaces processes as fast as they are signalled. Under heavy load, scanning and signalling hundreds of processes can also outlast 10 s. Failing closed is right: live writers must not overlap the next step. But the gap between "can't stop them" and "didn't stop them fast enough" costs a run.

## Change
1. **Freeze, then kill.** Each sweep sends SIGSTOP to every marked process it finds, so a stopped process can't fork, and rescans until no unstopped marked process remains. Then it sends SIGKILL to the whole set and confirms it is gone, keeping the PID-reuse checks. The deadline still bounds the whole stop. Refuse only when the frozen set still has live members at the deadline.
2. **Name the cause.** When confirmation still fails, the error names how many processes were alive and their command names, redacted. It should say whether the set kept growing, so "an agent's process tree kept forking" is distinguishable from "the machine was too slow".
3. **Slot waits and Claude's 600 s Bash limit.** A slotted command's wait counts toward Claude Code's per-command limit, so a long wait gets the command moved to the background and the turn ends with it running. Pick one fix, with a test:
   - the wrapper prints a waiting line, so the agent knows to wait instead of moving on; or
   - when an agent invocation ends, an agent test still waiting for a slot exits instead of starting.
   An agent test must never start after its invocation has ended.

## Acceptance
- A fake-harness test fails on today's code: an invocation leaves a process that keeps forking short-lived children. It is stopped within the deadline and the round continues.
- A test: a slotted command still waiting when its invocation ends never starts its command.
- Existing process-cleanup and PID-reuse tests still pass.

Related: #377 (cleanup retries), #150 (overload), #474 (agent test slotting). Budget: about 50 source lines, plus tests.


Closes #537

findings.title: An identity-inspection failure after SIGSTOP leaves the frozen process stopped forever
findings.detail: On any error, the catch block re-runs processBirth for each claimed member before its SIGKILL, inside `try { … } catch {}`. If that inspection throws as well (proc_pidinfo failing with an errno other than ESRCH, for example), the SIGKILL is silently skipped and the member stays in state T. That breaks the code's own rule, 'Never leave a frozen member behind'. Reproduction (Codex, temporary test with an owned /bin/sleep and real signal delivery): make darwinProcessBirth throw for that PID after its SIGSTOP. runProcess rejects, the recorded signals are only ['SIGSTOP'], and ps shows the sleeper in state T. Fix: never leave a member that this sweep froze in the stopped state. A process this sweep stopped can't exit by itself, so while it stays stopped its PID can't be reused. If its identity can't be re-confirmed after bounded retries, still SIGKILL the members this sweep froze, and report the inspection failure in the thrown error. Keep refusing to signal any PID this sweep never froze. Add a test with injected inspection failures (thrown after the freeze, and again in the error path) that ends with no stopped member and an error naming the failure.

findings.title: 'kept growing' is reported for ordinary discovery of an existing tree
findings.detail: `growing` becomes true as soon as any PID is claimed after the first populated scan, so a tree that existed before cleanup started, but was discovered over two scans, is reported as 'set kept growing'. Reproduction (Codex): start two sleepers before cleanup, expose one in the first injected snapshot and both afterwards, suppress their signals and advance the clock to the deadline. The error reports 2 processes and 'set kept growing', although neither forked. #537 asks for this to tell a forking tree apart from a slow machine. Fix: count growth from process birth times, using members born after the cleanup started (processBirth already returns the start time), instead of from discovery order. Add that case as a test.

head: 0f6d39e5884ed2f6c9c762db22bfc715e49b74ee
prompt:
# Deploy and gate-slot: a busy slot past the 30-minute wait runs the suite unslotted beside factory gates

## What happened (2026-10-15)
- #550's deploy (`limitless deploy --smoke`, which runs its checks inside `withGateLease("deploy", …)` in `src/cli/service.ts`) started waiting for the gate slot at 21:05. At 21:35 the wait hit its 30-minute budget (`maxWaitMs` defaults to 1,800,000 in `src/cli/gate-slot.ts`). `withGateLease` printed `warning: gate-slot coordination unavailable: Error: gate-slot wait passed the acquisition deadline` and ran lint, typecheck and the full suite anyway. That ran from about 21:35 to 21:57, beside the gate that held the slot.
- Two factory gates were running in that window:
  - **#537's regression retry failed again at 21:46** on `change view preserves PR text …`, which timed out at 5037 ms. A retry that fails again counts as a confirmed regression, so the run went back to its implementer for a load timeout.
  - **#545 round 1's test check took 1718 s and failed with 17 timeouts.** They include the baseline-cache, factory-merge-interruption and isolated-push land tests at their 25–30 s limits. Its implementer gets that output as feedback.
- Land 68 (#539) failed later, from 22:16 to 22:39, on 3 timeouts. It did not overlap the deploy, so it is not part of this issue.

## Why
After the wait budget runs out, `withGateLease` treats "the slot is still busy" like "the daemon is unreachable". In both cases it runs the work without the slot. For an unreachable daemon, that is the existing degraded mode, and it's announced. For a healthy daemon with a long queue, it defeats the slot: a second full suite (about 18 minutes here) runs on a machine sized for one, and other runs' gates time out into false regressions. `limitless gate-slot`, which `scripts/land-pr.sh` uses, takes the same path.

## Change
- While the daemon is reachable and answering lease requests, a busy slot never turns into an unslotted run. Keep waiting until the slot is acquired, and print the holder and the elapsed wait every few minutes, so a long wait is visible in the deploy output. Apply this to both `limitless deploy` and `limitless gate-slot`, through the one `withGateLease` path.
- The wait budget still bounds the unreachable-daemon case, which keeps today's fallback and warning.
- The agent-test lanes (#483, #537) keep their current rules.

## Tests (fake lease client and clock, no real daemon)
- A slot that stays busy past `maxWaitMs`, with the daemon answering, doesn't start the work until the slot is acquired. No "coordination unavailable" warning is printed, and progress lines name the holder. This test fails on main today.
- An unreachable daemon still falls back with the warning, as today.
- The agent-test lane behaviour is unchanged (existing tests).

## Out of scope
The number of gate slots, and the timeouts of individual load-sensitive tests.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.


Closes #554

findings.title: An expired reservation still runs the work unslotted while the daemon is answering
findings.detail: When a reply says the queued reservation expired (`{acquired:false, expired:true}`, which happens after a daemon restart, for example), the ordinary path throws 'gate-slot lease expired'. The outer catch then warns and runs `work()` unslotted, which is the case #554 forbids, because the daemon is clearly reachable. Reproduction (Codex, fake client and clock): reply `{id:'q', acquired:false}`, advance 250 ms, then reply `{id:'q', acquired:false, expired:true}`. With maxWaitMs 60000 the work runs unslotted with the warning. With maxWaitMs 0 the expiry check is skipped and the caller polls 'q' forever, even after capacity is free, which is a regression from main. Fix: for ordinary callers, treat an expired reservation as 'request a new reservation' (clear the id and keep waiting under the same responsive rule). Agent-test lanes keep their LeaseRejected. Add tests for both maxWait values.

findings.title: Progress lines always say 'unknown holder' because ordinary lease replies carry no holder
findings.detail: The ordinary `/api/admin/gate-slot` reply never includes `holder`, so `limitless deploy` and `limitless gate-slot` print 'holder: unknown holder' every 3 minutes, although the semaphore knows who holds the slot. #554 asks for the holder in the progress lines. Reproduction (Codex): occupy the semaphore as 'pipeline visible-holder', use a fake client with the endpoint's real reply shape, and advance the clock. Both the 180 s and 360 s lines say 'unknown holder'. The new test hides this by injecting `holder` into the fake reply. Fix: include the current holder (redacted) in ordinary busy replies on the daemon side, and test through the real reply shape.

findings.title: The growth diagnostic's clock can fail cleanup and is read on every child exit
findings.detail: bornAt = birthClock() runs before discovery on every child exit, including invocations with nothing left to claim. On Linux that reads /proc/self/auxv and /proc/uptime each time, and if either is unreadable or AT_CLKTCK is missing it throws. stopMarkedProcesses then fails before any scan: runProcess rejects with ProcessTerminationError and the scope latches the error, so later commands are refused. Reproduction (Codex): a Linux-backend fixture with valid ancestry and empty discovery but auxv or uptime unavailable; `exit 0` rejected, and with readable fixtures it succeeded. A diagnostic must not decide whether cleanup succeeds ('Fail closed, precisely'). Fix: read the clock only when a member is first claimed. If it can't be read, report growth as unknown and keep cleaning up. Add a test with the clock failing and nothing to claim, and one with a member to claim.

findings.title: Growth comparison ignores the clocks' precision
findings.detail: On macOS the cleanup clock is Date.now() * 1000 (millisecond precision), while process birth is in microseconds, so a member born earlier in the same millisecond compares as newer. Reproduction (Codex): an owned sleep spawned before sampling had birth 1792169203:23704 against a cleanup clock of 1792169203023000. On Linux, /proc/uptime (10.03) times 100 Hz gives 1002.9999999999999, so starttime 1003 from the same tick counts as growth. Fix: compare conservatively at the coarser precision (macOS: birth > clock + 1000 µs; Linux: birth > floor(uptime * hz) + 1 tick, computed in integers). Add both boundary cases to the growth test.each.

head: 67d65e5b9cb88535929f30547c9969138f25b32b
prompt:
# Workers: leased gate jobs, the lan executor and the worker loop (#513 slice 2)

The second slice of #513, split out of PR #546 per #513's budget rule ("If it runs over, split the work into two PRs: the listener, pairing, heartbeats and CLI first, then gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop").

## Scope
Gate jobs, the `lan` gate executor and the worker loop, on top of the first slice (#546: listener, pairing, heartbeats, CLI). The design is #513's. Its acceptance items about leased gate jobs, the `lan` executor and the worker loop move here.

PR #546 at 8562b3d1704bfc0d4746516b254f9e832f8c2ca0 already holds a draft implementation, which this slice can start from:
- `src/gates/lan.ts`;
- the `src/gates/executor.ts`, `src/gates/cache.ts`, `src/pipeline/gate-execution.ts` and `src/pipeline/engine.ts` changes;
- `src/workers/client.ts`;
- their tests in `test/workers.test.ts` and `test/gate-executor.test.ts`.

Budget: about 450 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: as in #513.


The draft commit is in the factory repository cache: read its files with `git show 8562b3d1704bfc0d4746516b254f9e832f8c2ca0:<path>` (start from them, then fit them to what landed in #546 on main).

## #513, the design this slice completes (slice 1 landed as #546)

The budget and scope above are this slice's; #513's text below is the design and acceptance reference. Its items about the listener, pairing, heartbeats and the CLI are already on main.


Part of #165 (M6.2 Throughput), the slice after the executor seam (#482). Matt decided on 2026-10-10 that other machines join as **discovered, as-available workers**, not as a fixed list. This slice builds the worker protocol and a `lan` gate executor on top of the seam. Discovery over Bonjour and availability rules follow in the next slice; here a worker is given the coordinator's URL.

Design reference: docs/research/13-cloud-workers.md §6.2 (executor interface), §3.5 (infrastructure failures).

## Shape
**Workers connect out to the coordinator, the way CI runners do.**
- A worker runs `limitless worker --coordinator https://<host>:<port>`.
- The coordinator never holds a list of machines. It knows only the workers that are paired and sending heartbeats right now.

## Change
1. **A worker listener on the coordinator, off by default.**
   - Configured with `[workers] listen = "<address>:<port>"`.
   - It serves only `/worker/*` routes, separate from the owner API and its port.
   - TLS uses a self-signed certificate generated at first start. Its key is stored as a private file: mode 0600 and read-denied in every agent sandbox, the same way as the API token (#484) and the credential stores (#487).
2. **Pairing.**
   - `limitless worker pair --coordinator <url>` sends the worker's name and its certificate fingerprint.
   - The coordinator records a pending request and shows a short code. The worker prints the same code.
   - The owner approves with `limitless workers approve <code>` (an authenticated owner route), or in the UI.
   - The coordinator then issues a per-worker token and stores only its hash. The worker stores the token and the coordinator's fingerprint, pinned.
   - `limitless workers revoke <name>` ends a worker's access at once.
   - The pairing route only ever creates a pending request. It's rate-limited and grants nothing until approved.
3. **Heartbeats, every 10 s, with the worker's token.** Each carries:
   - the release SHA, bun version, OS and version, CPU count and RAM;
   - free gate slots, whether the machine is on AC power, and idle seconds;
   - the jobs the worker holds.

   The coordinator keeps a `workers` table (additive migration) with each worker's last heartbeat and capabilities. A worker counts as available only while its heartbeats are fresh (30 s).
4. **Version lockstep.** A worker gets jobs only when its release SHA and bun version equal the coordinator's. Otherwise it shows as "needs update" and receives nothing.
5. **Gate jobs** (a `gate_jobs` table: request, state, worker, lease expiry, result).
   - The `lan` executor's `start` enqueues a job and returns `{ kind: "lan", id }`. `attach` waits for the job's result from the store, so a coordinator restart re-attaches without enqueueing again.
   - Workers long-poll `POST /worker/lease` (up to 30 s). A job goes only to a matching, available worker that is asking for work at that moment.
   - Leases expire after 60 s unless renewed by heartbeats.
6. **The worker runs the job.**
   - It fetches `GET /worker/jobs/:id/bundle`, a git bundle of the head (and base) from the coordinator's repository cache, so the worker needs no GitHub credentials. It imports the bundle into its own repository cache through the hardened git wrapper.
   - It checks out exactly the requested head and records `git rev-parse HEAD`.
   - It runs the request's gate config through `runLocalGates`, with its own Seatbelt confinement, scratch and gate slots.
   - It posts check events as they finish, then the `GateRun` and the checked SHA.
   - The worker redacts output with its own registered credentials before sending. Its token and the coordinator's fingerprint are read-denied to its gates.
7. **The coordinator checks the result.**
   - The result is untrusted data. It's validated against the `GateRun` schema, its SHA must equal the requested head, and its checks must be the requested ones.
   - It's redacted again with the coordinator's credentials and private strings before anything stores or shows it.
   - A result that fails any check is an infrastructure failure, never a pass.
8. **Infrastructure failures**:
   - no worker took the job within 60 s;
   - the lease expired;
   - the worker disconnected;
   - the result was invalid.

   These retry once on another available worker, then fall back to the local executor. They are logged as gate events, never sent to the implementer as feedback, and never turn a failing check into a pass. Cancelling the run cancels the job, and the worker stops it on its next heartbeat or lease reply.
9. **Selection.**
   - `[gates] executor = "lan"`, with `[workers] repos = ["owner/name"]` as a per-repository opt-in. Code goes to other machines only for listed repositories.
   - The prepare baseline and the run's gates use the same executor kind. The executor kind joins the baseline cache's environment hash.

## Tests (loopback only, temporary homes, no external network)
Run an in-process coordinator listener and a worker loop over loopback TLS, with certificates generated in temporary directories:
- **Pairing:**
  - an unapproved worker gets no token and no jobs;
  - approval issues a token;
  - revoking a worker refuses its next heartbeat.
- **A job end to end:** the worker leases it, runs real gate commands from a bundle and posts the result. The `GateRun` matches what the local executor gives for the same commit.
- **Restart:** a coordinator restart between `start` and the result re-attaches and doesn't enqueue again.
- **Infrastructure failures:**
  - a worker that stops heartbeating mid-job loses the lease;
  - the job retries once, then runs locally;
  - no implementer feedback is recorded.
- **Bad results:**
  - one whose SHA differs from the request is refused and treated as an infrastructure failure;
  - an extra check, or a check missing from the request, is refused the same way.
- **Version mismatch:** a mismatched worker gets no jobs.
- **Privacy:**
  - the worker's token and the coordinator's TLS key are unreadable from the gate sandbox (real-Seatbelt probes, `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)`);
  - a credential printed by a gate reaches the coordinator redacted.

## Budget
#513's budget was split; this slice's is about 450 source lines plus tests.

## Out of scope
- Bonjour discovery, availability rules (AC power, idle) and a Workers page in the UI: the next slice.
- Whole-run workers, workers that update themselves, and waking sleeping machines.
- Linux workers (they need their own confinement).
- Model logins on workers.



Closes #547

findings.title: Leased requests send credential-bearing gate commands to the worker
findings.detail: The lease reply sends the full GateRequest; it removes only cwd. Reproduction (Codex): register a synthetic coordinator credential, use it in a requested setup command, and lease the job over the loopback listener. The 200 reply contains the credential verbatim. Commands are executable, so redacting them would break the gate. Fix: when any executable input (setup or check commands, names, retry_files) contains a registered credential (canonicalize as redactGateOutput does), don't offer the job to workers. Run it locally and record a status event saying why. Test both cases.

findings.title: One attempt can stay leased forever while its requests retry
findings.detail: `call` retries 5xx and transport errors without limit while heartbeats keep renewing the lease. Reproduction (Codex): persistent 503s for the bundle download with real loopback heartbeats, and the coordinator clock advanced 20 s per heartbeat. After 800 s the job is still leased at attempt 1, so it never gets another worker or the local fallback. Fix (Every pending state ends): give each job one deadline (for example the gate timeout plus setup and transfer margin). The worker posts a failure when it passes, and the coordinator stops renewing a lease past it and moves the job on. One deadline, not a second retry layer. Test with the 503 reproduction.

findings.title: A gate that leaves an unreadable directory stops the worker loop
findings.detail: Reproduction (Codex): a bundled check `mkdir locked; touch locked/file; chmod 000 locked` with the injected confinement backend. The result completes, then worker cleanup fails: the worktree removal error is swallowed, the recursive removal throws on the unreadable directory, and the worker task rejects, leaving the checkout behind. Untrusted gate output must not be able to stop a worker. Fix: remove the checkout the way the factory cleans up local run worktrees after gates, restoring permissions within the checkout only, and report a cleanup failure without ending the loop. Add the reproduction as a test.

findings.title: Each lease poll sweeps every job once per held job
findings.detail: Every holds() call runs a full sweep, and the long-poll repeats the loop every 100 ms. Reproduction (Codex): 128 held leases cost 16,772 SQLite queries (about 80–93 ms) per iteration. Fix: sweep once per iteration and check ownership of the held IDs in one query. Keep the behaviour the same.

findings.title: Worker caches keep every job's temporary bundle refs
findings.detail: The worker fetches `+refs/limitless-bundles/*:refs/limitless-bundles/*` and never deletes them, so they accumulate and pin old job commits against garbage collection. Reproduction (Codex): after three jobs, all three job refs remain in the worker cache, while the coordinator removed its own. Fix: delete the job's imported refs once the checkout exists, and on failure paths too. Test that none remain after success and after a failure.

findings.title: Results may reorder the requested checks
findings.detail: validRun checks membership, uniqueness and count, but not position. Reproduction (Codex): checks requested as [pass, fail] are accepted and stored as [fail, pass]. Fix: compare each returned check with the requested check at the same index, as validRun already does for setup.
