Closes #585

findings.title: The push guard still runs before the retried push, not at it
findings.detail: pushExistingBranch calls guard() once and then hands the push to remoteSh, which goes through withGitHubRetry (src/git/repos.ts ~115): after a transient failure it pauses for seconds and runs the push again without consulting the guard, and cacheGit also awaits before it spawns (src/git/command.ts ~140). A reclaim during that pause still lets the stale worker push. Call the guard inside the retried operation, synchronously immediately before each push attempt spawns (the merge path already does this on every retry), so a lost claim stops every attempt. Add a test where the first push fails transiently, the entry is reclaimed during the retry delay, and no second push runs. The existing test at test/land-queue.test.ts ~2923 reclaims inside the guard itself, so it doesn't cover this.

findings.title: Per-attempt checkouts leak the base export after a crash
findings.detail: Checks export the base commit to `${cwd}-base`, i.e. land-<id>-<attempt>-base. Before this change every attempt reused land-<id>-base, so the next attempt's rmSync removed a crashed attempt's export; now each attempt has a new path, and the stale-checkout sweep in checkout() only matches a numeric attempt suffix, so land-<id>-<n>-base (and a legacy land-<id>-base) are never removed after a daemon restart during checks. Remove abandoned base exports for earlier attempts (and the legacy name) in the same sweep, as plain directories, not worktrees. Add a test that leaves a stale base export from an earlier attempt and asserts the next attempt removes it.

head: 3371f5a49843a99c8cf7d19f1293afb7da7776c5
prompt:
Delivery: a resumed run whose base advanced twice is refused after a valid second factory merge

## What's wrong
Delivery refuses a resumed run whose base advanced twice. Found while vetting #467 for the fresh review clean set (#542). Both adjudicators reproduced it independently at #467's head (261559d), and it passed at its base (1aa4f2b). Main has the same check today (`src/pipeline/engine.ts` `assertDeliveryHead`, `src/git/merge.ts` `validateMerge`), but it has not been reproduced on main yet.

1. Delivery makes a clean factory merge M of the reviewed commit R and base F1, persists it, and stops before pushing (a deploy restart, for example).
2. On resume the base has moved to F2. Delivery merges again, giving M2 with parents [M, F2], and the post-merge gates pass.
3. `assertDeliveryHead` then calls `validateMerge(worktree, reviewedSha = R, F2)`, which requires HEAD's parents to be exactly [R, F2]. M2's first parent is M, so the run ends needs_human with "Delivery refused: expected checked SHA R, actual HEAD M2".

The guard fails closed, so nothing unsafe is delivered. But a run that the restart rules say must resume ends up needing a human.

## Change
Accept a chain of factory merges whose first-parent path leads back to the reviewed SHA. Each merge must be one the factory recorded and validated (exactly one base parent each), and the last one must have passed post-merge gates. Anything else stays refused. Keep "Act on the exact commit you checked": the accepted HEAD is the newest validated and gated merge, pinned when pushing.

## Tests
- Reproduce on main first: kill after the clean merge is persisted and before the push, advance the base again, then resume. Today that ends needs_human; after the fix it delivers M2.
- A HEAD whose first-parent chain includes an unrecorded commit, or a merge with an extra parent, is still refused.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.

Closes #559

findings.title: A completed pending merge with MERGE_HEAD still present now passes the delivery guard
findings.detail: For the current head with pendingRebaseSha set, assertDeliveryHead now calls validateMerge with the commit SHA instead of "HEAD", which skips the "Completed merge still has MERGE_HEAD" check in src/git/merge.ts. The old code ran that check for pending merges. Concrete state: a crash leaves the pending merge M=[R,F1] committed (HEAD=M, HEAD !== preRebaseHead) with MERGE_HEAD still present. The guard now accepts it; mergeForDelivery → prepareMerge then fails on the same condition with a generic Error, and because that error is not a DeliveryHeadError the failure path publishes a verified-work draft (deliverVerifiedDraft) where the guard previously suppressed publication entirely. Skip the MERGE_HEAD check only where it is legitimately expected: a historical link in the chain, or a current HEAD that equals preRebaseHead while the pending merge (MERGE_HEAD = pendingRebaseSha) is still uncommitted. A current HEAD that is itself the completed pending merge must be validated as "HEAD" with the MERGE_HEAD check, and that failure must stay a DeliveryHeadError. Add a test for this state that asserts the run ends with the delivery refusal and publishes nothing (no push, no draft PR); keep the existing "merge still in progress" resume test passing.

head: d5954c930155a1d2b20453d57139074426afbb67
prompt:
Land queue: accept a pull request that no factory run opened

## Why
`LandQueue.request` (src/land/queue.ts) resolves its target to a factory run and throws "run not found" for any other pull request. A PR that a person or a hand-run session opened can only land through `scripts/land-pr.sh` or a direct merge. Both run the checks outside the gate sandbox, so a failure that appears only inside it reaches main unnoticed.

On 2026-10-18, #599 (a hand-run session's PR) was merged directly. Its new test assertion passed in CI and in local runs but failed in every confined land check: the gate environment sets `credential.helper` through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`. Every land and factory post-merge gate failed until #600 fixed the test.

## Change
- `limitless land <pr> --sha <full sha>` accepts an open PR on a configured GitHub repository that no factory run opened. The same approval rule applies: the exact head SHA is pinned, and the land stops if the head moves.
- Such a land goes through the same steps as a factory land: merge the current base, run the base commit's `.limitless.toml` checks confined, wait for CI on the resulting head, squash-merge exactly that head, and run the private-text publication checks.
- `land list`, the UI and the feed show these entries like any other; the entry records that no run owns it.

## Tests
- A land requested for a PR with no factory run is queued, checked confined, and merged at the pinned head.
- A head that moves after approval stops it, as for factory PRs.
- A PR on a repository that isn't configured, or one that is closed, is refused with a clear reason.
- Restarting the daemon mid-land resumes the entry without a run.

## Out of scope
- Changing `scripts/land-pr.sh`.
- Review rounds for hand-made PRs.

## Budget
About 100 source lines plus tests. Land entries reference a run today, so this probably needs an additive migration to allow an entry without one. Keep it compatible with the previous release.

Closes #604

findings.title: The digest drops blocked lands of PRs that no run owns
findings.detail: The digest deletes every feed item without a runId before resolving current state (`if (!item.runId) { group.items.delete(key); continue; }`). Lands of unowned PRs now produce land.* feed items with runId null, so a conflict or a failed check on such a land leaves actionable work while the digest reports "Blocked lands: 0". The issue requires these entries to show like any other. For land items without a run, resolve the current state from the land records by PR URL (the newest entry for that PR; actionable while it is still blocked and the PR isn't merged or closed) instead of requiring a Run, and keep run-backed items unchanged. Add a digest test: a blocked unowned land is listed under Blocked lands, and the same PR after a later successful land is not.

head: 65dad1a633b0eef13c1a7c383795b339270e48ce
prompt:
Invocation cleanup: a daemon crash mid-cleanup leaves descendants that a resumed run never recovers

## What's wrong
If the daemon dies while it is cleaning up an invocation's marked processes, nothing recovers the processes that cleanup hadn't finished with. A resumed run doesn't notice them.

Found while reviewing #561 (#537), which changes the cleanup to freeze and then kill. Reproduction (Codex, temporary test): a real runProcess invocation left a sleeper behind. Inspection was paused after the sweep's SIGSTOP, and the owned supervisor was then killed. A fresh runProcess in the same directory returned exit code 0, while the previous sleeper stayed in state T.

This predates #561. Before it, the same crash left the processes running, which is worse: they could keep writing to the checkout. With #561 they are stopped, but they are still never cleaned up. The claimed set and its birth identities live only in memory.

## Change
Before signalling any process, persist the cleanup's ownership record: the run, the invocation, the claimed PIDs and their birth identities. When a run resumes, or the daemon starts, finish any recorded cleanup. Kill a recorded member only if its birth identity still matches, and refuse with a clear reason if confirmation fails, as cleanup already does. A resumed invocation must not start in a checkout whose previous cleanup is unresolved.

## Tests
- Kill the cleanup process between freeze and kill, then resume. The stopped member is killed, identity-checked, before the next step runs.
- A recorded PID whose identity changed (reused) is never signalled.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #562

findings.title: A cleanup error can now leave the live direct child running
findings.detail: On a cleanup error, terminate used to SIGKILL the directly spawned child unconditionally ("ours even if process discovery is unavailable"). With a cleanup scope it now first reads the child's birth and records it, and skips child.kill() when that read throws or returns null, or when an earlier ownership write failed. On darwin processBirth throws "Native process inspection is unavailable" without the native module, which is exactly the discovery failure the old comment covered, so the child keeps running (and can keep writing to the checkout); a failed first write also leaves no recovery row. The live direct child (exitCode and signalCode both null) can't have a reused PID, so it must always be killed: record it first when its identity can be read, but never let a failed read or write prevent the kill, and keep that failure in the termination error. Better still, capture and persist the direct child's identity right after spawn so it is recorded before any cleanup starts. Change the new test that currently asserts the child survives so it asserts the child is killed.

findings.title: On Linux a record from before a reboot can match and SIGKILL an unrelated process
findings.detail: Linux processBirth returns only the boot-relative start time in clock ticks (/proc/<pid>/stat field 22). process_cleanups rows survive a reboot (and a rollback followed by a later upgrade), and after a reboot PIDs and start ticks repeat, so an unrelated process with the same PID and start tick passes the identity check and gets SIGKILL. That breaks "never signal a process you did not start". Persist the boot identity with each record (Linux /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; on macOS the birth is absolute, but recording kern.boottime keeps one rule) and retire records from another boot without signalling. The table is new in this PR, so change it in place. Add a test where a record from another boot matches a live process's PID and birth and is never signalled.

findings.title: Recovery waits on zombies and kills one member at a time
findings.detail: Recovery SIGKILLs one recorded member, then polls processBirth until it changes, for up to 10 s, before touching the next member. On Linux processBirth still returns the start time for a zombie (/proc/<pid>/stat exists), so a killed member whose parent is another recorded member that is still SIGSTOPped (frozen by the interrupted sweep, not yet killed) stays a zombie: recovery times out with "Recorded process still alive", stops, and leaves the frozen parent and its rows behind. Live cleanup already treats zombie state as gone (stillRunning). SIGKILL every confirmed member of the invocation first, then wait for all of them under one deadline, using the same zombie-aware liveness check as live cleanup. Add a Linux-path test with a stopped recorded parent and a recorded child where the child's row comes first.

findings.title: Matching records by command directory blocks unrelated runs
findings.detail: recoverProcessCleanups selects other runs' records whenever r.cwd equals the new command's directory. Several commands run from shared factory directories rather than a run's checkout, for example GitHub clones from paths.repos (src/git/repos.ts ~259). An unresolved cleanup recorded there by run A makes run B wait on it, and an inspection or signalling failure then sets B's terminationError for good. Only a run's own records, plus records whose directory is inside the run's own checkout (its worktreePath), should gate its commands; shared factory directories must not link runs. Add a test where another run's unresolved record in a shared directory doesn't block or fail this run.

findings.title: Startup recovery runs before the daemon reports healthy
findings.detail: startDaemon recovers every pending record sequentially before HTTP starts, at up to 10 s per stubborn member, and the deploy's health wait allows about 45 s, so a handful of unresolved cleanups from failed or cancelled runs can make a deploy roll back even though each run is already guarded (executeRun and runProcess recover before that run's next command). Don't block startup or the health endpoint on this recovery: start it after HTTP is up (or in the background), keeping the per-run barriers as they are.

head: cc78b8a68a388b04934d309330363a66910cf765
prompt:
Land queue: a draft PR runs the full check, then fails with an unexplained 'merge failed'

## What happened (2026-10-16)
The land queue accepted #546 while it was still a draft. Its needs_human round deliveries had left it a draft, titled "[needs human] …".

Land 74 ran the full check (20 minutes, all passing) and waited for GitHub CI, which passed. Then it blocked with `merge failed`, because `gh pr merge` refuses a draft. Nothing in the land entry, the log or the feed said why. The reason was found by hand.

## Why
- `src/land/queue.ts` `merge()` calls `mergePullRequest` (`src/git/repos.ts`). That function turns any non-transient `gh pr merge` error into the bare outcome `"failed"`, and the queue records it as `merge failed` with no detail.
- Nothing checks the PR's draft state before the expensive checks start.

## Change
1. **Check the PR's state before the land checks.** Look for a draft, a closed PR, or a missing head. For an approved draft, either mark it ready (the approval is explicit) or refuse at once with `PR is a draft`; pick one and document it. Keep the existing head-SHA pinning.
2. **Carry the reason on every merge failure.** When `gh pr merge` fails, record its error text in the land entry's reason and the `land.blocked` feed item, redacted with `redactCredentials` and truncated after redaction. The private-text and head-moved refusals need distinct reasons too.

## Tests (fake gh)
- An approved draft PR is handled before any check runs, by being marked ready or refused per the decision. Today it runs the checks and ends `merge failed`.
- A non-transient `gh pr merge` error appears, redacted, in the blocked reason.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.

Closes #566

findings.title: A transient GitHub failure in the new preflight blocks the land
findings.detail: The preflight `gh pr view` goes through runGh, which has no retry, and any failure becomes LandBlocked("cannot inspect current GitHub PR metadata: …"). A single 502 or timeout therefore ends a land that previously would have proceeded (there was no call at this point before), and it stays blocked until someone requeues it. The merge itself uses withGitHubRetry (src/git/repos.ts). Run the preflight lookup through the same bounded, abortable retry (one retry layer, transient errors only, the claim re-checked after the await as now); keep refusing at once on a permanent error or a response that fails validation, and on exhausted retries block with a reason that says GitHub was unavailable. Add a test where the first preflight lookup fails transiently and the land proceeds, and one where a permanent error still blocks before any check runs.

findings.title: The draft decision isn't documented
findings.detail: The issue asks to pick one behavior for an approved draft and document it. The PR refuses with "PR is a draft" (approval doesn't mark it ready), but neither the landing docs nor the `limitless land` help say so. Add one sentence where landing is documented (docs/GUIDE.md or docs/OPERATIONS.md, wherever `limitless land` is described) and in the CLI usage text if it lists refusals: a draft is refused before any check runs; mark it ready (`gh pr ready`) and request the land again.

head: 4b864374e98d8ca948120263b5e287baaa1ddfe5
prompt:
Delivery: a pending merge with the wrong MERGE_HEAD target publishes a draft instead of refusing

## What's wrong
When delivery resumes a pending clean merge whose HEAD is still the pre-merge head but whose `MERGE_HEAD` points somewhere other than the recorded pending base (`pendingRebaseSha`), `prepareMerge` (src/git/merge.ts) fails with a generic error. Because that error is not a `DeliveryHeadError`, the failure path takes the verified-work fallback (`deliverVerifiedDraft`, src/pipeline/engine.ts) and pushes the verified SHA as a draft PR, instead of ending with a delivery refusal that publishes nothing.

This predates #621: on main, `assertDeliveryHead` returns early when HEAD equals the reviewed SHA, so the single-merge case reaches the same generic error. #621 extends the same path to a pending second merge. Found while verifying #621 (Codex review).

What gets published is the verified commit, so nothing unchecked reaches GitHub, but an inconsistent merge state in the worktree should stop delivery, not turn into a publication.

## Change
In the delivery guard, when a pending merge is still uncommitted (HEAD equals `preRebaseHead`) and `MERGE_HEAD` exists, require `MERGE_HEAD` to equal `pendingRebaseSha`; anything else is a `DeliveryHeadError`. Keep `prepareMerge`'s own check as is.

## Tests
- Pending merge, HEAD at the pre-merge head, `MERGE_HEAD` at another commit: the run ends with the delivery refusal, with no push and no draft PR (single-merge and second-merge cases).
- Matching `MERGE_HEAD`: the merge resumes as today.

## Budget
About 10 source lines plus tests.

Closes #626

findings.title: The MERGE_HEAD check reads only the first entry and treats a failed read as no merge
findings.detail: The guard uses `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` with allowFail. Two inconsistent states still pass it and then fail generically in prepareMerge/validateMerge, which takes the verified-draft fallback this issue removes: (1) MERGE_HEAD with pendingRebaseSha on the first line and another commit on a second line: rev-parse returns the first, the guard passes, and git would commit an octopus merge with both; (2) a MERGE_HEAD whose content isn't a full object id (abbreviated, garbage): rev-parse fails, stdout is empty, and the guard treats it as no merge in progress. Read MERGE_HEAD's contents through the hardened wrapper (`git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD`, then read the file): only a confirmed absence (the file doesn't exist) passes; otherwise require exactly one line equal to the full pendingRebaseSha; any other content or a failed read is a DeliveryHeadError. Add tests for a two-line MERGE_HEAD and an abbreviated one: both end with the delivery refusal and publish nothing.

head: 254dac4df3097d3d0435301ad6b32f1bada1c21e
prompt:
Implement: a stuck implementer's background process makes cleanup fail the run

Seen 2026-10-04 on run muuofmq0mqbx (#353). The Codex implementer started the full test suite in the background, writing to `node_modules/.ci-check-final.log`, then polled that log until the stuck detector stopped it ("repeated the same shell call 6 times"). The background test process kept running. The worktree cleanup that follows (`git … clean -ffdxq`) then failed with `warning: could not lstat node_modules/…` (files changing under it), and the whole run failed instead of moving to the next implement round.

Fix:
1. When an agent invocation ends (normally, stuck, or cancelled), kill its whole process tree before any worktree cleanup. Background children must not outlive the invocation.
2. Treat a cleanup failure after a stuck/failed implement round as a round failure (retry the round, or escalate), not a run failure; retry the clean once after the kill.

Acceptance (fake harness): an implementer that spawns a long-running background writer and then stalls is stopped; its child is gone before cleanup; the run proceeds to the next round. A `git clean` that fails once is retried.

Small: about 40 lines plus tests.

Closes #377

findings.title: The change misses the issue's remaining gap and adds an unrequested process mechanism
findings.detail: Issue #377 was narrowed on 2026-10-14 (status comment on the issue): every invocation's descendants are already stopped before cleanup (#392), and `git clean` is already retried once and turned into round feedback. The one remaining gap is the gate-timeout re-run in src/pipeline/engine.ts (around line 1284), which calls `checkoutCommitted(cwd)` without the clean retry, so a still-running background writer there fails the run. This PR doesn't touch that path. Instead it adds a new invocation-level tracker (withInvocationProcesses in src/util/proc.ts, wired into RunContext.invoke in src/pipeline/context.ts) that aborts and awaits unawaited runProcess commands; nobody asked for it, it duplicates what #392 covers, and it rewrites runProcess, which another open PR (#624) is changing heavily. Remove the proc.ts and context.ts changes and their tests, and implement the narrowed fix: give the gate-timeout re-run's checkoutCommitted the same clean retry the initial gate checkout uses (`checkoutCommitted(cwd, undefined, Boolean(ctx.state.implementerIssue))` or the equivalent), with failure handled the same way as there. Add a test where the re-run's first `git clean` fails once (a writer still changing files) and the re-run proceeds, and one where it keeps failing and is handled like the initial checkout's failure. Keep to the issue's budget (a few source lines plus tests).

head: 4191304423590b0facf08702314a1199f1a1e35d
prompt:
Workers: update to the coordinator's release after a deploy

## What's wrong
A LAN worker reports the release it started on, and the coordinator marks it `needs update` whenever that differs from its own (`src/db/workers.ts`: `releaseSha` or `bunVersion` not equal). After every deploy both workers sit idle until someone updates each checkout and restarts the worker by hand in its terminal. On 2026-10-19 that kept all gate work on the coordinator's single local slot overnight, and review rounds waited up to two hours in prepare. Each deploy has to be batched around when the owner can restart the workers.

## Change
When the coordinator's release differs from the worker's, the worker updates itself between jobs and restarts:
1. Learn the coordinator's release SHA over the existing authenticated channel (for example in the heartbeat response).
2. Only while no job is leased: `git fetch` the worker's checkout, require the SHA to be reachable from `origin/main` (refuse any other commit), check it out detached, and run `bun install --frozen-lockfile`.
3. Re-exec the worker with its original arguments, so a worker started in a terminal keeps running there.
4. If any step fails, stay on the old release, take no jobs, and report the reason as the worker's setup warning, so `workers ls` shows why. Never run a job on a mismatched release.

A Bun version mismatch is reported as today; upgrading Bun is out of scope.

## Tests
- Fake coordinator reports a newer release: the worker finishes its current job, updates, and re-execs (exec and git injected).
- A SHA not reachable from `origin/main` is refused; the worker keeps its release and reports why.
- A failed `bun install` leaves the old release in place and takes no jobs.

## Out of scope
Upgrading Bun on workers; changing `limitless deploy`.

## Budget
About 60 source lines plus tests.

Closes #632

findings.title: A failed update rolls back the code but keeps the new dependencies
findings.detail: After `bun install --frozen-lockfile` has run for the target's lockfile, a later failure (process.execve missing or throwing) restores HEAD but not node_modules, so the running worker's later module loads and the next manual restart use dependencies that don't match the checked-out lockfile; a partially failed install does the same. Check that process replacement is available before changing anything, and on rollback re-run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` at the original HEAD (report that failure too). Add a test where exec throws after install: the original HEAD is restored and the install runs again at it.

findings.title: One transient failure disables updates until a manual restart
findings.detail: `updateAttempted` latches after the first try and `updateTarget ??=` never changes, so a transient `git fetch` error or lock contention leaves the worker advertising zero slots forever: network recovery, a newer coordinator release, or a coordinator rollback to the worker's own release don't help. Track the latest release the coordinator reports; when it equals the worker's own, clear the update state and take jobs again; when it changes, start over. Retry transient failures with a bounded backoff (one retry layer, a deadline per target), keep the last failure as the warning, and don't retry a permanent validation failure (a SHA not on origin/main) for the same target. Add tests: a transient failure followed by a successful retry; a target change after a failure; a coordinator that returns to the worker's release.

findings.title: The coordinator carries a stale update warning forward
findings.detail: heartbeat() copies the previous updateWarning whenever a heartbeat omits it and the release is unchanged. After a failed update, a coordinator rollback to the worker's release and a manual worker restart, the clean worker keeps the old warning, and the new `json_extract(capabilities,'$.updateWarning') IS NULL` guard then stops both a successful setup from clearing setup_warning and a later setup fallback from recording its real warning. The worker sends its update state on every heartbeat, so store exactly what the current heartbeat reports (no carry-over), and keep the setup-fallback warning separate from the update warning. Add a test for the rollback-then-restart sequence.

findings.title: A worker reporting an update failure breaks against the previous coordinator
findings.detail: The previous release's Heartbeat schema is `.strict()`, so after a coordinator rollback a worker that sends the new `updateWarning` field gets HTTP 400, call() throws, and the heartbeat task stops the worker. Send updateWarning only to a coordinator that has advertised the update protocol (for example only after a heartbeat reply that included releaseSha), so a new worker keeps working with the previous coordinator. Add a test with a strict legacy heartbeat schema.

head: 1690c79f7ad3ff38da8e270f18213e3800f99420
prompt:
gate-executor test: 'process is gone' checks race zombie reaping on Linux CI

## What happened
`forgotten local execution stops before replacement (sha)` in `test/gate-executor.test.ts` failed once on Linux CI, on #563, a catalog-strings-only change. Main passes.

```
773 |           expect(() => process.kill(pid, 0)).toThrow();
error: expect(received).toThrow()
Received function did not throw
```

## Why (likely)
The test checks that a forgotten execution's `sleep 900` is gone by asserting `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws, right before the replacement starts and after each result. On Linux, a killed child stays in the process table as a zombie until its parent reaps it, and `kill(pid, 0)` on a zombie succeeds. The assertion therefore races the reap, and on a slow runner it can see the zombie. This is test flakiness. Nothing shows the cleanup itself leaving a live process, but the fix must confirm that.

## Change
- Make the test assert that the process is gone or a zombie, not merely that `kill(pid, 0)` fails. For example:
  - on Linux, read `/proc/<pid>/stat` and accept state `Z`, or a missing entry;
  - on macOS, use the existing process inspection.
- Alternatively, wait for the stop's own exit confirmation before asserting.
- Keep the assertion strict about a running (non-zombie) process.
- Check the other `process.kill(pid, 0)` "is gone" assertions in the test files for the same race.

## Acceptance
- The test still fails if cleanup leaves the process running. Show this by disabling the stop in a temporary probe.
- The test passes on Linux CI and macOS.

## Budget
Test-only. A few lines.

Closes #564

findings.title: Five "is gone" assertions still race zombie reaping
findings.detail: The issue asks to convert every `process.kill(pid, 0)` "is gone" assertion with the same race. These still assert that a killed or cancelled descendant makes kill(pid, 0) throw, so they can see a not-yet-reaped zombie: test/signal-confinement.test.ts:209 (owned descendant after timeout/cancel), test/hardening.test.ts:672 and :741 (cancelled writer), test/smoke.test.ts:1570 (completed attempt's child), and test/pipeline-delivery-privacy.test.ts:540 (cancelled scan child, `toThrow(... ESRCH)`). Convert them to expectProcessStopped. Leave assertions that a process is still alive (`expect(kill(control.pid, 0)).toBe(true)`) as they are.

findings.title: On Linux a missing stat file is accepted without confirming the process is gone
findings.detail: expectProcessStopped returns on ENOENT/ESRCH from reading /proc/<pid>/stat. If procfs isn't mounted, or hides other users' processes (hidepid), a live process also gives ENOENT, so the helper passes for a running process, against the issue's requirement to stay strict about one. Before accepting a missing stat file, require `process.kill(pid, 0)` to fail with ESRCH (a zombie is already handled by the stat path); let any other outcome fail the assertion.

head: 1989445c641c560e42d0a44cbc07b9986d3f1160
prompt:
CI: a hung test run leaves no log; stop it inside the step so the log is kept

## Problem
On 2026-10-08, two CI runs on Linux hung until the job's `timeout-minutes: 25` cancelled them (run 37725010065 on #408 at b3386bf, and run 37725905014 on #415 at 2e75ecc, about 15 minutes apart). A rerun of each passed in about 9 minutes, so something in the suite hangs intermittently on Linux.

Neither run left a log. When GitHub cancels a job at its timeout, the job log is not uploaded (the logs API returns `BlobNotFound`), so there is no way to see which test or process hung. The CI classifier then sees a cancelled run, not a failure with output.

## Change
1. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: stop the check inside the step, a few minutes before the job timeout, so that the step fails and its log is kept. For example, run it under `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=30s 20m`, and before the kill, print what is still running: the process tree below the runner, and the test file bun was in. Keep `timeout-minutes` as the outer limit.
2. Make the hang identifiable from that log. If bun's own output doesn't show the active test file when it is stopped, print a marker as each test file starts, through the cheapest mechanism bun supports in CI only. Don't change local or factory test output.
3. Once a hang has been captured, fix its cause in a follow-up. This issue only has to make it visible.

## Tests
- A workflow-level check is enough: the step's command is a real `timeout` wrapper whose limit is below `timeout-minutes`. If any helper script is added, test it with a command that sleeps past a short limit: it must exit non-zero, print the process tree, and stop its children.

## Budget
About 20 lines in the workflow and any helper script.

## Out of scope
- Raising `timeout-minutes`.
- Retrying in CI.
- Factory changes: the CI classifier's handling of cancelled timeouts is tracked separately.

Closes #416

findings.title: The marker test fails on macOS outside the sandbox, so `bun run check` fails there
findings.detail: Reproduced unconfined on macOS: `bun test test/ci-check.test.ts` fails "CI file-start markers bypass parallel Bun buffering and are opt-in" with Expected "[test:start] /var/folders/…/hang.test.ts", Received "[test:start] /private/var/folders/…/hang.test.ts". tmpdir() returns the /var spelling and Bun reports the canonical /private/var path. It passes inside the factory's confined gate only because TMPDIR there isn't a symlinked path; the deploy gate, scripts/land-pr.sh and a developer's `bun run check` run unconfined and would fail. Canonicalize the fixture directory (realpathSync of the mkdtemp result) before building the expected paths, and run the test both confined and unconfined (`bun test test/ci-check.test.ts` from a plain shell).

findings.title: On Linux CI the nested wrapper run exits 1 instead of 137
findings.detail: Linux CI (GitHub Actions run 39256013886 at 1989445) fails "CI file-start markers bypass parallel Bun buffering and are opt-in": the Linux-only part that runs `bash -c 'export LIMITLESS_CI_TEST_LOG="/proc/$$/fd/2"; bash "$@"' fixture scripts/ci-check.sh 1s <bun> test --parallel=2 --preload test/setup.ts <dir>` gets exit code 1 where the test expects 137 (`expect(result.exitCode).toBe(137)`, Received: 1). The other Linux wrapper tests (exit status pass-through and the TERM-ignoring children case, which run the wrapper with a plain spawn) passed in the same run, so the difference is this nested invocation under `sh()` with a hanging parallel bun test. Find why the wrapper exits 1 there (for example `set -m` or job control failing when the wrapper runs under a non-interactive parent, the monitor's group signal, or bun exiting first) and fix the wrapper or the test so a timeout always yields the timeout status. This can't run on macOS; reason from the script and GNU timeout's behavior, and say in the report what Linux CI should show.

head: 63067719384488c91cdbb8e4bf1fd28912ba6311
prompt:
Audit: flag scratch output committed into the checkout before it blocks publication

## What's wrong
On 2026-10-19 a review round on #624 committed about 9,000 lines of gate output that the implementer had written into the checkout (`.tmp-gate/out.txt`, `.tmp-gate/report.xml`). A later implement round in the same run deleted them. The diff audit passed every commit ("0 blocking, 0 warnings"). Only at delivery did the private-text check refuse the branch, because the history now contained content beyond its decoding limit. The run ended `needs_human` with the message "Published content exceeds the private text decoding limit; publication blocked", and nothing was delivered. That cost a whole review round (about $6.50) and gave no hint which file or commit caused it.

## Change
1. **Catch it at the commit, not the delivery.** The audit already sees each round's diff. Add a warning for a round that adds files under a hidden directory at the checkout root, or a single new text file over a size threshold. Feed it back to the implementer as round feedback, so the next round removes it before anything is published. Don't block: a legitimate change can add a large fixture.
2. **Name the cause when publication is refused for size.** The refusal should say which commit and path exceeded the decoding limit (with credentials redacted, as now), so the owner and the next round can act on it.

## Tests
- A round that adds `.tmp-gate/report.xml` gets an audit warning in its feedback; the following round sees it.
- A publication refused for size names the commit and path.

## Out of scope
Changing the private-text limits, and rewriting round history before publication.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #635

findings.title: Encoded credentials survive the new diagnostic's redaction
findings.detail: diagnose() builds the refusal message from a path with redactCredentials (which matches registered credentials literally) and redactPrivate, then calls checkPublicationText(section, name(path), []) with no entries, which enforces only the decoding limit. A file whose name contains a percent-encoded (or otherwise encoded) registered credential, in a change that also exceeds the decoding limit, therefore yields a refusal message containing the recoverable credential, and that message is stored and shown. AGENTS.md: decode before you redact. Decode the path the way the publication check does before redacting credentials and private strings, and if a decoded form still matches a credential or private entry, withhold the filename ("[redacted filename]") rather than printing it. Add a test with a percent-encoded registered credential in a filename plus oversized content: the refusal names the commit and "[redacted filename]" and never contains the encoded value.

findings.title: Audit filenames are checked for private strings before they are normalized
findings.detail: The finding's file is checked with privateMatches on the raw path and only then passed through redactGateOutput. A new path such as `.tmp-gate/secret-\x1b[31mhost.example.txt` doesn't match the private entry `secret-host.example` while the escape sequence is in it; redactGateOutput then strips the escape and produces the literal private string, which reaches persisted audit findings and the implementer's next-round feedback. Canonicalize first (redactGateOutput / strip terminal sequences, redact credentials), then run privateMatches on the normalized filename and replace it with "[redacted filename]" on a match. Apply the same order to the detail text. Add a test with an escape sequence splitting a private entry in an added path.

findings.title: Diagnosis is quadratic in the number of files
findings.detail: For every patch section, diagnose() searches the whole raw entry list (`raw.find(ids)`), so a refused change with many files does O(files²) synchronous work after the aggregate check has already refused, outside git's subprocess timeout and without observing cancellation. Index the raw entries by blob id pair (a Map) so each section is a constant-time lookup, and keep diagnosis bounded: if it can't locate the offending file within a fixed budget, rethrow the original refusal unchanged.

findings.title: Legitimate dot-directory additions get scratch-output advice
findings.detail: root-hidden-addition warns on any new file beneath a root dot-directory and tells the implementer to "Remove accidental scratch output". A required new file such as `.github/workflows/<name>.yml` or `.github/dependabot.yml` gets the same advice, which can lead an implementer to delete it. Exempt `.github/` (and any other dot-directory the repository already tracks files in at the base commit), so the rule targets new hidden directories like `.tmp-gate/`. Add a test that a new `.github/workflows/x.yml` gets no warning.

head: ea7af370b8165578114c8d8fffc17e268a7ab061
prompt:
Invocation cleanup: a daemon crash mid-cleanup leaves descendants that a resumed run never recovers

## Scope (re-scoped 2026-10-19)
A first attempt (#624) didn't converge after three review rounds. It changed `processBirth`'s zombie semantics, and each later round found a new reaping race in the macOS leader inspection. Build the smaller change below; the original description further down is background.

**Change**
1. Before signalling any member during invocation cleanup, persist an ownership record: run, invocation, checkout directory, PID, birth identity and boot identity. The boot identity is `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` on Linux and `kern.bootsessionuuid` on macOS; `kern.boottime` moves when the clock is set, so don't use it. Delete an invocation's records once its cleanup completes.
2. Recover recorded cleanups when a run resumes and before a run's next command in its own checkout. At daemon start, recover in the background after the HTTP server is up, so health isn't delayed. Recovery retires a record from another boot without signalling it, SIGKILLs every member whose birth identity still matches, then waits for all of them under one deadline, using its own liveness check that treats a zombie or a missing process as stopped. If confirmation fails, refuse with a clear reason, as cleanup already does.
3. Gate a run's commands only on that run's own records, or on records whose directory is inside the run's own checkout; shared factory directories (for example the repository cache) must not link runs. A missing checkout means no other run's records match, and the run's own records are still recovered (don't throw on a missing path).
4. In the cleanup error path, the live direct child (its ChildProcess handle has no exit or signal yet) is always SIGKILLed, even if recording it or inspecting it fails; keep those failures in the termination error.

**Don't change** `processBirth`, `captureDarwinInvocationLeader` or the live cleanup's process inspection. Rediscovering processes an interrupted sweep never recorded is #625.

**Compatibility** New table only (`process_cleanups`); the previous release ignores it.

**Tests**
- Kill the cleanup between freeze and kill, then resume: the stopped member is killed, identity-checked, before the next step runs.
- A recorded PID whose identity changed (reused), or a record from another boot, is never signalled.
- A cleanup error with inspection unavailable still kills the live direct child.
- Another run's unresolved record in a shared directory doesn't block or fail this run; a missing checkout doesn't fail recovery.

**Budget** About 120 source lines plus tests. Write scratch output under `$TMPDIR` only (AGENTS.md).

---

## What's wrong
If the daemon dies while it is cleaning up an invocation's marked processes, nothing recovers the processes that cleanup hadn't finished with. A resumed run doesn't notice them.

Found while reviewing #561 (#537), which changes the cleanup to freeze and then kill. Reproduction (Codex, temporary test): a real runProcess invocation left a sleeper behind. Inspection was paused after the sweep's SIGSTOP, and the owned supervisor was then killed. A fresh runProcess in the same directory returned exit code 0, while the previous sleeper stayed in state T.

This predates #561. Before it, the same crash left the processes running, which is worse: they could keep writing to the checkout. With #561 they are stopped, but they are still never cleaned up. The claimed set and its birth identities live only in memory.

## Change
Before signalling any process, persist the cleanup's ownership record: the run, the invocation, the claimed PIDs and their birth identities. When a run resumes, or the daemon starts, finish any recorded cleanup. Kill a recorded member only if its birth identity still matches, and refuse with a clear reason if confirmation fails, as cleanup already does. A resumed invocation must not start in a checkout whose previous cleanup is unresolved.

## Tests
- Kill the cleanup process between freeze and kill, then resume. The stopped member is killed, identity-checked, before the next step runs.
- A recorded PID whose identity changed (reused) is never signalled.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #562

findings.title: Recovery isn't serialized with an active live cleanup
findings.detail: Recovery reads and acts on process_cleanups records without coordinating with a cleanup that is still running for the same invocation. A concurrent command in the same run (review panels and gates run invocations concurrently) can recover and SIGKILL a member that live cleanup A has frozen and is still tracking; A keeps `identity.frozen = true`, and if its later identity inspection fails, its fallback (around src/util/proc.ts:535) can SIGKILL that PID, which may by then belong to another process, without confirming its birth. Serialize live cleanup and recovery per invocation across recording, signalling and record deletion (an in-process lock keyed by invocation: recovery skips or awaits an invocation whose cleanup is active), and make concurrent recovery callers coordinate the same way. Add a regression test for this interleaving: a concurrent command's recovery must not signal members of a cleanup that is still in progress.

findings.title: The real boot-identity reader is never exercised
findings.detail: test/setup.ts stubs boot inspection for every test, and no test calls darwinBootIdentity (kern.bootsessionuuid) or the Linux boot_id reader unstubbed, so a broken reader would pass the suite and break recovery in production. Add a test that calls the real reader and checks it returns the same non-empty value twice. The read is denied inside the factory's confinement, so give it `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)` with seatbeltSkip from test/confinement.ts in the title, as AGENTS.md describes for real-Seatbelt tests (the Linux reader can run unconditionally on Linux).

head: ca723d51e3efcdda767dcb9c314d085e88178a50
prompt:
Preview: run setup in the coordinator's worktree when gates ran on a LAN worker

## What's wrong
With `[gates] executor = "lan"`, a run that touches the UI fails at its preview build. On 2026-10-19 the run for #470 ended with `Preview build failed: $ bun scripts/build-ui.ts ... error: Could not resolve: "solid-js/web". Maybe you need to "bun install"?`.

The gates and their setup commands (`bun install --frozen-lockfile` here) ran on a LAN worker, in the worker's own checkout. The preview, though, starts in the coordinator's worktree (`startPreview(cwd, ...)` in src/pipeline/engine.ts, around line 1799), and that worktree never ran setup: its `node_modules` is empty. Under the local executor, setup had already run in that worktree, which is why this didn't show before.

## Change
Before building a preview, make sure the repository's setup has run in that worktree. When the gates ran remotely, or setup otherwise hasn't run there, run the base commit's setup commands (from `.limitless.toml`, the same ones the gates use) locally in the run's worktree first, confined and under the gate slot exactly like local gate setup. If setup fails, the preview reports that setup failure, not a build error. Don't change where the gates themselves run.

## Tests
- Gates on a fake remote executor and a preview configured: the preview first runs the setup commands locally in the run's worktree, then builds.
- Gates run locally: no extra setup run.
- A failing setup surfaces as a preview setup failure.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.

Closes #643

findings.title: The new preview-setup tests fail on unconfined macOS
findings.detail: The assertion compares the paths written by shell `pwd` with `agent.cwd` as literal strings. On macOS outside the factory's confinement, TMPDIR is under /var/..., while /var is a symlink to /private/var, so `pwd` records /private/var/... and the remote, local, local fallback and local retry cases all fail (reproduced: `bun test test/pipeline-preview.test.ts` gives 4 failures, cwd=/var/folders/... vs calls=/private/var/folders/...). These tests must pass in development and in the manual land-pr.sh check, not only inside confined gates. Compare canonical paths (realpath both sides), as test/AGENTS.md describes for temporary paths, and run the file both unconfined and with LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1.

findings.title: Preview setup results are logged as ordinary gate setup
findings.detail: The preview's setup run reuses gateEvents(ctx), so its results appear in the run's event log as plain `setup: pass/FAIL` gate events, the same as the candidate's gate setup. Someone reading the log cannot tell that a setup failure came from the coordinator's preview preparation rather than the gates. Give these events a preview label (for example a `preview setup:` message prefix) while keeping the same slot, confinement, scratch and cancellation behaviour, and assert the label in the existing test.

head: 3488ca31038b2ed85809486412d5362991b0cd35
prompt:
Cleanup recovery: rediscover marked processes an interrupted sweep never recorded

## Scope note (2026-10-19)
Recovery landed in #641 (not #624, which was closed): records live in `process_cleanups`, recovery uses its own zombie-aware liveness check, and a per-invocation lock serializes live cleanup and recovery. Build rediscovery on that. As in #562's re-scope, don't change `processBirth`, `captureDarwinInvocationLeader` or the live cleanup's process inspection; persist what discovery needs (marker, canonical directories) with the existing record and reuse the existing discovery code from recovery.

## What's wrong
Crash recovery of an invocation's cleanup (#562, PR #641) finishes only the members the interrupted sweep had already recorded. Live cleanup rescans after freezing, because a process tree keeps forking while it is being stopped. If the daemon dies mid-sweep, any process that a not-yet-frozen member forked after the last scan, or a sibling the sweep hadn't claimed yet, has no record. Recovery kills the recorded members, deletes the rows, and lets the next command start while those processes keep running in the checkout.

Found while reviewing #624 (Codex review). The window is the crash landing inside an active sweep of a growing tree, so it is rare, but the result is the state #562 set out to remove.

## Change
Persist what live cleanup uses to find an invocation's processes (the invocation marker and its canonical directories) with the ownership record. Before completing a recovered cleanup, run the same discovery: claim and record any newly found member (with its birth identity) before signalling it, and repeat until a scan finds nothing new, as live cleanup does. Keep the existing rules: never signal a process whose identity can't be confirmed, refuse with a clear reason when discovery is unavailable, and don't complete the record until the invocation is quiescent.

## Tests
- Interrupt a sweep after it froze a parent that then forked an unrecorded child; resume: the child is found, recorded and killed before the next command runs.
- Discovery unavailable during recovery: the record stays unresolved and the run refuses with a clear reason.

## Out of scope
Changing live cleanup.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests.

Closes #625

findings.title: Recovery accepts a process group the saved leader no longer proves
findings.detail: Recovery passes the persisted Darwin leader to markedProcesses, and discovery accepts numeric session/group membership when the leader's birth matches or the leader is gone (birth null, src/util/processes-darwin.ts:333). During live cleanup the group is still the invocation's. Across daemon downtime it may not be: once every original member has exited, the kernel can reuse that ID, an unrelated process can become a group leader with it and exit, and recovery then treats that group's surviving members as ours and SIGKILLs them. In recovery, use numeric group membership only while continuity is proven, for example the saved leader is still alive with its recorded birth, or a member the factory recorded and confirmed by birth is still in that group (a group ID cannot be reused while any member lives). Otherwise pass no leader, so discovery relies on markers, proven parent chains and orphan cwd. Don't change live cleanup's discovery. Add a test: saved leader gone, no confirmed recorded member alive, an unrelated process in a group with the saved ID is never signalled.

findings.title: Cleanup records from the running release block their run until reboot
findings.detail: Rows written by the release now running (#641) have discovery = NULL. Recovery throws `Missing process discovery context` for them before checking anything, keeps the rows, and only a reboot (boot mismatch) ever removes them, so a run whose daemon crashed mid-cleanup before this deploy refuses every command in its worktree until the machine restarts. AGENTS.md: runs created before the change still resume. Recover such rows as #641 does: retire rows whose process is gone or whose birth differs, SIGKILL confirmed recorded members and wait for them, and skip only rediscovery (say so in the log). Change the legacy test to assert that the recorded member is killed and the record cleared.

head: b04735032bfc1f193f94d70030eca97670a90044
prompt:
Gate substitution: accept skipped tests the base commit's baseline also skipped

## What's wrong
When a verifier marks a criterion such as "existing test suites still pass" as blocked by its sandbox, verify can substitute the factory's own gate result for it (`applyGateEvidence` in src/pipeline/gate-evidence.ts). Substitution refuses whenever any candidate gate check has `testCoverage.skippedFiles`, with "candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests".

This repository's suite always has skipped files inside confined gates: tests that need real Seatbelt use `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)` and skip there by design (AGENTS.md, "Isolation"). So substitution can never apply here, and every run whose holdout or criteria include "the existing tests pass" ends as needs_human, even when every test that ran passed. Since 2026-10-14 this was the stated reason for about 20 of 49 needs_human runs (for example #644's run: test gate 4573 passed, 0 failed, 10 skipped files that the base commit's baseline also skipped).

## Change
Let substitution accept skipped tests that are inherited from the base commit, and nothing else:
- Record the identities of skipped tests (file plus test name, from Bun's `(skip)`/`(todo)` lines) in the gate result's test coverage, bounded in count and length like the existing coverage fields. Redact them like other gate output.
- In `passed()` (gate-evidence.ts), a check with skipped tests still qualifies only if the run's baseline (`ctx.state.baseline`, the same check name and command at the base commit) recorded skipped-test identities and every candidate skipped test appears in that baseline set. Pass the baseline in alongside the gate evidence; take it from factory records only.
- Refuse exactly as today when the baseline is missing, has no recorded identities (results from an older release), comes from a different command, or the candidate has any skipped test the baseline didn't have. A `(fail)` line still disqualifies the check, as do retries (`firstAttempt`), timeouts, confinement failures and incomplete output. The citation should say how many inherited skips there were.

Don't change what counts as a passing gate, a retry or a flaky result anywhere else.

## Compatibility
`testCoverage` is part of the worker protocol (src/workers/protocol.ts, `.strict()` schemas). Add the new field as optional. An older coordinator receiving it from a newer worker would reject the result, so check whether that can happen (workers follow the coordinator's release since #633), and note it in the PR.

## Tests
- A candidate whose skipped tests are a subset of the baseline's gets substitution; the citation counts the inherited skips.
- A candidate with one skipped test the baseline didn't have is refused; so is a missing baseline, a baseline without identities, and a `(fail)` line.
- Parsing records skipped-test identities from real Bun output lines (inline fixture).

## Budget
About 50 source lines plus tests.

Closes #646

findings.title: Skipped-test identities come from console rows that Bun doesn't reliably print or attribute
findings.detail: Reproduced with Bun 1.4.3 and the gate's environment (CI=1 NO_COLOR=1 FORCE_COLOR=0 LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, `bun test --parallel=4 --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=...`): runs of 3, 5, 32 and 79 test files printed no `(skip)` rows at all, only the `N skip` summary, so skipRows (0) never equals the summary and every such run is marked incomplete. In a full gate run (run mvg1mzsu0yzg7or1jabn5p's test gate) Bun printed a headerless list of all 103 skipped tests just before the summary, so `this.current` attributes every row to whichever file header was printed last; with --parallel, file headers repeat and interleave in arbitrary order, so identities differ between baseline and candidate or name the wrong file. The gate already writes a JUnit report (LIMITLESS_GATE_REPORT, parsed by src/gates/junit.ts), where each skipped testcase carries its `file` and `name` with validated counters. Take skipped-test identities from that report, under the same validation readJUnit/attributedJUnitCounts use (counters agree with testcases, size limits, safe paths), treat a missing or inconsistent report as incomplete, and add tests built from real Bun 1.4.3 JUnit output (a small inline fixture copied from a real run, not hand-written objects).

findings.title: Duplicate skipped-test identities are merged, so a new duplicate skip counts as inherited
findings.detail: Identities are deduplicated in a Map. If the baseline skips one test `x` in a file and the candidate adds a second skipped test with the same file and name, both runs record the single identity and substitution accepts the new, unexecuted test. Compare occurrence counts per identity: every candidate identity's count must be at most the baseline's. Add a test.

findings.title: The baseline may come from a different base commit than the one the candidate was merged with
findings.detail: A conflict round updates run.baseSha to the newly fetched base (engine.ts:2645) but keeps ctx.state.baseline, which records no commit (GateRun has no sha). Substitution then compares the candidate's skips with a baseline taken on the old base, so a skip that the new base removed and the conflict resolution reintroduced counts as inherited. Record the commit the baseline ran on and accept inherited skips only when it equals the base the candidate was checked against; otherwise refuse (results without a recorded commit refuse). Add a test.

findings.title: Skipped tests in files the candidate changed count as inherited
findings.detail: Identity matching ignores what the candidate changed: editing the body of an already-skipped test, or a skipped test in a file the diff modifies, keeps the same identity, so substitution reports the tests as passing although the changed test never ran. Pass the candidate's changed files (from the factory's own diff, never model output) into substitution and refuse inheritance for any skipped test whose file the diff adds, modifies, renames or deletes. Add a test.

findings.title: Credential redaction can make two different test names compare equal
findings.detail: Lines are redacted before identities are recorded, so a baseline name containing a registered credential and a different candidate name containing the replacement text become identical. Keep redaction for anything stored, but treat an identity that redaction changed as incomplete evidence (refuse inheritance) rather than comparing redacted names. Add a test.

findings.title: The refusal reason no longer says why skips were refused
findings.detail: When skips are present but not inherited, the evidence still says `candidate gate checks did not all pass cleanly without retries or skipped tests`. Say which condition failed (for example `skipped tests not inherited from the baseline at <base>` or `baseline skip identities unavailable`) so a reader can tell an inheritance refusal from a failing or retried check.

head: 34b408c69172b62cc7269ce2a81d55eb3c3b7a3d
prompt:
Redaction: decode filenames before matching credentials and private entries (audit findings, base64)

## What's wrong
Filenames in factory diagnostics are redacted only literally in two places, so an encoded secret in a path can be stored and shown:

1. **Audit findings.** `auditDiff` (src/gates/audit.ts) normalizes a finding's `file`, then checks it with `privateMatches` against the private entries only. Credentials are removed by `redactGateOutput`, which matches registered credentials literally. A filename containing a percent-encoded registered credential, or an HTML-encoded private entry (`privateMatches` doesn't decode HTML), survives into persisted audit findings, events and the implementer's next-round feedback. This applies to every audit rule that names a file, not just the scratch-output rules #640 added.
2. **Base64.** The publication decoder in src/gates/private.ts has no base64 support. A base64-encoded credential is not caught in published content, and #640's refusal diagnosis prints such a filename unchanged.

Found while verifying #640 (Codex review); both predate it.

## Change
- Audit: check each finding's normalized filename with the same decoding the publication check uses, against private entries and registered credentials, and replace it with `[redacted filename]` on a match. Treat the detail text the same way.
- Decide whether the publication check should recognise base64 runs that decode to a registered credential or a private entry (decoding only runs long enough to hold one, to keep false positives low), and apply that decision to the filename checks too. Document the decision if base64 stays out of scope.

## Tests
- An added file whose name holds a percent-encoded registered credential produces an audit finding with `[redacted filename]`, in persisted findings and in retry feedback.
- The same for an HTML-encoded private entry.
- Base64: per the decision above.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests.

Closes #642

findings.title: Decoding is split across separate paths, so combined encodings still escape
findings.detail: HTML references are decoded only once, outside the layer loop (publicationMatches); base64 is spliced into the loop; and auditDiff adds a third pass that removes each entry's literal spelling and re-checks. Each review round has found another composition that slips through (most recently percent or HTML encoding around base64, and literal redaction destroying evidence before decoding). Replace the special cases with one decoder and one decision point: (1) in normalizedLayers, every round applies all supported decoders: percent runs, \u escapes, HTML character references (with the whitespace collapse publicationMatches does now), then base64 runs whose decoded text contains a protected value. Repeat until nothing changes, within the existing round limit (not settling stays a refusal, as now). Replacing only matching base64 runs keeps unrelated base64-looking words from affecting convergence. publicationMatches/checkPublicationText then use that matcher directly. (2) In auditDiff, decide on the terminal-escape-stripped raw file and detail, before any literal redaction, with that matcher over private entries plus registered credentials: a matching file becomes `[redacted filename]`, a matching detail `[redacted diagnostic]`, otherwise keep the text. Remove the per-entry redactLiteral pass and the separate raw-base64 pass. (3) Encodings nested inside a decoded base64 run (base64 of percent- or HTML-encoded text) stay out of scope: say so in a short comment where base64 is decoded. (4) Add one table-driven test covering, for a private entry and a registered credential, in an added file's name and in a finding's detail: percent(HTML(x)), HTML(percent(x)), percent(base64(x)), HTML-escaped base64, base64 at a non-zero byte offset (`user:` + x), and an unrelated base64-looking word that must neither redact nor refuse. Keep the source change small: the issue budgeted about 30 lines, and this version is about 70.

findings.title: One passing test with a newline in its title makes the whole JUnit report unusable

findings.title: Identical duplicate titles can swap which one is skipped

head: 288606893a0c5acc5485ae5db89ec48f8625aa3b
prompt:
Landing queue follow-ups: deploy when idle, and a land list in the UI

Follow-up from #352, parts 6 and 7, which weren't built when the landing queue shipped (#388).

## Change
1. **Deploy when idle (self-hosting only).** With `[deploy] after_land = "when_idle"`, the daemon deploys once the landing queue has no active entry and no run is active. It is off by default, and a new optional config key with a default is fine for an older release (say so next to the key in the docs). Today the orchestrator does this with a script that polls `land_entries`.
   - Reuse `limitless deploy`'s path: checks, smoke, drain and restart with rollback.
   - Deploy only a main that changed since the running release.
   - A failed deploy blocks further automatic deploys until the next landing. The feed says why.
2. **A land list in the UI.** Show the queue's entries (state, PR, approved SHA, reason, log link), newest first, with a cancel action for active entries. It reads `/api/land`. Follow the UI rules in AGENTS.md: the newest response wins, and refresh after a mutation.

## Tests (no network)
- With `after_land = "when_idle"` and a fake deploy hook: a landing followed by an idle queue deploys once. An active run delays it. A second landing during the delay still deploys only once.
- With the key unset, nothing deploys.
- The UI list renders entries and refreshes after a cancel.

## Out of scope
Deploying for repositories other than the daemon's own.

Closes #470

findings.title: A rollback after the new release boots is never recorded
findings.detail: At boot the daemon clears the persisted attempt as soon as bootSha equals attempt.sha, but the deploy job is still health-checking that new daemon. If the health check then fails and `limitless deploy` rolls back (src/cli/service.ts), the rolled-back daemon finds no attempt: nothing is blocked and the feed never says the deploy failed. The reverse also happens: a boot on the old SHA while the job is still running declares failure early. The job's exit status (its status file) is the only authority for the outcome, and the caller that reads it is killed by the restart. Keep the attempt (with its job id) until its terminal status has been read; at boot and on later ticks, reconcile an unfinished attempt from that job's status file, recording success, or a block plus a deploy.failed feed item with the redacted log tail. Add tests: target boots then the job reports failure (rollback): blocked and reported; old-SHA boot while the job is still running: not judged until the status exists.

findings.title: A deploy job that never writes its status stalls automatic deploys forever
findings.detail: deployProcess polls the status file with no deadline and no check that the launchd job still exists, so a job that was removed, crashed before writing its status, or hung leaves AutoDeploy's `running` flag set and no later landing ever deploys; and removeDeployJob skips jobs without a status while the boot reconcile forgets the job id. Bound the wait (a deadline above `limitless deploy`'s own maximum) and detect a job that no longer exists (for example `launchctl list <label>` failing); either way record a block with a clear reason and remove the job, and keep the job id durable until its removal has succeeded. Add tests for a missing job and a deadline.

findings.title: The deploy job loses the daemon's port override
findings.detail: The job forwards only PATH, LANG, LIMITLESS_HOME and LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR. A daemon started with LIMITLESS_PORT (documented) launches a deploy whose CLI resolves the default or configured port instead (src/cli/client-port.ts) and can drain, health-check or restart the wrong daemon. Pass the running daemon's port to the deploy explicitly (or forward LIMITLESS_PORT and HOME), and add a test asserting the job's command carries it.

findings.title: Deploy output is stored without redaction
findings.detail: launchd writes the deploy's stdout and stderr straight to ~/.limitless/logs/<label>.log; only the excerpt returned as the failure reason is redacted. AGENTS.md requires redaction wherever secret-bearing text is stored. Send the job's output through redactCredentials before it reaches the file (for example a small wrapper that redacts each line with the daemon's registered credentials), and make the existing secret-emitting test assert the log file itself is redacted.

findings.title: The Land page doesn't refresh after the event stream reconnects
findings.detail: The page loads on mount and every 15 seconds but ignores the existing reconnect notification, so after an SSE reconnect it shows stale rows until the next poll. Refresh (coalesced) on reconnect, as AGENTS.md's UI rule asks, and cover it in test/land-ui.test.ts.

findings.title: after_land = "when_idle" on a platform without launchd fails only at deploy time
findings.detail: The deploy job uses /bin/launchctl, so on Linux every automatic deploy fails and blocks. Refuse `deploy.after_land = "when_idle"` when the daemon isn't on macOS, with a clear message, and say in the docs next to the key that it needs the launchd service.

prompt:
Landing queue follow-ups: deploy when idle, and a land list in the UI

Follow-up from #352, parts 6 and 7, which weren't built when the landing queue shipped (#388).

## Change

It is off by default, and a new optional config key with a default is fine for an older release (say so next to the key in the docs). Today the orchestrator does this with a script that polls `land_entries`.
   - Reuse `limitless deploy`'s path: checks, smoke, drain and restart with rollback.
   - Deploy only a main that changed since the running release.
   - A failed deploy blocks further automatic deploys until the next landing. The feed says why.
2. **A land list in the UI.** Show the queue's entries (state, PR, approved SHA, reason, log link), newest first, with a cancel action for active entries. It reads `/api/land`. Follow the UI rules in AGENTS.md: the newest response wins, and refresh after a mutation.
