- The UI list renders entries and refreshes after a cancel.

## Out of scope
Deploying for repositories other than the daemon's own.

Closes #470

findings.title: The plaintext credentials file is readable by agents
findings.detail: deployProcess writes every registered credential to ~/.limitless/logs/<label>.credentials. File modes don't stop processes running as the same user, and that directory isn't in the read-deny list that tool-enabled editors and readers get (src/harness/read-policy.ts; src/harness/codex.ts), so an agent running concurrently can read all factory secrets while the file exists. The file also survives some paths: death before submit returns, a filter that fails before unlinking, and the wrapper's relaunch branch, which never removes it. Put the file only where every confined process (gate, Claude editor/reader, Codex) is already denied reads, for example beside the other private credentials, or add its exact location to the shared deny list. Remove it on every path, including the relaunch branch and the boot reconcile. Prove it with a real Seatbelt probe (test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null), title including seatbeltSkip, per AGENTS.md): a confined reader can't read the file while the deploy runs, and a control read of an allowed path succeeds.

findings.title: Cleanup treats a failed launchctl inspection as the job being gone
findings.detail: removeDeployJob (and deployJobStatus's missing-job path) treat any nonzero result of `launchctl list <label>` as absence. With allowFail a timeout returns exitCode null, so a slow launchctl makes cleanup delete the status and started marker and report success; AutoDeploy then drops the durable job id while the job may still be registered, and without the started marker a relaunch deploys again. Treat only launchctl's definite not-found result as absence; on any other failure keep the job id and markers and retry on the next tick. Add tests for a timed-out list during removal and during status checks.

findings.title: A failing redaction filter can kill the deploy mid-way, or go unnoticed
findings.detail: The deploy writes into the filter's pipe. If the filter throws before it starts reading stdin (missing or invalid credentials file, unlink failure), the pipe closes and the deploy's next write gets EPIPE/SIGPIPE; `limitless deploy` can then die between checking out the candidate and restarting, or during health checks, bypassing its rollback. Make the filter unable to stop reading early: on any setup error, keep draining stdin to EOF and write only a fixed `[deploy output withheld: redaction unavailable]` line (never unredacted text). Record the filter's own exit status as well and include `log unavailable` in the recorded outcome when it failed, without changing the deploy's exit status. Add a test where the filter's credentials file is invalid: the deploy command still completes and its status is recorded.

head: 2cb9942e447bf8f41682932788f5ea9fbe2745d3
prompt:
Run review and verify in parallel

## Scope (refreshed 2026-10-20 for the current pipeline)
In a round of the standard and deep profiles, `oneRound` (src/pipeline/engine.ts) runs review, then, only if review approves, waits for the holdout scenarios, builds the preview (when the change needs one) and runs verify. Review and verify are both read-only, work from the same committed HEAD, and neither needs the other's output, but verify always waits for review. Run them concurrently, with the outcome unchanged.

## Change
1. **Order.** After gates and audit pass, settle everything that touches the worktree first: wait for the holdout scenarios and run the preview stage (its setup and build, #644) when one is needed. Then start the review stage and the verify stage together. Nothing may change the worktree (verify's `discardChanges`, `resetTo`, preview setup) while either stage runs; verify's post-invocation discard moves to after both have settled.
2. **One decision point.** Neither branch writes `ctx.state.feedback` or decides the round. Wait for both with `Promise.allSettled`, then decide deterministically:
   - review requests changes: the round's feedback is the review feedback, followed by a separate `### Acceptance criteria not yet met (verify)` section listing verify's unmet criteria, if any. Panel limits (`PANEL_REVIEWS`) and the needs_human path behave exactly as today;
   - review approves: the outcome is exactly today's verify outcome, including the blocked-only verify retry on another model, which runs after both have settled;
   - an error in either branch (holdout failure, `Holdout scenarios are unavailable`, `Commit changed during verification`, cancellation) still lets the other branch settle (no orphaned invocation, no stage row left `running`) before it propagates.
   The final state and feedback must not depend on which stage finishes first.
3. **Paths that stay sequential.** Quick profile (no verify), verify-change flow, review-resolution rounds and conflict rounds keep today's order.
4. **Resume.** Review results are cached per round and HEAD (`completedChecks`); verify isn't. A restart after review finished reuses review only if HEAD is unchanged and reruns verify. `ctx.run.stage` holds one name; set it to `review` while both run (display only).

## Out of scope
No change to verdict logic, routing, vendor exclusion, panel rules, holdout authoring or gate evidence.

## Tests (fake harness)
- Both invocations start before either finishes (controllable fakes, overlapping timestamps).
- Review blocks and verify passes: review feedback only. Review approves and verify fails: verify feedback. Both fail: review feedback plus the verify section.
- Each of those runs in both finish orders and produces identical state and feedback.
- An error in verify while review is in flight: review settles, then the error propagates; no stage row left running.
- No worktree change happens while review runs (assert discard/reset/preview timing against the review invocation).
- A restart after review finished reuses it at the same HEAD and reruns verify; at a different HEAD it reruns both.
- Quick, verify-change and resolution rounds are unchanged.

## Budget
About 120 changed source lines plus tests. Earlier attempts at large engine changes looped in review; keep it tight.

Closes #82

findings.title: A verify-side failure now overrides a review that requested changes
findings.detail: After Promise.allSettled, a rejected verify result is thrown before rejectReview runs. When review requests changes and verify fails for its own reasons (verifier models out of capacity, NoCapacityError, a structured-output failure, a NeedsHumanError raised inside the verify stage), the run now ends needs_human/failed, while before verify never ran and the round returned the review feedback to the implementer (including panel R3's own limit reason). Apply the review decision first: if review requested changes, a verify rejection other than cancellation/termination (CancelledError, SimulatedTermination, signal aborted) and `Commit changed during verification` is logged and dropped, and the round returns the review feedback; verify reruns next round. Add tests: review requests changes + verify throws (capacity, needs_human) → review feedback, round continues; + verify cancelled → cancellation propagates.

findings.title: A retry recorded at an older SHA now consumes the current SHA's retry
findings.detail: `retryHistory` in concurrent mode searches every verify result in the round, dropping the previous SHA filter (`!v.sha || v.sha === verifiedSha`). After a recorded retry at SHA A, a restart at SHA B whose fresh initial result is blocked-only stops immediately, where before B got its own alternative-model retry. That changes the retry policy beyond concurrency (the issue's out-of-scope list), and test/pipeline-verification.test.ts:783 encodes the change for changedHead=true. Keep the per-SHA filter for retry accounting and change that test back to the previous expectation.

findings.title: A resumed retry can rerun the verifier that just blocked
findings.detail: Concurrent mode always runs a fresh initial verify attempt on resume, but the blocked-only retry still picks the model to exclude (`firstModel`) from the historical `previous` results. Example: historical attempt by model A blocked; after a restart the fresh attempt by B blocks; the retry excludes A and can select B again, so the alternative-model retry no longer tries a different model. Exclude the model of the attempt that actually produced the current result. Add a restart test that asserts the retry's model differs from the fresh attempt's.

head: fc08d3f9bc12732133e0dd0ae12bd70d29dbae5d
prompt:
M5.2: a requirement-and-entry-point trace pass as a second finder (pre-registered)

**Question.** Does a second finder that only looks for unguarded paths raise recall on the
orchestrator's spec-mismatch and every-path findings without more false blocks?

**Why.** Production catches 0 of 6 spec-mismatch defect-trials and misses 13 defects that required
reading files the diff did not touch (research/14 §2). The orchestrator finds these by re-reading
the request's "every", "never" and "on resume" clauses against each entry point.

**What.** A `trace` finder prompt: list the request's universal clauses; for each guard the diff
adds or changes, enumerate sibling call sites and entry points with `rg` and the persisted state
that outlives a restart; report only an unguarded path cited by file and line with the clause it
violates. No logic review. Single mode accepts a second finder with this prompt; findings are
unioned with the main reviewer's by the existing merge; no verifier. Eval-only until adopted.

**Systems.** Baseline: production's reviewer, `codex/sol-6.1@medium` with the standard prompt
(E1's stored dev trials, 33/98 and 2/8). Variant E: baseline plus the trace finder.

**Cases and run.** The 35 dev ids, k=2. One eval run, about $14 plus the trace pass's input
tokens (the baseline is stored).

**Measures.** As #531, plus recall by category and the trace finder's findings reported
separately: added, landed on gold, blocked a clean case.

**Decision rule.** As #531 (+8 points, at most +1 clean block). Held-out once if adopted, and
only after #542's fresh clean set exists (#541 showed the current held-out clean set is
saturated).

**Budget and scope.** About 150 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: a verifier, the probe
prompt, production adoption.

Drafted in docs/research/14-review-strength.md (PR #540), Appendix B, proposal A2. Updated 2026-10-15 after #541: the adversarial prompt was not confirmed on held-out, so the rule's baseline is production's standard prompt, and the held-out run waits for #542's fresh clean set.

Closes #552

findings.title: The trace report can credit trace with a defect the main reviewer already caught
findings.detail: Candidates with `raisedBy: [1]` are treated as trace additions and matched against gold on their own. When the main reviewer and the trace finder report the same gold defect with titles or scenarios different enough to escape the merge, `addedOnGold` still counts it for trace, although the main report already catches that defect. The issue asks for the trace finder's findings to be reported separately (added, landed on gold, blocked a clean case), and this inflates its gold credit. Count a trace addition as landing on gold only when it matches a required defect that the main finder's own report did not catch (match the main report against gold first, then credit trace only for the remaining defects). Add a test with a main finding and a trace finding on the same gold defect under different titles: trace gets no gold credit.

head: 482ac4f30a70a8c4fd46e32c10550dbf73daf365
prompt:
M5.2: per-item recurring-defect sweep in the adversarial prompt (pre-registered)

**Question.** Does asking the reviewer to apply the repository's recurring-defect list item by item
raise recall without more false blocks?

**Why.** 22 of production's 30 dev misses match an item in AGENTS.md's "Defects reviews keep
finding" or the redaction ordering rules. The Codex reviewer has read the file; nothing asks it to
apply the list to the diff. BitsAI-CR's taxonomy raised precision; G-Research gates rules on
recall per severity; frontier models gain less from behavioural scaffolding, so the gain is
uncertain and must be measured.

**What.** An `adversarial-checklist` eval prompt: the adversarial prompt plus a fenced checklist
read from the base commit's AGENTS.md (never the PR's), capped in length, and a structured
`checklist[]` output field per item: `applies` (changed hunks), `checked` (command, traced path or
input tried), `finding` (id or none). Grading ignores the field.

**Systems.** Baseline for the rule: production's reviewer, `codex/sol-6.1@medium` with the
standard prompt (E1's stored dev trials, 33/98 and 2/8; the adversarial prompt alone was not
confirmed on held-out, #541). Attribution: E3's stored adversarial trials. Variant F: the
adversarial prompt plus the checklist.

**Cases and run.** The 35 dev ids, k=2, about $15.

**Measures.** As #531, plus the gain over E3 (what the checklist adds beyond the adversarial
framing) and how many findings cite a command or input in `checked` versus a bare pattern match.

**Decision rule.** As #531 against the production baseline. Held-out once if adopted, and only
after #542's fresh clean set exists.

**Budget and scope.** About 60 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: lenses, the probe prompt,
production adoption.

Drafted in docs/research/14-review-strength.md (PR #540), Appendix B, proposal A3. Updated 2026-10-15 after #541: the adversarial prompt was not confirmed on held-out, so the rule's baseline is production's standard prompt, and the held-out run waits for #542's fresh clean set.

Closes #553

findings.title: Record the cohort change as the authorized amendment
findings.detail: The narrowed cohort is now authorized: see the amendment comment on #553 (2026-10-20, before any trial). The run uses the dev cases whose base AGENTS.md contains both the recurring-defect bullets and the Privacy redaction-ordering bullets, 19 of the original 35 plus #542's dev cases once #674 makes them runnable, with the stored E1 (standard) and E3 (adversarial) trials restricted to the same cases as the baseline and attribution arms; decision rule unchanged. Make the research doc's recipe say exactly that and cite the amendment, keep the original 35-case registration visible as the registered design it amends, and list the excluded case ids with the reason (base predates the section).

findings.title: The checklist arm bypasses the pipeline's review entry point
findings.detail: For `adversarial-checklist` the runner skips `runReview` and calls the model directly (`pipelineReview = !checklist && reviewInput`), while the stored E1 and E3 trials it is compared against went through `runReview`. Any difference in how the request is assembled, invoked or post-processed there becomes a confound in the measured gain. Route the checklist arm through the same review entry point as the other single systems, differing only in the appended checklist text and the extra `checklist[]` output field (extend the schema there rather than bypassing it). Add a test that the checklist arm's request equals the adversarial arm's request plus the checklist block, and that both are graded through the same path.

findings.title: Resolve the conflicts with main
findings.detail: #662 (trace finder) and #663 (samples: 2) landed in review-system.ts, prompts.ts, schemas.ts and core/types.ts. Merge main, keep all three eval-only options (trace, samples, adversarial-checklist) refused by production schemas and rosters, and keep the existing validation that `samples` takes exactly one finder.

head: 9b43146b6968c8702886222798cf3cfd255d97f1
prompt:
Gate retries keep their gate slot

Slice of #150 (overload). A gate's retry of its failing test files releases its gate slot and then queues for a new one, so under load the retry waits behind other runs' full suites (noted while reviewing #151; `retryRegressions` and the land queue's targeted retry do the same).

## Change
Keep the gate slot held from a gate run through its own retries (regression retries and targeted file retries), on the local executor and in land checks, and release it once the gate's result is final. Retries that run on a LAN worker are unaffected. Waiting behaviour for other runs is unchanged: they still queue by priority.

## Tests
- A gate with a failing file that passes on retry holds one slot throughout: a second run queued for a slot doesn't get it between the first attempt and the retry.
- Cancellation during the retry releases the slot.

## Budget
About 40 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: slot priorities, LAN worker scheduling.

Closes #669

findings.title: A small targeted retry inside a scope that holds no slot now waits for a full gate slot
findings.detail: Inside a reservation scope, `acquireGateSlot` ignores `skipGateSlot` and does `held.release ??= gateSlots.acquire(...)`. A targeted retry small enough for the unslotted lane (`retryFailures` sets `skipGateSlot` for few, short files so it uses `agentTestSlots` and never queues behind full suites) therefore takes a full gate slot whenever the scope doesn't hold one yet, and then keeps it until the scope ends. That happens under the LAN executor, the production setup, when the first attempt ran on a worker and the retry runs locally as a fallback. Reproduced with the real module: with every gate slot held by other holders, `acquireGateSlot(signal, undefined, 'retry', true)` outside a scope acquires at once; `gateSlotScope(() => acquireGateSlot(signal, undefined, 'retry', true))()` stays blocked behind the full suites. Required: a `skipGateSlot` request inside a scope that holds no gate slot keeps today's behaviour (the agent-test lane, released after that attempt, without setting the scope's reservation). When the scope already holds the gate slot, reusing it is fine. Add a test for both.

findings.title: A local slot stays held while a later attempt in the same scope runs on a LAN worker
findings.detail: The LAN fallback is bound into the scope, so when a worker job fails and the gate falls back to local execution, the fallback's `runLocalGates` takes the scope's reservation. The retry that follows is a new executor job, and `lanExecutor.start` enqueues it to a worker (every job for a listed repository goes to the LAN). The scope keeps the local gate slot held, unused, for the whole remote retry. With `max_concurrent_gates = 1` that blocks every other local gate on the coordinator, plus agents' slotted commands in the `gate` lane, for the length of a remote suite. The issue says retries that run on a LAN worker are unaffected. Fallbacks are not rare: 36 'LAN gates falling back to local execution' events on this installation in three days. Required: the coordinator's gate slot is never held while an attempt runs on a LAN worker. Either keep LAN-executor attempts, including their local fallbacks, on today's per-attempt acquire and release, or release the scope's reservation when an attempt in the scope is dispatched to a worker. Add a test: a scope holding a slot from a local attempt, then a LAN-dispatched attempt, lets a queued waiter take the slot.

findings.title: Binding an unscoped caller lets a restored start context reuse another gate's reservation
findings.detail: When the caller has no reservation, `bindGateSlotScope` returns `fn` unchanged, and `started.context(...)` then restores whatever reservation was active when the handle was started. Reproduced in isolation (one slot: gate A holds it; B's handle is started inside A's context, then attached outside any scope; B's check runs while occupancy shows only A), so B runs without a slot of its own. Make the binding exact: when the caller has no reservation, run `fn` with none (`reservation.exit`, or `run` with an empty store), so only the attaching operation's own reservation applies.

findings.title: A rejected acquisition replaces the scope body's error
findings.detail: `finally { held.closed = true; (await held.release)?.(); }` re-awaits the acquisition. If it rejected (cancelled while queued) and the body then threw a different error, such as a cleanup failure from the gate-result save in `runGateExecution`, the `finally` throws the acquisition's rejection instead, and the original failure is lost (AGENTS.md: keep the original failure). Release only an acquisition that succeeded, and never throw from this `finally` because of a rejected one. Add a test.

head: 250e04ed806ca5ad1761f96786612d66157d036f
prompt:
Land queue: wait for another person's GitHub approval before merging (per repository)

Slice of #37 (M6, work-ready). Work repositories require another person's GitHub approval before merging, and the factory must never approve its own PRs.

## Change
A per-repository operator setting in `config.toml` (the operator's policy, never read from the repository): `[repos."<owner>/<name>"] land_requires_approval = true`.
- When set, a land entry waits in a new `waiting_approval` state until the PR's GitHub review state shows an approval from an account other than the one the factory acts as, given on the exact head commit being landed (the review's commit id equals the entry's approved SHA). Stale approvals on an earlier head don't count. Then the entry continues through today's checks, CI wait and `--match-head-commit` merge unchanged.
- Observation is by the existing conditional polling, so it works with webhooks off.
- The orchestrator's `limitless review --approve` still records the factory-side approval; it never submits a GitHub review.
- `limitless land list`, the Land page and the feed show `waiting_approval` with the reason.
- Unset: behaviour unchanged.

## Tests (fake `gh`, no network)
- With the setting, an entry waits until an approval from another login on the approved SHA arrives, then lands.
- An approval on an older head, or from the factory's own login, doesn't release it.
- Without the setting, behaviour is unchanged.

## Budget
About 100 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: discreet mode (#37's other half), requesting reviewers, CODEOWNERS.

Closes #671

findings.title: After a rollback the previous release lands entries that are waiting for approval
findings.detail: A waiting entry is stored physically as `state = 'checking'` with `approval_wait = 1`. The previous release doesn't know `approval_wait`: after a graceful shutdown (`releaseLandClaims` clears the claim) or once the claim goes stale, its `claimLandEntry` reclaims any `checking` entry and runs its own `land()`, which has no approval gate, so it checks, waits for CI and merges without anyone's approval. Reproduced: create an entry with this PR's Store, move it to `waiting_approval`, call `releaseLandClaims`, then open the same database with the deployed release's Store; `claimLandEntry('test/repo', …)` returns the entry in `checking`. A deploy rolls back automatically when the new release doesn't come up, so this gate fails open on a routine event (AGENTS.md: 'Leave the previous release working', 'Fail closed, precisely'). Required: store a waiting entry so that the previous release never lands it, for example as a state the previous release treats as finished (such as `blocked` with the approval flag; the new release reads it as `waiting_approval`, and the old one shows it blocked, needing a re-queue), or in a separate table keyed by the entry id with the entry in a non-landable state. Add a test that opens the database with the previous release's claim query (or an equivalent SQL-level check) and asserts it can't claim a waiting entry.

findings.title: A waiting entry holds its repository's only running land slot
findings.detail: Because the waiting entry stays physically `checking` with a live claim, it occupies `land_entries_one_running` for its repository and blocks the queue's worker for as long as approval takes, possibly days. Every other PR in that repository, including ones already approved, can't start landing. Reproduced: two entries in `test/repo`; after the first moves to `waiting_approval`, `claimLandEntry('test/repo', …)` returns null for the second. Required: an entry waiting for approval doesn't stop other entries in the same repository from landing. Approval is observed by polling and the entry rejoins the queue when it arrives. Order among approved entries stays FIFO by queue time. This fits naturally with the storage change in the blocker finding. Test: entry 1 waiting, entry 2 approved, entry 2 lands first.

findings.title: A stale saved snapshot can release the gate
findings.detail: With polling on, `awaitApproval` reads `savedSnapshot(this.store.githubPrData(...))` with no check of when it was observed or whether the last poll succeeded. If an approval is dismissed or replaced by a change request and the next poll fails (GraphQL error, rate limit), the saved snapshot still shows the old `APPROVED` review, and a successful `user` lookup releases the entry (reproduced by Codex: save an approval, return a GraphQL error from polling, the entry moves to `checking`). Required: release only on review evidence from a successful observation made after the entry started waiting (record the observation time with the snapshot, or observe directly as the polling-off path does). A failed or stale observation leaves approval unknown, and the entry keeps waiting. Test: saved approval, then a failing poll, and the entry stays waiting.

findings.title: Any GitHub account's approval counts, including accounts without push access and bots
findings.detail: `hasOtherApproval` accepts any latest review in state `APPROVED` from a login other than the factory's. On a public repository anyone can submit an approving review, and on a private one a read-only member can; GitHub's own required reviews count only reviewers with write access. A bot (for example `github-actions[bot]` where the repository allows Actions to approve PRs) also counts. So the gate meant to require another person's approval can be satisfied by an account with no authority over the repository. Required: count an approval only from a `User` (not a `Bot`) with push access. GraphQL `PullRequestReview` has `authorCanPushToRepository` and `author { __typename login }`; add them to `OBSERVE_QUERY` and `reviewEvidence`, treat missing fields as no approval, and also hold the entry while any such reviewer's latest review on the PR is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Tests: an approval from an account without push access and one from a bot don't release the entry; an outstanding change request from a push-access reviewer keeps it waiting despite another approval.

findings.title: Approval is checked once, before checks and CI, and never again before the merge
findings.detail: `awaitApproval` runs before land checks; after that, checks, the CI wait and the merge (often 20 to 40 minutes, longer under load) proceed without looking at the reviews again. An approval dismissed, or a change request submitted, in that window doesn't stop the merge (AGENTS.md: 'Check-then-act across an await'). Entries that already recorded `pushedSha` skip the gate entirely, so enabling the setting while a land is in flight merges that PR without approval (reproduced by Codex: reach `waiting_ci` with the policy off, restart with it on, and the entry merges with no identity or review lookup). Required: when the policy is on, re-check immediately before `merge`, regardless of `pushedSha`, using fresh evidence as in the stale-snapshot finding. Require a qualifying approval on the approved SHA or on the pushed head, and no outstanding change request. If it fails, the entry goes back to waiting instead of merging. Tests: approval dismissed during CI doesn't merge; policy enabled with a pushed entry waits for approval.

findings.title: Older MCP proxies fail on the new state value
findings.detail: The previous release's MCP status schema validates the land state against a fixed enum, so a long-running MCP proxy from before the deploy fails `limitless_status` and `limitless_get_run` as soon as any run-backed entry is `waiting_approval` (reproduced by Codex against the base schema). AGENTS.md: 'HTTP JSON changes are additive… Readers tolerate missing and unknown fields.' Keep the existing state values on the MCP wire (report the waiting entry with its current wire state plus a new optional field and the reason), or otherwise make sure a previous-release reader still parses the response. Make the new reader tolerate unknown states so the next addition doesn't repeat this.

head: 2eead4e34853bb0ffd855c2c280236557c82acd4
prompt:
Provider workload statistics from stored invocations

Slice of #34 (M6). The owner wants long-term provider workload numbers: how much work each provider and model does.

## Change
`limitless stats providers [--since <ISO-8601>] [--json]` and `GET /api/stats/providers?since=`, computed from the stored invocations (no new tracking):
- per provider and model: invocations, successful share, input/output/cached tokens, metered cost and API-equivalent cost, total and p50 wall time;
- broken down by role (triage, spec, implement, review, verify, …) and by day;
- eval invocations shown separately from production runs.
The HTTP field set is additive and readers tolerate absence. No UI in this slice.

## Tests
Seeded invocations across two providers, roles and days produce the expected aggregates; `--since` filters; eval invocations are separated.

## Budget
About 80 source lines plus tests.

Closes #673

findings.title: Compound eval trials credit every model's usage to the trial's first model
findings.detail: A trial without `rounds` becomes one record with `provider: details.provider` and `modelId: t.model_id`, carrying the whole trial's tokens, cost and duration. Review-eval trials with verifiers or several finders call other models too: 715 stored trials on this installation have a `details.verifiers` list (for example `claude/opus` verifiers on a `codex/sol-6.1` finder), and all of their usage is credited to the finder's provider, while the verifiers' provider shows none. Codex reproduced it with the fake runner: a panel of `openrouter/candidate-a`, `provider-b/candidate-b` and `provider-b/verifier-c` at $0.10 each reported $0.30 under `openrouter`, and `provider-b` disappeared. Required: never attribute a compound trial's usage to a single provider or model. Where the stored data doesn't split it by member, report it in a separate compound or unattributed row that lists the participating models, and keep the per-provider rows to records that really belong to one model. Test with a stored trial that has verifiers.

findings.title: Interrupted eval trials are dropped instead of counted with unknown usage
findings.detail: The filter for trials that never reached a provider (no rounds, no `invocationStatus`, skipped or preparation-failed, zero usage) doesn't check `details.interrupted`. A trial interrupted by a restart while running is persisted with `interrupted: true` and zero recorded usage, and disappears from the statistics (Codex reproduced it with `store.interruptEval()`). Count interrupted trials as executions, with token and cost fields unknown (`null`) rather than zero. Test it.

head: bde698f0b9181e0fd59ac3f8f0b3186a37a8a7d9
prompt:
Config: no hardcoded default GitHub owner (M6 portability)

## What's wrong
`src/config.ts` gives `[owners] github` a hardcoded default, the repository owner's own login: `githubOwner: str(owners.github, "<login>")`. On any other installation where the key is unset, that login silently becomes the trusted owner. Its `/limitless` comments and issue labels then trigger runs. Examples in README.md, docs/GUIDE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md repeat the literal login.

This matters for M6 (portable and work-ready). The work pilot runs under a different GitHub account, and a fresh `limitless init` on a second machine must not trust a stranger.

## Change
- No default owner. With `[owners] github` unset, owner-gated GitHub triggers (issue labels and `/limitless` comments) are off. Report that in `limitless doctor`.
- `limitless init` asks for the owner, or takes it from `gh api user`, and writes it.
- Existing installs that set the key are unchanged. Document in the config docs that this installation must set it before upgrading, or its owner triggers stop.
- Replace the literal login in docs examples with `<owner>`.

## Tests (no network)
- With the key unset, an owner comment from any login starts no run and doctor reports it.
- With the key set, behaviour is unchanged.
- `init` writes the owner it's given.

## Budget
About 30 source lines plus tests and doc edits.

## Out of scope
Multiple owners, and the Discord owner.

## Deployment
This installation's config sets only `[owners] discord`, so it relies on today's default. The orchestrator adds an explicit `[owners] github` value (equal to today's default) to this installation's config before the release with this change deploys. Say so in the PR so the deploy doesn't change behaviour here.

Closes #472

findings.title: Doctor, init and the upgrade notes don't say Dependabot triggers stop too
findings.detail: With `[owners] github` unset, `mapGitHubEvent` returns 'GitHub owner is not configured' before any event-specific handling (src/integrations/github.ts:85), so Dependabot PR triggers stop as well as issue labels and `/limitless` comments. The reopen handling also needs the owner. Reproduced with the existing Dependabot fixture: a configured owner produces a run request, while `null` or an empty string produces that note. The doctor warning, init's warning and the upgrade notes in README.md, docs/GUIDE.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md mention only issue labels and comments, so an installation that relies on Dependabot runs would not know the upgrade turns them off. Name Dependabot runs in all of them, and extend the doctor test to assert the wording.

head: d94e6c8af2324b2326d911e0ac1a2963530d7914
prompt:
Discreet mode: no factory marks in branches, commits, PRs or comments (per repository)

Slice of #37 (M6, work-ready). At work nothing shared may advertise the factory until the owner says so.

## Change
A per-repository operator setting in `config.toml`: `[repos."<owner>/<name>"] discreet = true`, with an optional `branch_prefix` (default `change/`).
- **Branches:** `<branch_prefix><slug>` instead of `limitless/<run id>-<slug>`; collisions get a short suffix.
- **Commits:** round and merge commit subjects without the `limitless:` prefix or factory trailers; the run title as the subject.
- **PR titles, bodies and comments:** no "Generated by Limitless" footer, no run id or local run URL, no factory branding in review-round, conflict-round or CI-round comments; the content (summary, checks, review) stays.
- **Identification:** anything that recognises factory PRs, branches or commits by the `limitless/` prefix or by marks in PR text must use the factory's own records (store: run ↔ PR ↔ branch) for discreet repositories. Find every such place (polling, rounds, the land queue, cleanup, MCP, the UI) and route it through one helper.
- Unset: behaviour unchanged.

## Tests
- A discreet repository's delivery produces a branch, commits, PR title/body and round comments with no factory marks (assert on the strings), and polling, review rounds and landing still find the PR through the store.
- A non-discreet repository is unchanged.

## Budget
About 150 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: approval-gated landing (#37's other half), the daemon UI's own branding.

Closes #672

findings.title: Merge and rebase commits pushed to a discreet PR are authored as Limitless
findings.detail: `mergeGit` sets `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` and `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL` to `Limitless <limitless@localhost>` for every merge commit, and `rebaseOnto` (src/git/repos.ts) sets the same committer. These commits are pushed to the PR branch: delivery-time base merges (engine.ts `completeMerge` at the conflict-round, delivery and post-merge sites) and the land queue's base integration (src/land/queue.ts `completeMerge`). The PR's commit list therefore shows 'Limitless' as author and committer next to the operator's round commits, the most visible factory mark left. (Round commits use the operator's git identity.) Required: in a discreet repository, every commit the factory creates or rewrites and pushes uses the same identity as round commits, never `Limitless` or `limitless@localhost`. Non-discreet repositories keep today's identity. Test: in a discreet delivery that merges the base (and one that lands with base integration), `git log --format='%an %ae %cn %ce'` over the pushed range contains no factory identity.

findings.title: Strict `[repos.*]` key validation breaks #687's key and makes every new key a rollback hazard
findings.detail: `parseRepos` throws `Unknown repos key` for anything other than `discreet` and `branch_prefix`, so the daemon refuses to start. #687 (in review) adds `land_requires_approval` to the same `[repos."<owner>/<name>"]` table with its own parser. Whichever lands second conflicts, and with this parser a config that sets `land_requires_approval` stops the daemon. More generally, after any release adds a repository key, rolling back to this release refuses to start (AGENTS.md: 'Leave the previous release working'; 'If an older release would refuse to start with a new key set, say so in the docs'). Required: ignore unknown `[repos.*]` keys with a warning instead of refusing to start, keep strict type checks for the keys this release knows, and put the repository-settings parser in one place both features use (`repoSettings`). Test: an unknown key loads with a warning.

findings.title: Turning discreet mode on mid-run publishes commits and reports made before the switch
findings.detail: Commit messages and the stored report are produced when the work happens, but checked only by the mode at publish time. A run that committed while the repository wasn't discreet, then resumes after the operator enables discreet mode (with a daemon restart), skips the finished implementation, `commitAll` returns null for the clean worktree, and delivery pushes the existing `limitless:` subjects with `Run:` trailers (traced by Codex). The land queue likewise sends the stored `report.md` as the squash body (src/land/queue.ts `reportBody`, about line 900). A report rendered before the switch keeps the run id, local URL and branding and writes them into main's history (reproduced by Codex). Required: in a discreet repository, never publish factory-marked text that was produced earlier. Before pushing, check the unpublished commits' messages (and identities) and rewrite or fail closed with a clear reason. Render the PR body and the squash body from the current setting at publish time instead of reusing a stored report. Tests for both.

findings.title: PR recovery by head SHA can override the recorded PR URL
findings.detail: `matchesPullRequest` accepts a candidate whose URL equals the recorded `prUrl` or whose `headRefOid` equals the head SHA, and the lookup takes the first candidate that matches either. Two open PRs can share a branch and head while targeting different bases. Codex reproduced it: identity records #10, the lookup lists #11 first with the same head, and #11 is selected. A resumed delivery then edits #11's body and records its URL. Required: an exact match on the recorded `prUrl` always wins; fall back to the head SHA only when no URL is recorded, and refuse rather than guess when several PRs match the SHA. Test with two PRs sharing a head.

findings.title: Branch-name collision search has no overall bound
findings.detail: Each candidate suffix can cost a GitHub PR lookup, each with its own retry budget, while the repository lock is held. After a cache rebuild, historical PRs whose branches were deleted are found only by those lookups and are probed again on every later run with a similar title. Bound the probes (for example a few numbered suffixes, then a short random suffix checked once), and fail with a clear error rather than looping when lookups fail. Test the bound.

findings.title: A valid prefix can still produce an invalid branch name
findings.detail: `branch_prefix` is checked with `isBranchName(`${prefix}x`)`, but the slug is appended later. Codex reproduced it: `branch_prefix = "feature.l"` passes, and the title 'ock' gives `feature.lock`, which `isBranchName` and git both reject. Validate the complete candidate (prefix, slug and suffix) before using it, and fall back to a safe slug if needed. Test it.

findings.title: `[needs human]` title prefix in discreet repositories
findings.detail: Needs-human and verified-work draft PRs are titled `[needs human] <title>` regardless of the setting. For a discreet repository that prefix signals automation to colleagues reading the PR list. The PR is already a draft, which carries the same meaning. In discreet mode, keep the plain title (the land path's retitle and the notifier must accept both forms). Test it.

head: 602db75665f306941ccfc35d8becb53d17915a75
prompt:
Issue #682: CI failure signature and excerpt should come from the failing lines

## Problem
`ciSignature` in `src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts` picks the first log line matching `/timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i` anywhere in the line. In a Bun log that is usually a *passing* test whose name contains "failure" or "error". On #676 the signature line was `(pass) an answering endpoint rejection never falls back, and socket failure rechecks HTTP`, although the failing test was `(fail) real Bun bail blocks targeted land retry …`. The `emit` excerpt is the first 2,000 characters of the whole job log, which is the runner-provisioning header (runner version, image, region).

Both go to the CI-fix round: `startRoundTrigger` puts the trigger's `check`, `line` and `excerpt` in the fix round's request, and the round's PR comment quotes `line`. A fix round therefore gets a passing test's name and runner boilerplate instead of the failure. The signature also names the record in `ci_failures` for a PR, commit and check, so different failures on one commit get the same name.

## Requirements
- Choose the signature line from failure-shaped lines only, parsed by structure: the same line-start patterns `securityFailure` already uses (`(fail)`, `FAIL`/`FAILED`, `✗ ✕ × ● ❌`, `--- FAIL:`, `not ok`, `##[error]`, `error:`), plus the timeout diagnostics. Keep today's fallback when no line matches.
- Take the excerpt from the failure region: the lines around the chosen signature line, still bounded to 2,000 characters, redacted before truncation as now.
- One implementation for both call sites that build a signature from a log (the inspection path and rerun resolution).
- Records written by the previous release still resolve. A pending rerun recorded under an old signature must not be requested again or lost after the deploy; the rerun claim is also matched by job, so check that path with a test.
- Tests built from a short inline Bun log: a passing test whose name contains "failure" appears before a real `(fail)` line, and the signature and excerpt name the real failure. Also a GitHub Actions log with the runner header first.

## Out of scope
The security classification, the transient/timeout rules, which failures trigger reruns, and the test-title annotation problem (filed separately).

Budget: about 80 lines including tests.

Closes #682

findings.title: Redacting the whole job log twice adds over half a second of event-loop blocking per inspection
findings.detail: `ciSignature` now runs `redactCredentials(logLines(redactCredentials(log)).join('\n'))`, two passes over the entire job log, to protect a multiline credential at a window boundary. `redactCredentials` costs one split/join per registered value, and a daemon holds hundreds after a day of uptime (every agent-test session and worker claim registers one). Measured with this branch's `ciSignature` on a 5 MB log with 600 registered credentials: 635 ms per call, against 4 ms on main, all synchronous in the GitHub poller on the daemon's event loop, for every failing check each time it is inspected. The daemon already stalls for seconds under load (#690, #700), and this adds to it. Required: redact only what is published, the chosen line and the excerpt window, after widening the window by the longest registered credential variant minus one character on each side, so a credential crossing the window edge is still replaced before cutting. Then cut to the final bounds. Keep the security scan (`securityFailure`) as it is. Add a test: a credential (including one with a newline) that straddles the window edge is redacted in both the line and the excerpt, and the redaction work is limited to the window, not the whole log (for example, by asserting on the length of the text passed to `redactCredentials`).

findings.title: Window redaction drops the exact-field match for short credentials
findings.detail: `redactCredentials` replaces credentials shorter than eight characters only when the whole input equals the credential, to avoid redacting common short strings. Before this change the signature line was redacted on its own (`bounded(line)`), so a short registered value that formed the whole line was replaced. Required: after the window redaction, also apply `redactCredentials` to each published field on its own (the signature line, and each line of the excerpt), so exact-field matches keep working. Add this case as a test.

findings.title: A pending fix trigger recorded under the previous signature is duplicated after the deploy

head: 97b29b9ef0bf1cc732ad8a29bb6aa5513b89bd75
prompt:
Land queue: wait for another person's GitHub approval before merging (per repository)

Slice of #37 (M6, work-ready). Work repositories require another person's GitHub approval before merging, and the factory must never approve its own PRs.

## Change
A per-repository operator setting in `config.toml` (the operator's policy, never read from the repository): `[repos."<owner>/<name>"] land_requires_approval = true`.
- When set, a land entry waits in a new `waiting_approval` state until the PR's GitHub review state shows an approval from an account other than the one the factory acts as, given on the exact head commit being landed (the review's commit id equals the entry's approved SHA). Stale approvals on an earlier head don't count. Then the entry continues through today's checks, CI wait and `--match-head-commit` merge unchanged.
- Observation is by the existing conditional polling, so it works with webhooks off.
- The orchestrator's `limitless review --approve` still records the factory-side approval; it never submits a GitHub review.
- `limitless land list`, the Land page and the feed show `waiting_approval` with the reason.
- Unset: behaviour unchanged.

## Tests (fake `gh`, no network)
- With the setting, an entry waits until an approval from another login on the approved SHA arrives, then lands.
- An approval on an older head, or from the factory's own login, doesn't release it.
- Without the setting, behaviour is unchanged.

## Budget
About 100 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: discreet mode (#37's other half), requesting reviewers, CODEOWNERS.

Closes #671

findings.title: A merge retry reuses an approval that was revoked after the pre-merge check
findings.detail: The approval re-check runs once, outside `mergePullRequest`'s retry loop, whose guard checks only claim ownership. Reproduced by Codex: the approval passes, the merge call returns HTTP 502, the approval is dismissed, and the retry merges the unchanged SHA. Two merge attempts, one review observation, entry `landed`. `--match-head-commit` can't catch a review change on the same SHA. Required: re-check approval with fresh evidence immediately before every merge attempt, including retries. Test the 502-then-dismissed sequence.

findings.title: A truncated review list can hide an outstanding change request
findings.detail: `latestReviews(first: 20)` has no pagination or completeness check. With a qualifying approval on the first page and a push-access reviewer's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` beyond it, `hasOtherApproval` returns true (it returns false when given the complete list). Both approval checks use this query, so this reaches merge. Required: page through completely (`pageInfo`), or treat incomplete evidence as no approval. Test with more than 20 reviewers.

findings.title: A later neutral review hides an unresolved change request
findings.detail: `latestReviews` returns each reviewer's latest submitted review, including `COMMENTED`. A reviewer who requested changes and later left a plain comment, without approving or having the request dismissed, no longer counts as requesting changes, so another reviewer's approval releases the gate (reproduced by Codex with a query-shaped snapshot). Required: decide change requests from each reviewer's latest opinionated review (`latestOpinionatedReviews`, or reduce the full review history so a `COMMENTED` review never clears an earlier `CHANGES_REQUESTED`). Test it.

findings.title: Wall-clock timestamps don't establish that an observation came after the wait began
findings.detail: `observedAt` is the time the response was processed, compared with the wait's start (src/land/queue.ts about line 587). Reproduced by Codex: a response captured before the wait began, delivered after it, gets a newer timestamp and releases the entry. Moving the clock backward also let a saved snapshot release a new wait with no later observation at all. Required: order observations against the wait durably, for example with a monotonically increasing observation sequence recorded when the wait begins, and exclude requests that were already in flight when it began. Keep the claim-time fresh check as a second barrier. Tests for both cases.

findings.title: Partial GraphQL errors are recorded as successful observations
findings.detail: Every `NOT_FOUND` error is accepted without checking its path. A response with an approval, a null review and a review-path `NOT_FOUND` was saved as fresh and released the wait (reproduced by Codex; the direct path correctly rejected the same response). Required: accept `NOT_FOUND` only for an unresolved top-level PR node. Any error on the review evidence makes the observation incomplete, so it can't authorize a release. Test it.

head: 295aee8fc629bdde895fa0970c8e49bb05dbb088
prompt:
Issue #681: Test titles create a security error annotation on every CI run

## Problem
`test/ci-classifier.test.ts` runs `test.each(securityRecords)("a failing security record blocks reruns and the ledger: %s", …)`, so each raw record is printed in a test title. One record is `##[error]security tests failed`. The GitHub Actions runner parses a legacy `##[…]` command anywhere in a line, not only at its start. So every CI run of this repository, passing or failing, gets a real error annotation reading "security tests failed [50.25ms]". The job log shows it as `##[error]security tests failed [50.25ms]` (see https://github.com/MattFlower/limitless/actions/runs/39530195892).

`src/integrations/ci-classifier.ts` treats an `##[error]` line that mentions security as a security failure, correctly and fail-closed. As a result, every failing CI run of this repository since a9221aa (2026-10-06) has been classified unsafe: no rerun of transient failures, no `ci_failures` record and no CI-fix trigger. The factory raised 39 `ci.needs_fix` items in that time, but recorded 2 CI failures and 1 fix trigger.

## Requirements
- No test title or printed string in the suite contains a runner command: `##[` anywhere in a line, or `::error`, `::warning`, `::notice`, `::group` and the like at the start of a line. Give the `test.each` cases labels instead of the raw records. The records themselves stay as they are.
- Keep the classifier unchanged. A real `##[error]` line about security must still block reruns.
- Add a line to `test/AGENTS.md` next to the existing `sandbox_apply` warning in AGENTS.md: Actions parses `##[…]` anywhere in a line of the job log, so test titles and printed output must not contain runner commands.
- Test: a guard test that fails when a test title in `test/ci-classifier.test.ts` would contain `##[`. Optional if a simpler check covers it.

## Out of scope
Classifier logic, signature or excerpt selection (filed separately), other test files unless they print runner commands too (check with `grep -rn '##\[' test/`).

Budget: about 20 lines.

Closes #681

findings.title: Resolve the conflicts with main
findings.detail: The change itself is right (labels instead of raw records in titles, and the test/AGENTS.md line). The PR now conflicts with main after #704 changed `test/ci-classifier.test.ts`. When merging: #704's signature test spreads `...securityRecords` into an array (around line 681 on main), so with this PR's object form it must use `Object.values(securityRecords)`. Keep every new title free of runner commands (`##[` anywhere, or `::` at the start of a line), including any `test.each` titles #704 added. Change nothing else. The earlier post-merge gate failure was load-related timeouts in unrelated pipeline tests, not this change.

head: 40485515a5d8705cc48438f86280736a200ae235
prompt:
Discreet mode: no factory marks in branches, commits, PRs or comments (per repository)

Slice of #37 (M6, work-ready). At work nothing shared may advertise the factory until the owner says so.

## Change
A per-repository operator setting in `config.toml`: `[repos."<owner>/<name>"] discreet = true`, with an optional `branch_prefix` (default `change/`).
- **Branches:** `<branch_prefix><slug>` instead of `limitless/<run id>-<slug>`; collisions get a short suffix.
- **Commits:** round and merge commit subjects without the `limitless:` prefix or factory trailers; the run title as the subject.
- **PR titles, bodies and comments:** no "Generated by Limitless" footer, no run id or local run URL, no factory branding in review-round, conflict-round or CI-round comments; the content (summary, checks, review) stays.
- **Identification:** anything that recognises factory PRs, branches or commits by the `limitless/` prefix or by marks in PR text must use the factory's own records (store: run ↔ PR ↔ branch) for discreet repositories. Find every such place (polling, rounds, the land queue, cleanup, MCP, the UI) and route it through one helper.
- Unset: behaviour unchanged.

## Tests
- A discreet repository's delivery produces a branch, commits, PR title/body and round comments with no factory marks (assert on the strings), and polling, review rounds and landing still find the PR through the store.
- A non-discreet repository is unchanged.

## Budget
About 150 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: approval-gated landing (#37's other half), the daemon UI's own branding.

Closes #672

findings.title: Enabling discreet mode mid-run publishes the stored legacy branch name
findings.detail: The stored branch is reused, and the publication checks never inspect it for factory marks. Reproduced by Codex: pause a run after prepare, enable discreet mode, resume, and the run creates a PR from `limitless/<run-id>-add-farewell`, which exposes both the factory name and the run id. Required: in a discreet repository, a branch that hasn't been published yet and whose name carries factory marks gets a neutral name from the discreet allocator before its first push, or the delivery refuses with a clear reason. A branch that is already published keeps its name (moving it would orphan the PR). Test the pause, enable, resume sequence.

findings.title: Attribution trailers in commit messages pass the discreet inspection
findings.detail: The unpublished-commit check recognizes selected message templates and author/committer fields, but not trailers. Reproduced by Codex: a fake implementer commits an otherwise neutral change with `Co-authored-by: Limitless <limitless@localhost>`, and discreet delivery pushes that trailer. Agent harnesses add their own attribution lines too (for example `Co-Authored-By: Claude …` or a 'Generated with …' line). Required: in a discreet repository, no published commit message carries a trailer or line attributing the change to the factory or to an agent harness. Parse the trailers with `git interpret-trailers --parse` rather than matching substrings, and either rewrite those commits before pushing (the factory owns the branch) or refuse with a clear reason. Test both a factory trailer and an agent trailer.

findings.title: PR recovery treats a truncated `gh pr list` as complete
findings.detail: Recovery uses `gh pr list` without pagination or a completeness check (its default limit is 30). Reproduced by Codex with 31 PRs: recovery selected one SHA match while another was outside the window, and a recorded URL outside the window led to a `gh pr create` attempt. Required: look up a recorded PR URL directly (`gh pr view <url>`), and when matching by head SHA, establish uniqueness across complete results (paginate, or query by head branch and SHA) or refuse. Test with more PRs than one page.

findings.title: Combined review pages can keep an approval that was dismissed between page reads
findings.detail: Pages of review evidence are combined after comparing only the head, PR state and draft status. Reproduced by Codex with fake transports: page one holds the only qualifying approval, it is dismissed before page two arrives, the head is unchanged, and the combined evidence keeps the approval and is marked complete. One merge call, entry `landed`, with no current qualifying approval. Required: fail closed. If the evidence needs more than one page, either treat it as incomplete (keep waiting and report why), or prove the pages are consistent, for example by re-reading the first page after the last one and requiring an identical review set. findings.title: The final approval read can be overtaken by a newer observed change request

head: 0cb6431dda3e50572b0c1133c5cc5745a137e5b5
prompt:
Issue #709: Admin sampling profile to find the daemon's event-loop stall sources

## Problem
#690's stall reporter (shipped in #700) shows the daemon's event loop still stalling in production: 51 stalls over 2.5 hours after a restart, median 4.9 s, longest 30 s. In every report the instrumented activities (`credentials.redact`, `credentials.data`, `gates.redact`, `store.event`) add up to under 10 ms, so the time goes to code the reporter doesn't cover.

A 4-minute native stack sample that caught four stalls (about 21 s in total) found the daemon's main thread running JIT-compiled JavaScript for about 36 s. It was not blocked in I/O (`sqlite3_step` accounts for about 0.6 s). The release Bun binary is stripped, so a native sample can't name the JavaScript functions, and the next step of #690 (find and fix the top stall sources, with before and after numbers) needs those names.

`profile(callback, sampleIntervalMicroseconds)` from `bun:jsc` samples all JavaScript on the main thread while the callback's promise is pending, including timer, I/O and HTTP callbacks unrelated to the callback itself. Checked: with `profile(() => Bun.sleep(3000), 1000)` and a 300 ms busy `setInterval` callback, the callback got 1395 of 1397 samples, by name. It returns `{ functions, bytecodes, stackTraces }` as text.

## Requirements
- Add `POST /api/admin/profile` to `src/server/http.ts`, next to `/api/admin/drain` and `/api/admin/resume`, with the same loopback-only and authentication rules as the other admin routes. The body is `{ "seconds": number }`, from 0.2 to 120 with a default of 30. The route runs `profile(() => Bun.sleep(seconds * 1000), 1000)` and responds with JSON `{ seconds, functions, stackTraces }`. Each text field is passed through `redactCredentials` and capped at 64 KiB.
- Only one profile can run at a time. A second request while one is running gets HTTP 409 with a clear message. A failure inside the profiler responds with an error and leaves no profile marked as running.
- A test that starts a busy, uniquely named timer callback, calls the route with `seconds: 0.3`, and finds that name in `functions`. A second test asserts the 409 for a concurrent request. Keep both well under a second.
- Document the route in `docs/OPERATIONS.md` under Troubleshooting: what the "Event loop stall" log lines mean, how to call the route with the API token, and that a profile adds a little sampling overhead while it runs.

## Out of scope
Fixing the stall sources (a follow-up, once a production profile names them), changes to the stall reporter, the CLI, and the daemon's launchd job settings.

Budget: about 40 lines plus tests and the doc paragraph.

Part of #690.

Closes #709

findings.title: Capping the raw stackTraces JSON keeps an arbitrary prefix and drops the source mapping
findings.detail: The issue text was wrong here, sorry: `profile()` returns `stackTraces` as an object `{ interval, traces, sources }`, not text. Measured: 3 s of profiling gives 386 KB of JSON, `traces` comes first and `sources` (the sourceID to URL map) last, so the 64 KiB cap returns a cut-off prefix of individual samples and never the sources. `functions` names anonymous functions only as `anonymous#hash:sourceID`, so the file can't be found. Each trace is `{ timestamp, frames: [{ sourceID, name, sourceURL, line, column, category, flags }] }`, innermost frame first. Required: replace the raw value with an aggregated text field (keep the name `stackTraces`): render each trace's first 8 frames as `name (sourceURL:line)` joined with ` < `, count identical stacks, sort by count descending, and emit one `<count>  <stack>` line per distinct stack, then redact and cap at 64 KiB as now, so the most frequent stacks always survive the cap. Use `<anonymous>` for an empty name. Update the tests: a busy, uniquely named timer callback appears in the first line of `stackTraces` with its file and line, and the mocked-profiler test feeds an object with `traces` and checks ordering by count. Update the OPERATIONS paragraph to describe the field. Run only test/profile-http.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`.

prompt:
Discreet mode: no factory marks in branches, commits, PRs or comments (per repository)

Slice of #37 (M6, work-ready). At work nothing shared may advertise the factory until the owner says so.

## Change
A per-repository operator setting in `config.toml`: `[repos."<owner>/<name>"] discreet = true`, with an optional `branch_prefix` (default `change/`).
- **Branches:** `<branch_prefix><slug>` instead of `limitless/<run id>-<slug>`; collisions get a short suffix.
- **Commits:** round and merge commit subjects without the `limitless:` prefix or factory trailers; the run title as the subject.
- **PR titles, bodies and comments:** no "Generated by Limitless" footer, no run id or local run URL, no factory branding in review-round, conflict-round or CI-round comments; the content (summary, checks, review) stays.
- **Identification:** anything that recognises factory PRs, branches or commits by the `limitless/` prefix or by marks in PR text must use the factory's own records (store: run ↔ PR ↔ branch) for discreet repositories. Find every such place (polling, rounds, the land queue, cleanup, MCP, the UI) and route it through one helper.
- Unset: behaviour unchanged.

## Tests
- A discreet repository's delivery produces a branch, commits, PR title/body and round comments with no factory marks (assert on the strings), and polling, review rounds and landing still find the PR through the store.
- A non-discreet repository is unchanged.

## Budget
About 150 source lines plus tests. Out of scope: approval-gated landing (#37's other half), the daemon UI's own branding.

Closes #672

findings.title: Attribution detection depends on the repository's trailer configuration
findings.detail: Thank you for round 2: the branch-name refusal and the complete PR recovery are verified fixed. Required: classification must not depend on the repository's configuration. Pin the trailer options you rely on when calling `git interpret-trailers` (for example `-c trailer.separators=:` and no `trailer.*` keys from the repository), and in the whole-message scan accept a key followed by any of `:`, `=` or `#` with optional surrounding spaces. Test with `trailer.separators` set to `=` and to `#` in the run's repository.

findings.title: Model names outside the list pass the attribution check, while human names are blocked
findings.detail: Reproduced from the patterns at markers.ts:80-83: `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1` (no email) passes because only Opus, Sonnet and Haiku are listed, while `Co-authored-by: Someone <claude@example.org>` and `Co-authored-by: Claude <human@example.org>` are treated as agents and end the delivery in needs_human. findings.title: PR bodies and comments still publish factory and harness branding from model-written text

Agent harnesses append exactly these lines to PR descriptions by habit.
